papers.title: Capability-Guided Iterative Online Optimization of Cascaded Spoken-Dialogue Modules
papers.abstract: Cascaded spoken dialogue systems comprise perception-and-comprehension, decision-making, and response-generation modules. We study iterative optimization of the first and last modules. Their reciprocal speech-content interfaces enable one-sided data to provide cross-module supervision: acoustic observations, such as waveforms or feature sequences, can be pseudo-labeled to train generation, whereas content-only samples can be rendered into speech to train comprehension. Because the reliable teacher-student direction varies across domains, we propose a two-stage, capability-guided pipeline for iterative online optimization. Stage 1 compares both modules through a shared intelligibility probe and obtains a domain-wise capability prior. Stage 2 activates the compatible one-sided-data route, constructs and filters supervision with the current teacher, updates the selected student, and refreshes the relevant checkpoints across cycles. We instantiate comprehension with Whisper large-v3 and generation with CosyVoice2. After only 200 steps for Whisper and 600 for CosyVoice2 of our iterative online optimization, we observe that, on the Chinese MAGICDATA-RAMC dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 14.18% to 10.77%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 4.78% to 4.04%. On the Japanese Common Voice dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 15.23% to 15.10%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 14.85% to 11.18%. These results demonstrate the feasibility of capability-guided iterative optimization of complementary spoken-dialogue modules.

papers.title: Flash evaporation Riemann Problem: Thermodynamic Relaxation and Oscillation-Free Real Fluid Finite Volume Method
papers.abstract: The Flash evaporation Riemann problem (FeRP) formulated the wave structures of flash evaporation in the vapor-liquid homogeneous equilibrium limit. However, physical flash evaporation involves finite-rate interphase heat and mass transfer, inducing the wave structure to deviate from the equilibrium state. To solve such a non-equilibrium Riemann problem, this paper first derives the governing equation of mechanical equilibrium evolution in a relaxation system, based on which an oscillation-free Homogeneous Relaxation Real Fluid (HRRF) finite volume method is developed. In addition to the Euler equations with mass relaxation, the HRRF method evolves advection equations for the internal energy--pressure affine parameters and the vapor volume fraction, in order to eliminate numerical pressure oscillations inherent in conservative methods while preserving phase-transition-induced pressure changes, and consistently degenerate into a completely pressure-equilibrium method in supercritical flows. The HRRF method is then employed to comprehensively evaluate how thermodynamic relaxation affects the FeRP solution. Results indicate that the non-classical expansion shock of the FeRP loses its traveling-wave characteristics with increasing relaxation time, continuously degenerating into a self-similar rarefaction wave. Compared with the equilibrium limit, an increased mass transfer relaxation time smooths the expansion branch of the RP solution, lowers the intermediate pressure and velocity, and induces a pseudo-splitting of the rarefaction wave as well as a pseudo-advance of the phase transition onset. Meanwhile, the heat transfer relaxation time primarily dictates the temperature difference in the vapor-liquid mixture, thereby modulating the liquid superheat and in turn influencing the mass transfer rate.

papers.title: Causal discernment and the direction of clinical research
papers.abstract: A clinical trial can establish an intervention's effects while leaving their causal pathways unresolved. We call causal discernment the practice of identifying explanations that fit the evidence but imply different decisions or research directions, and seeking studies that distinguish them. METHOD: We combine causal graphs and prose around four questions: delivery of the intended target change, routes of benefit and harm, stability of causal relations across regimes, and whether unresolved pathways could change the decision. With quantitative assumptions, graphs support plausible reasoning by showing which findings could distinguish explanations even when effects are not identified. Prose specifies clinical meaning, effect size and timing, and supporting evidence. We use conceptual analysis, hypothetical calculations, CAST and lipid-lowering therapy. SUBSTANTIVE RESULTS: Concordant coronary associations for HMGCR and PCSK9 perturbations support LDL mediation over target-specific explanations predicting unequal effects per unit of LDL reduction, but leave a shared receptor pathway possible. Diabetes associations leave LDL lowering, receptor-mediated uptake and weight gain as possible explanations. An illustrative causal record specifies a genetic comparison and assumptions under which it could distinguish them. CONCLUSION: The causal record formalises the reasoning behind the choice of the next study by making competing explanations, evidence and assumptions explicit and stating what each design could resolve. Prepared before a design or recommendation is adopted, it enables scrutiny of that reasoning and interpretation of results in relation to the stated explanations. Its added value over ordinary rationale review remains to be assessed.

papers.title: sdos: spectral densities of large sparse Hermitian and generalized eigenproblems
papers.abstract: sdos is an open Python package that computes the density of states (DOS) and related spectral quantities of very large sparse Hermitian matrices A, and of generalized problems A psi = lambda B psi, from Chebyshev moments estimated with random vectors. The density is reconstructed by the kernel polynomial method (KPM, the default) or by maximum entropy (Maxent); the same interface gives band energies, Fermi levels, local and projected densities, harmonic thermodynamics, exact HOMO-LUMO gaps and eigenpairs in a spectral window. Interfaces cover electronic (empirical tight-binding, DFTB, SIESTA) and vibrational (matrix-free LAMMPS Hessians) problems. I checked most ingredients against dense diagonalization or an independent code; the exceptions are listed in Sec. V. On a workstation (4 threads, 19 GB) the DOS of an 884,736-atom amorphous silicon model (a 6^3 tiling of a 4096-atom cell; 3.5 million orbitals; the orthogonal empirical tight-binding model of Kwon et al.) takes 71 s (M=100, R=2, no exact moments; 383 s with the default exact moments), and a matrix-free 2,097,152-atom crystal 10 min in 1.8 GB. A 17^3 replica of a 216-atom amorphous cell (1,061,208 atoms) agrees with exact Bloch spectra: electronic DOS in 229 s, matrix-free ACE vibrational DOS in 2.2 h on one GPU. Shift-invert, incomplete-Cholesky setup, exact moments of high order and Maxent at high moment counts do not scale. The underlying methods are due to Silver, Roder, Kress, Voter, Drabold, Sankey and collaborators; the Introduction states what is added.

papers.title: Sharp bounds for posterior causal attribution given complete factual records
papers.abstract: Retrospective causal attribution evaluates whether altering an earlier event would have prevented an observed outcome. Observational data determine marginal potential-response probabilities at fixed inputs while leaving cross-world joint distributions unspecified. Conditional on a complete factual record in a finite Markovian structural causal model, independence across mechanisms is preserved and each unobserved conditional response distribution is restricted to a capped probability simplex. Every collection of conditional distributions satisfying these local bounds is jointly attainable within a single compatible structural causal model. Optimizing the counterfactual expectation over the resulting product domain yields sharp attribution bounds for multistage interventions and mediated effects, and compatible response-vector polytopes extend these bounds to structural response restrictions. Exact algorithms for causal chains and general directed acyclic graphs, consistent plug-in endpoint estimators, and finite-sample and asymptotic confidence intervals are developed and illustrated using synthetic reactor experiments and health survey data.

papers.title: A Rule That's Made to be Broken? Reframing the Arrhenius Law for Ionic Transport
papers.abstract: The Arrhenius law is ubiquitous in the physical sciences. It describes how an observable property scales with temperature, $T$, as $\exp(\pm E_A/k_BT)$ for a constant $E_A$, the 'activation energy'. Fitting to the Arrhenius law is a common procedure for both experimental and computational data. However, the physical significance of any 'activation energy' calculated is unclear. Here we focus on self-diffusion coefficients for potential solid electrolytes, and by identifying the individual 'diffusive steps' within the system, show how a physically significant activation energy can be extracted. There are also many examples of non-Arrhenius behaviour including `super-Arrhenius' curvature, where the effective activation energy appears to increase with decreasing temperature. We demonstrate how it is still possible to extract the underlying Arrhenius law, by quantifying self-correlations such as back-and-forth motion. The methodology described here is material-agnostic and can be utilised to analyse the molecular dynamics trajectories of both ordered and disordered materials.

papers.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero Kähler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

papers.title: Rapid, High-Precision Numerical Evaluation of Multiloop Feynman Diagrams
papers.abstract: We numerically evaluate multiloop Feynman diagrams by using Sinc function approximations to transform the integrals into rapidly convergent, multidimensional sums. We compare the efficiency of this approach to Monte Carlo evaluations of electron g-2 terms. We show that the two strategies reach parity at precisions of around 1% for the full sets of three and four loop diagrams. Beyond this level Sinc function methods are dramatically faster - computing 3-loop integrals to six digit precision takes minutes whereas Monte Carlo timings map to years. We show that the method can evaluate individual 5-loop g-2 integrals and discuss extrapolation techniques that would further improve performance. We note that the method appears to be applicable to more general diagrams.

papers.title: Fingerprints of feedback cycles in stationary diffusions
papers.abstract: When does the stationary density of a $d$-dimensional diffusion process driven by standard Brownian motion uniquely determine its drift? In general, it does not: the $d$ drift components enter the stationary Fokker-Planck equation only through a single scalar divergence. We consider drifts whose component functions only depend on a subset of their input variables, and encode this dependence with a directed graph. We exclude 2-cycles, which admit rotations that leave the stationary density invariant, but otherwise allow arbitrary graphs, including those with feedback cycles. We show that if the stationary density is sufficiently $s$-concave, e.g., strictly log-concave, then the drift is uniquely determined among graph-structured drifts in a weighted Sobolev space. For drifts with linear self-regulation, a single locally strictly convex level set of the stationary density is sufficient to identify the drift in the region it encloses. Both results follow from Raychaudhuri equations. Excluding 2-cycles allows treating nontrivial rotational and symmetric terms simultaneously, extending the scope of the corresponding Bochner- and Reilly-type arguments. We illustrate the results by recovering the Hill-type regulation of a stochastic genetic repressilator from samples of its stationary distribution.

papers.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
papers.abstract: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from $22.5^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, all stationary, with $Re \approx 1.0 \times 10^4$. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance. In the wake, high-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, concentrating fluctuation energy in a dominant low-rank mode. Deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are therefore decoupled: the quasi-circular $(1 \times 19)$ cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, while the deep-grooved $(3 \times 7)$ cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force. These results support construction-dependent cable selection and aerodynamic load modeling.

papers.title: Tail behaviour of infimum of Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: We investigate the upper tail of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$, where $X$ is a centred Gaussian process (GP) with continuous sample paths on a nonempty compact metric space $\mathcal T$. As suggested by the findings of [1], the exponential rate is governed by an optimal-measure problem, while the exact prefactor depends on the local geometry of the corresponding contact set. In the full-contact regime, we strengthen the known Gumbel max-domain of attraction property of the distribution of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$ by establishing the von Mises condition. For fractional Brownian motion on $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, with Hurst index $H\in(0,1/2)$, we also determine the order of the logarithmic correction to the leading Gaussian exponential. For finite contact sets, we distinguish dominated, smooth-critical, and rough-critical regimes and derive exact asymptotics of $P\{\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)>u\}$ as $u\to\infty$ under suitable local assumptions. We illustrate our findings with examples including fractional Brownian motion and the fractional Brownian sheet.

papers.title: Energy-Harvesting-Aware Cell-Free LEO Satellite Networks: A Lyapunov Framework for Sustainable User-Centric Beamforming and Clustering
papers.abstract: We study battery-aware downlink control in user-centric cell-free low Earth orbit satellite networks with intermittent solar harvesting and finite onboard batteries. A perturbed Lyapunov controller coordinates clustering and hybrid beamforming using measured battery states and causal harvest forecasts. The per-slot solver combines group-sparse association, rate bounds, a quadratic transform, and successive convex approximation. We establish robust battery invariance for feasible implemented actions and give a utility bound conditional on a comparison policy and the per-slot implementation gap. Multi-orbit control-layer simulations show that queue-aware scheduling preserves a larger battery reserve in the stressed scenario at the expense of effective energy efficiency. A separate fixed-cluster matrix snapshot illustrates recovered hybrid beam patterns and the per-slot objective trace.

papers.title: Strain Controlled Hydrogen Interstitial Site Preference and Hydride Phase Suppression in Epitaxial Vanadium
papers.abstract: Understanding hydrogen behavior in transition metals is crucial for energy storage and sensing technologies. Here we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with in-situ electrical measurements to reveal how epitaxial strain governs hydrogen interstitial site selection and phase stability in vanadium. Our calculations demonstrate a robust thermodynamic preference for tetrahedral (T) over octahedral (O) sites, with the energy difference modulated by lattice anisotropy through strain-tunable H 1s-V 3d orbital hybridization. Experimentally, epitaxial V films on MgO(001) exhibit a critical thickness-dependent crossover: 50 nm films show characteristic first-order alpha-beta hydride transitions, while 10 nm films display continuous solid-solution behavior with complete transition suppression. This crossover is governed by the progressive relaxation of epitaxial strain with increasing film thickness: the 10 nm films retain strong coherent strain that flattens the free-energy landscape and suppresses hydride nucleation, whereas the 50 nm films approach the strain-relaxed bulk limit where long-range elastic interactions restore first-order phase behavior. Finite-size truncation of elastic fields and interfacial electronic reconstruction further reinforce this dimensional crossover. Our work establishes a unified framework connecting atomic-scale orbital physics to mesoscopic phase thermodynamics, providing design principles for strain-engineered metal-hydride systems.

papers.title: WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation
papers.abstract: Wireless foundation models learn transferable channel state information (CSI) representations across heterogeneous wireless systems. However, conventional grid-aligned representations couple feature sequence length to CSI dimensions, restricting the allocation of representation capacity to different propagation conditions and task requirements while increasing inference overhead. This paper proposes WiFo-R, a wireless foundation model that learns progressive channel representations with selectable capacity. A channel-query cross-attention encoder aggregates spatial, temporal, and spectral CSI information, while parameter-shared recurrent updates refine existing channel features and introduce additional latent tokens. Multi-mask, multi-depth self-supervised pretraining equips intermediate states with strong reconstruction capabilities, followed by task-aligned post-training for channel estimation and CSI feedback. WiFo-R supports temporal and frequency-domain channel prediction, channel estimation, and variable-rate CSI feedback, and transfers to localization and LoS/NLoS classification. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution channel configurations demonstrate accurate reconstruction, progressive performance improvements, and strong transferability. A single feedback encoder--decoder supports six payload lengths at fixed quantization precision, while cross-attention and selectable recurrent depth improve the accuracy--complexity trade-off for large-scale CSI observations.

papers.title: Zero Replacement and Latent Profiles in Short Media Diaries: Checking Recording Status Before User Segmentation
papers.abstract: Short media diaries contain many zeros because many activities go unrecorded during the observation period. Log-ratio analysis of time allocation requires these zeros to be replaced with small positive values; as a result, all respondents who did not record an activity receive nearly the same value. We examined how such zero replacement affects classification in latent profile analysis and propose checks to perform before profiles are interpreted. Three-day diaries of 8,089 adults from the 2025 Korea Media Panel Survey were converted into nine-part time-use compositions. Gaming was not recorded by 88.9% of the respondents, and in every model with two to eight profiles and a covariance matrix held equal across profiles, respondents who recorded gaming and those who did not were classified into different profiles. Even when the replacement value equaled the minimum recording unit (5 min/day), the two-profile classification largely matched gaming recording status, and the two groups separated more sharply as the replacement value decreased, until the separation was complete. Before naming profiles, researchers should therefore check the proportion of respondents who did not record each activity and its replacement value, the same proportion within each profile, and the distribution of usage time among those who recorded the activity.

papers.title: Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data
papers.abstract: Clinical speech is increasingly used for disease screening and clinical assessment, but directly distributing speech recordings poses privacy risks because they contain both speaker-identifying voiceprints and sensitive spoken content. Existing speech anonymisation approaches are primarily developed for general speech applications or task-specific clinical speech and overlook that different clinical tasks rely on distinct speech characteristics, necessitating task-adaptive anonymisation strategies to protect patient privacy while preserving clinical utility. Here we introduce CASA, a clinically adaptive speech anonymisation agent that transforms anonymisation from a fixed processing procedure into a task-guided optimisation process, dynamically tailoring voiceprint and content anonymisation to task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements. Through recursive self-improvement (RSI), CASA iteratively evaluates and refines anonymisation strategies against task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements, while learning from these outcomes to guide more efficient planning in subsequent clinical tasks. CASA is validated across 14 clinical tasks encompassing five languages, diverse elicitation paradigms, and mental health, cognitive and voice disorders. CASA preserved disease-related classification performance while meeting speaker-anonymisation requirements across all clinical tasks, versus only 8/14 for the strongest fixed method. Assessments of resistance to speaker re-identification by external attackers and identification and redaction of sensitive personal information in clinical speech further demonstrated CASA's dual protection of speaker identity and sensitive spoken content. Clinical expert assessments further supported the preservation of clinically relevant information and the acceptability of anonymised speech for controlled research sharing.

papers.title: Parametrizations of the solutions of Love equations and their momenta
papers.abstract: The Love equation is a paradigmatic example of a Fredholm integral equation of great interest in mathematics and physics, where its applications range from electrostatic problems to exactly solvable models for one-dimensional systems. In this work we propose a method to approximate the normalized solutions of Love equations of the first and second kind via a parametrization obtained by Hermite interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. Following the same approach, we also obtain approximations for the second, fourth and sixth momenta of the solution of the Love equations. We focus in particular on one-dimensional quantum gases described by the Lieb-Liniger and the Gaudin-Yang models. For these models, the solutions of Love equations correspond to the normalized densities of pseudorapidities. We show that remarkably accurate results can be obtained using the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation with a number of points as low as 17+2. In the case of the Lieb-Liniger model, we also propose a very accurate closed-form estimate of the dimensionless ground state energy valid for all values of the dimensionless interaction parameter incorporating known results for small and large couplings supplemented by the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation for intermediate couplings. As an application of this result, we compute the dimensionless local two-particle correlation function and the black soliton solutions of the Lieb-Liniger model.

papers.title: Theory of spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy with topological insulator tips
papers.abstract: Topological insulators have enabled a new class of spin-sensitive scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) probes based on helical boundary states. However, how these probes generate a net spin-polarized tunneling current remains unclear. We present a theory of spin-polarized STM with topological insulator tips and show that asymmetric tunneling-contact geometry and spin dephasing enable helical boundary states to generate a spin-polarized tunneling current. Within the standard Landauer-Büttiker formalism, we demonstrate this mechanism for a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator tip: asymmetric contacts make the two counter-propagating helical edge states, which carry opposite spins, traverse path lengths that differ by $\Delta L$, and spin dephasing induces backscattering that reduces the conductance more strongly for the longer path. For a representative asymmetric contact and weak spin dephasing, the QSH tip exhibits a tunneling spin polarization of $P_s=-17.2\%$ under positive bias, whose magnitude can reach $50\%$ for larger $\Delta L$, and which remains robust against Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Crucially, this polarization, dominated by helical edge transport rather than by bulk states, naturally reverses sign with the bias polarity owing to spin-momentum locking. Our findings are consistent with recent STM experiments using topological tips.

papers.title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
papers.abstract: As ferroelectric devices approach the nanometer scale, their behavior becomes increasingly sensitive to boundary conditions. In perovskite oxide nanocapacitors, epitaxial strain and electrostatic screening are well-established control parameters. Then, while expected to contribute to the epitaxial stabilization of ferroelectric ultrathin films, the lattice-dynamical state of the electrodes has not been isolated as an independent tuning knob. Here we call this poorly explored coupling interfacial phonon bias, whereby the electrodes' phonon energy landscape reshapes that of the adjacent ferroelectric across their shared interface. Using first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular-dynamics simulations, we examine this mechanism in symmetric BiFeO${}_3$ nanocapacitors in contact with a metallic perovskite oxide. By independently controlling the orientatio and amplitude of the electrodes' octahedral-tilt landscape, while keeping conventional elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed, we show that the electrodes' phonon energy landscape can modify the stability of competing BiFeO${}_3$ phases. In particular, this allows us to shift the ferroelectric transition temperature and even induce antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions. We thus showcase interfacial phonon bias as a complementary and powerful strategy to modify and optimize the properties of ultrathin epitaxial films.

papers.title: Chaos Growth in a Generic 2D Hamiltonian System
papers.abstract: We examine the geometric mechanism controlling the transition from local to global chaos in a generic 2D Hamiltonian system, the generalized Hénon-Heiles system. Using Poincaré sections and invariant manifolds, we show that the chaotic fraction grows through abrupt transitions associated with the destruction of invariant barriers. We introduce an index that gives the time required for the first penetration of a local chaotic domain into the global chaos. This index increases sharply and tends to infinity as a critical energy is approached. The set of lobes generates heteroclinic connections, while multiple unstable periodic orbits exhibit a global manifold structure characterised by repeated loops and lobes. However, in special chaotic cases close to the integrable Hénon-Heiles potential, where two asymptotic curves extend to infinity, the manifold topology differs qualitatively from the generic case, as the asymptotic curves no longer form closed structures surrounding the periodic orbits.

papers.title: Probing the Supersymmetric Grand Unified Theories with Anomaly Mediation at the Future Proton-Proton Colliders and Hyper-Kamiokande Experiment
papers.abstract: With the grand desert hypothesis, we investigate the Supersymmetric (SUSY) Grand Unified Theories (GUTs) with the minimal anomaly mediated supersymmetry breaking (AMSB) as a continuation of our program of studying SUSY GUTs at the future 100 TeV proton-proton Collider such as $\rm FCC_{hh}$ and SppC as well as proton-decay experiment such as Hyper-Kamiokande experiment. We show that for the GUT scale $M_{GUT} \ge 0.84 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, the upper mass bounds on the gluino and first two generation squarks are 8 TeV and 6 TeV, respectively. Therefore, the gluino and first two generation squarks can be probed at the $\rm FCC_{hh}$ and SppC. In addition, we discuss the mass spectra for the colored sparticles, sleptons, pseudo-scalar Higgs and electroweakinos. We also shed light on the possible search strategies of gluino and winos at the future 100 TeV colliders. Moreover, for $\rm M_{\rm GUT} \le 0.84 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, the proton lifetime for dimension-six proton decay via heavy gauge boson exchange is less than or around $5 \times 10^{34}$ years, and thus we can probe it at the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment. To be concrete, we present a couple of benchmark points representing the above two mentioned GUT conditions on $\rm M_{\rm GUT}$.

papers.title: Effect of Correlation on the Pressure-Induced Insulator to Metal Transition in Complex Spin-Orbit Coupled Double Perovskite La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$
papers.abstract: We study the effect of electron correlation ($U$) and hydrostatic pressure on the electronic properties of double perovskites La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$ for $x$ = 0, 0.5, and 1, using first-principles electronic structure calculations within density functional theory (DFT). At ambient pressure, we systematically vary the electron correlation, i.e., on-site Coulomb interaction to study its effect on band gap and structural parameters. Increasing the value of $U$ enhances the band gap of all three compositions while producing only a slight variation in structural parameters. The effect of hydrostatic pressure is also studied for the same compositions. The estimated band gap values at ambient pressure closes at approximately 39, 42, and 53 GPa for $x$ = 0 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), 0.5 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), and 1 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 4 eV), respectively, indicating pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transitions. These results show that electron correlation stabilises the insulating state, whereas hydrostatic pressure favours the metallic state by closing the band gap. These findings highlight the tunability of correlated oxides through electron correlations and pressure, offering insights for materials design.

papers.title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
papers.abstract: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids. Moreover, the resulting strain field has been used to describe how elasto-plastic models respond to external strains. It is thus important to examine carefully the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids, especially when anomalous elasticity is at play. Here we solve the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids with both even and odd dipole screening and a complete analytical result is obtained for the displacement and strain fields. The analytical results are crucial for understanding the anomalous responses in displacement fields measured directly from experiments and numerical simulations. The computation of strain fields clearly demonstrates the deviations from their classical counterparts for perfectly elastic solids. The decomposition of the displacement field shows the excitation of higher-order Fourier modes. The presence of higher excitations other than the imposed Eshelby geometry therefore suggests the possible nonlinear mode coupling that can influence and modify the anomalous responses.

papers.title: FESOM2.8 in single precision: climate fidelity over six decades and performance on CPUs and GPUs
papers.abstract: Halving the floating-point precision of an ocean model can make it substantially faster, but whether the rounding errors stay negligible over climate time scales has rarely been tested. We implement single precision in the global ocean-sea-ice model FESOM2 and compare 60-year hindcasts with double-precision controls. A first implementation lost salt steadily, accumulated a heat-content deficit of 129 ZJ, and shifted major ocean fronts. Controlled experiments trace the drift to the tracer update: small increments added to a large salinity value are rounded away, and the increments themselves are biased. Accumulating tracer tendencies and layer thicknesses in 64 bits, and carrying the rounding error of each tracer update into the next, removes the drift for at most 8% additional runtime. Single- and double-precision simulations then differ in heat content and mean state about as much as two double-precision runs with slightly perturbed initial conditions, sea ice differs by at most 0.2%, and he salinity difference is four orders of magnitude smaller than before. In the coupled model AWI-ESM3, single precision adds no detectable heat source or sink over 60 years. Single precision speeds up the 60-year hindcasts by a factor of 1.35, and the model by up to 1.66 on meshes of up to 5 km resolution; on GPUs, a C++/Kokkos version runs up to 1.27 times faster and needs 43% less memory. Whether reduced precision is safe for climate integrations is decided by long-term budgets, not by short tests.

papers.title: Direct Light-Cone Reconstruction of the $B$-Meson Shape Function in HQET
papers.abstract: The $B$-meson shape function encodes the nonperturbative residual-momentum dynamics of the heavy quark within heavy quark effective theory (HQET). From a Wilsonian perspective, HQET provides a natural framework for lattice calculations when the heavy quark mass is comparable to or exceeds the inverse lattice spacing. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a $B$-meson quasi-shape function directly in HQET and calculate its one-loop matching to the light-cone shape function, avoiding an intermediate matching step involving a full-QCD light-cone distribution. We determine the one-loop renormalization kernels and matching coefficients in both the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ and regularization-independent momentum-subtraction (RI/MOM) schemes for the quasi-shape function, while keeping the light-cone shape function in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme. The matching coefficients are obtained at leading power in the large-$v^z$ expansion and are independent of the infrared regulator. Our results provide the perturbative ingredients for a direct lattice HQET determination of the $B$-meson shape function.

papers.title: Hardware-Efficient Continuous-Variable Quantum Computation: Finite-$N$ Non-Gaussian Gates in a Floquet-Engineered Cavity-BEC
papers.abstract: Continuous-variable (CV) quantum computation in bosonic modes offers a hardware-efficient route toward fault tolerance, yet synthesizing deterministic, macroscopic non-Gaussian gates with Wigner negativity remains challenging. Here, we establish two physical breakthroughs and two tensor-network innovations using a single-cavity 87Rb Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) as a macroscopic bosonic logical mode. Physically, building on our orthogonal optical dual-driving architecture, we propose deterministic, unitary Floquet-engineered Two-Axis Twisting (TAT) non-Gaussian gates without post-selection, and introduce a paradigm shift from quantum metrology to CV quantum computation: via a normal-ordered Holstein-Primakoff expansion and non-perturbative spin simulations, we show that the over-squeezed regime ($t>t_{opt}$, where Wineland squeezing $\xi_R^2$ degrades) harnesses finite-$N$ Bloch-sphere curvature - manifesting at $O(1/S)$ as cubic shearing and quartic Kerr $(a^\dagger a)^2$ interactions - to deterministically generate Wigner negativity. Methodologically, we formulate an exact automaton Matrix Product Operator in the compact SU(2) spin basis with an $N$-independent Liouvillian bond dimension ($D_L=6$), bypassing Fock cutoff errors ($N_{max}$) and $O(N^3)$ permutational-invariant scaling. Finally, we decouple $4^N$-dimensional Lindblad evolution from collective observation via an Exact Bilateral Dynamic Programming Dicke Projector with log-gamma normalization, extracting the $(N+1)\times(N+1)$ symmetric projection $\tilde{\rho}_{n_L,n_R}$ without moment truncation while tracking symmetry retention $p_{sym}(t)$. Our proof-of-principle $N=50$ benchmark resolves deep Wigner negativity ($W_{min} \approx -0.214$ at $t=2.00\mu$s, after $\xi_R^2 \approx 0.124$ at $t_{opt} \approx 0.64\mu$s), establishing a scalable architecture for $N \sim 10^3-10^5$ macroscopic BEC processors.

papers.title: An $SU(5)$ GUT with non-holomorphic modular $S'_4$ symmetry: fermion masses, mixing and leptogenesis
papers.abstract: A non-supersymmetric $SU(5)$ grand unified model is constructed based on the non-holomorphic modular $S'_4$ flavor symmetry, supplemented by a global Peccei--Quinn $U(1)_{PQ}$ symmetry that constrains the Yukawa couplings. Constructed from polyharmonic Maaß forms, these couplings allow the model to reproduce the observed charged-fermion masses and mixing as well as the neutrino oscillation parameters for both normal ordering (NO) and inverted ordering (IO), with all Pull values satisfying $|\mathcal{P}| < 0.8$. The model further yields specific predictions for yet-unmeasured parameters, including the absolute neutrino masses, the Dirac CP phase, the Majorana phases, and the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$. We then study thermal leptogenesis by solving the density matrix equations. For a given benchmark point, the final baryon asymmetry depends solely on the single free parameter $b$ that sets the right-handed neutrino mass scale, and an appropriate choice of this parameter reproduces the observed value $\eta_B \simeq 6.12 \times 10^{-10}$. Finally, the correlation between this scale parameter and specific low-energy observables provides a potential bridge between the fermion flavor structure and early-Universe cosmology.

papers.title: Stretched near-groups
Precision Fragmentation Functions from Modern COMPASS SIDIS Data
authors: Maryam Soleymaninia (On behalf of HAPS Collaboration)
papers.abstract: We present a comparative account of three global determinations of collinear fragmentation functions (FFs) for charged pions, charged kaons, and unidentified charged hadrons. The HAPS-PiFF1.0, HAPS-KaFF1.0, and HAPS-hFF1.0 analyses combine single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation with charge-separated semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS), including the 2025 COMPASS proton-target measurements and the revised 2026 isoscalar-target results. Flexible neural-network parametrizations, Monte Carlo replicas, and NLO/NNLO perturbative setups are employed. The proton and isoscalar samples sharpen the flavor sensitivity of SIDIS, while gluon fragmentation remains comparatively weakly constrained. We discuss the effects of perturbative accuracy, the principal limitations, and prospects for future measurements.

papers.title: Algorithms for Soft Tree Containment on Tree-Child Networks
papers.abstract: Phylogenetic networks generalize evolutionary trees by allowing lineages to merge. The Tree Containment problem asks whether a network $N$ displays a tree $T$ on the same taxa. When the polytomies of $T$ reflect uncertainty rather than simultaneous divergence, the relevant notion is soft display, in which $N$ may refine the polytomies of $T$. We take it in its asymmetric reading. Soft Tree Containment is NP-hard on reticulation-visible networks even at reticulation indegree three, and it was open for a non-binary tree and a tree-child network with multifurcating tree nodes or reticulations of indegree above two. We solve this case. A cluster characterization reduces soft display to realizing all clusters of $T$ by one switching, and in a tree-child network the vertices that can realize a cluster lie on a single chain. The per-cluster requirements then form a constraint network of width one, which arc consistency decides without search, and a $2$-SAT instance when $N$ is binary. This yields, to our knowledge, the first polynomial-time algorithm for soft Tree Containment on single-labelled tree-child networks of arbitrary reticulation indegree, and a linear-time algorithm when $T$ is binary. The same method decides the symmetric variant of the problem, in which the polytomies of $N$ may be resolved as well.

papers.title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
Joint Poisson Reconstruction for Prompt-Gamma-Enabled 68Ga/18F Dual-Isotope Quantitative PET Imaging
papers.abstract: Objective:To enable simultaneous quantitative 68Ga/18F PET imaging despite low prompt-gamma triple-coincidence counts and random-triple contamination. Methods: We developed an expectation-maximization reconstruction method (PNR-EM) that jointly estimates pure-emitter, non-pure-emitter, and random-triple components using a Poisson model of prompt double, prompt triple, and delayed triple measurements. A consistent-delay strategy estimates random triples while preserving true-pair temporal correlations. Prompt doubles additionally constrain the non-pure component, and total variation regularization suppresses reconstruction noise. The method was evaluated with quantitative and Derenzo phantoms, a nine-well separation phantom, and tumor-bearing mice. Results: Phantom quantitation showed strong linearity (r2>0.99) and a maximum relative deviation below 9.9% relative to single-isotope references. The separated images largely preserved rod resolvability relative to their corresponding single-isotope references. The best PSNR, SSIM, and RMSE were 33.72 dB, 0.975, and 0.0206 for 18F, and 34.86 dB, 0.955, and 0.0181 for 68Ga in the 9-well phantom. The 68Ga RMSE was 41.4% lower than that of the best image-domain separation baseline. Tumor-bearing mouse imaging demonstrated in vivo separation of 68Ga-DOTA-NOC and 18F-FDG distributions. Conclusion: Joint estimation improved dual-isotope separation under the evaluated low-count conditions. Significance: To our knowledge, this study provides the first experimental demonstration of simultaneous 68Ga/18F PET separation using prompt-gamma coincidences, supporting simultaneous imaging of complementary metabolic and receptor-targeted tracer distributions.

papers.title: Nonlinear Interference Estimation in Coherent Optical Systems: Principles and Applications
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of nonlinear interference (NLI) is important for monitoring and optimizing coherent optical networks. This invited paper reviews the main techniques proposed for receiver-side NLI estimation, with particular focus on longitudinal power monitoring (LPM). We discuss the principles, advantages and limitations of LPM-based NLI estimation, including recent experimental demonstrations. We then experimentally investigate the impact of the spatial step size and the number of averaged constellation blocks on estimation accuracy. The results show that accurate NLI estimation does not necessarily require a highly accurate power profile, with limited improvements obtained by increasing the number of averaged blocks. Finally, we discuss the main practical limitations and applications of NLI estimation, with particular attention to end-to-end and span-wise optical power optimization.

papers.title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
GFM Control Automatic Compliance Toolbox
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation reduces system inertia, short-circuit strength, and voltage support. European grid codes, including the ENTSO-E Network Code on Requirements for Generators and the ACER Demand Connection Code, now define disturbance-based validation procedures for grid-forming (GFM) generation and converter-based demand. Commercial RMS tools, however, lack an integrated workflow aligned with these recent requirements. This paper presents an automated Python-PowerFactory compliance toolbox and an RMS test bench for a co-located system comprising a 1 MW GFM photovoltaic (PV) plant, a 0.3 MW GFM battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 1 MW converter-interfaced dynamic load at a 20 kV point of common coupling fed from a 110 kV grid. Extended virtual synchronous machine models and a DCC-oriented load model are tested in batch, with results automatically extracted and plotted for assessment. Results show compliant RMS performance for the slower, electromechanical tests, while the paper identifies which tests require complementary electromagnetic transient (EMT) verification.

papers.title: Regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes in the EAST tokamak
papers.abstract: The pedestal pressure profile plays a critical role in determining the overall confinement of tokamak fusion plasmas. This letter reports the first evidence on regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes (MTMs) via limiting the pedestal gradient, which was thought to be limited by kinetic ballooning modes over the last decades. This is observed in an ITER-baseline-like target plasma in the EAST tokamak. MTMs arrest the recovery of pedestal electron temperature (and hence pressure) by clamping its gradient at a critical value while leaving the density profile essentially unaffected. Global fluid and local gyrokinetic simulations confirm the excitation of MTMs when the pedestal electron temperature gradient exceeds a threshold value in this experiment. This finding reveals MTMs as an alternative electromagnetic micro-instability that imposes an additional constraint in determining the pedestal structure in tokamaks.

papers.title: Electron cooling mediated by transverse optical phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$
papers.abstract: Soft transverse optical (TO) phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$ couple to electrons through the polarization field, quadratically in the paraelectric phase and, additionally, linearly in the polar phase due to the onset of spontaneous polarization. We investigate heat flow between a three-dimensional electron gas and soft TO phonons. For two-TO-phonon scattering, the heat flow of hot electrons crosses over from $T^5$ to $T^3$ at the Bloch-Gruneisen temperature. In the polar phase, an additional one-TO-phonon channel emerges, yielding a softer temperature dependence of the heat flow, $T^3$ at low and $T$ at high temperatures, with the spectral weight set by the spontaneous polarization. This channel may dominate at low temperatures and leads to a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the heat flow in the vicinity of the polar transition.

papers.title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
Grid-forming Control of Offshore Wind through a Diode-Rectifier HVDC System: a 2 GW Case Study
papers.abstract: Diode-rectifier-unit (DRU)-based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission considerably reduces the volume and weight of the offshore converter platform for remote wind farms and, hence, its cost, but shifts the task of forming and regulating the offshore AC network to the wind-turbine converters. This paper examines which grid-forming control strategy is the most suitable for DRU power transfer. The DRU commutation relationship shows that the delivered active power depends on the offshore voltage magnitude (but not on the converter voltage angle), so the angle-based active-power loop of virtual synchronous machine control is not closed through the rectifier. A $P-V/Q-{\omega}$ grid-forming architecture, which regulates active power via the voltage magnitude and derives frequency from the reactive power error, is therefore adopted. Electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1GWaggregated grid-forming turbine on a 66 kV collector network with a $\pm$525 kV bipolar DRU link show that the commanded power is delivered over 800 to 1000MW with the offshore voltage held near nominal. The paper also examines how grid-forming operation changes the allocation of control duties within the Type-4 turbine: once the grid-side converter forms the network, DC link regulation must move to the machine-side converter, which limits the achievable bandwidth of the DC-link control. Extending the system to 2 GW with two 500 MW grid-following units achieves full power transfer in simulation, but with the grid-forming converter loaded beyond its continuous rating and a steady-state offshore frequency deviation of approximately 1.8 Hz.

papers.title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
papers.abstract: Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports gene-function discovery and regulatory analysis. Existing studies often focus only on highly variable genes, restricting the expression changes available for downstream analysis. Cells exposed to the same intervention can also show heterogeneous expression responses, with coordinated gene programs active to different degrees. We propose scBIG++, a full-gene perturbation prediction framework that models this heterogeneity by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation. To preserve shared gene structure while accommodating cellular variation, Gene-Relation Clustering organizes genes into common windows, within which Dynamic SoftSub learns expression-dependent submodule memberships. This shared organization enables Set-GCAE to exchange information about corresponding gene groups across control cells, placing individual representations in their source-population context. The cell representations initialize a latent flow, while their pooled summary and the perturbation representation condition response generation. Generated states are decoded into expression profiles covering all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing, supporting comprehensive analysis of perturbation-induced expression changes. Experiments across six genetic and chemical settings spanning 6,539--19,451 genes demonstrate competitive perturbation-effect recovery and full-gene expression reconstruction under unseen targets and combinations, cross-cell-line transfer, and held-out compounds. Our implementation is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Spot Markets for AI Inference: Dynamic Capacity Allocation and Pricing on a Shared Accelerator Fleet
papers.abstract: Inference providers size their accelerator fleets for the interactive peak and sell spare capacity through fixed discounts, such as batch tiers at half price. However, inference differs from conventional cloud capacity in four respects: capacity depends on the latency tier through batching, moving weights between models is slow and costly, spot demand can wait until its deadline, and power can bind. In this paper, we develop a framework for dynamic capacity allocation and pricing of AI inference on a shared accelerator fleet. We consider a provider that serves several models under a power cap and sells each model in an interactive tier with a speed promise and in a spot tier for preemptible work with a deadline. In each period, the provider chooses how many replicas of each model to keep loaded and what spot price to quote. We show that one interactive token displaces a fixed number $\rho_m>1$ of spot tokens, and that the optimal spot price lies midway between the interactive price and the effective cost of capacity in the deadline window, which is close to the prevailing half price only when the fleet is slack. We further show that a spot tier raises the optimal reliability of the interactive tier, and that placement should follow persistent demand shifts while prices absorb transients. Building on these results, we design a model predictive controller based on a linear program with explicit approximation bounds, which solves each period in milliseconds. Numerical experiments on a simulated week with a measured daily demand profile, a flash crowd, and a grid curtailment show that the controller raises profit by 7.4% over fixed half-price practice, captures 93% of the gain available with perfect forecasts, keeps the interactive promise through both events, and leaves spot buyers better off.

papers.title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2\Omega_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

papers.title: On the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem for $k$-trees
Synergizing CKM and ISAC for Environment-Aware Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) have emerged as two key technologies for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks, enabling a new paradigm toward environment-aware system design. CKMs provide static or stochastic wireless environment information a priori by learning location-dependent mappings from transceiver positions to channel knowledge of various types, whereas ISAC exploits wireless signals to sense environmental objects in real time. CKM and ISAC have primarily been studied separately in prior works, while their integration offers a promising approach for enhancing the environment awareness of 6G networks and further improving both sensing and communication capabilities. On the one hand, sensing can support CKM construction by providing location-tagged measurements and richer environmental observations, while also enabling real-time CKM refinement in dynamic environments. On the other hand, CKM can enhance sensing by offering prior environmental information for clutter mitigation, and CKM and sensing information can be jointly leveraged to improve communications. This article provides an overview of the complementary interactions between CKMs and ISAC, with particular emphasis on three design approaches: sensing-assisted CKM construction and refinement, CKM-assisted sensing, and joint CKM- and sensing-enhanced communications. We also discuss future research directions for achieving environment-aware wireless networks.

papers.title: Independence number and odd dominating models
Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
Holographic dissociation of tetraquark and hybrid meson in the spinning plasma
papers.abstract: We explore the dissociation of the tetraquark \(Z_c\) and the hybrid meson \(\pi_1\) in a spinning quark-gluon plasma described by the planar limit of a spinning Myers-Perry black hole. Both states are treated within one holographic framework, using a non-quadratic dilaton profile whose parameters are fixed by the \(Z_c\) and \(\pi_1\) mass spectra. Spectral functions are computed in the longitudinal and transverse channels. The boost parameter and temperature both lower the peak height and broaden the width, and the effect is stronger in the transverse channel. In both channels, the heavier 2S states melt before the 1S states. Furthermore, the two exotic channels display distinct dissociation behaviors within the same effective framework. This provides a unified holographic approach to compare how different exotic states behavior, without requiring a dynamical calculation of their binding energies.

papers.title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schrödinger system
Optimal Dividends and Voluntary Liquidation under Omega-Type Regulatory Termination
A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
Monotonicity of Wang's recursive sequence and logarithmically complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the inverse tangent
Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
Token graphs of stars
On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
Exactly integrable field theory in $(2+1)$-dimensional space-time: the spectral equations
A Multistage Extension of Witsenhausen's Counterexample with Linear Signaling
papers.abstract: We study a multistage scalar extension of Witsenhausen's counterexample in which controller 1 observes the initial state exactly, whereas every subsequent controller observes only a local noise-corrupted state and does not inherit its predecessors' observations, so that every nonterminal action both regulates the state and shapes the signal available to the next controller. Restricting the signaling controllers to linear policies while leaving the terminal controller unrestricted, we compute the exact value within this class and reduce the optimization to a deterministic dynamic program in a single propagated variance. The optimal intermediate gains are shown to have a shrinkage form, and the value functions of that program are concave. For two stages, the benchmark admits a closed form on a matching locus, where for small effort weights it has two distinct minimizers, and at the standard parameter instance on that locus a two-point nonlinear policy strictly improves upon it. For three stages, numerical continuation at a reference instance reveals three distinct local minima, and two values of the initial variance at which the lowest of the three changes abruptly. Under the terminal-cost normalization we further prove, for every finite horizon, that the optimal linear value becomes asymptotically equal to the signaling-idle benchmark as the initial variance tends to infinity.

papers.title: Coherent Conversion of an Interacting Dark-State-Polariton Condensate into a Photonic Bose-Einstein Condensate
papers.abstract: An interacting condensate can retain an observable imprint of its preparation after the interactions are switched off. For light, accessing this regime requires separating the formation of a photon condensate from the material medium that redistributes its energy. We investigate a multimode-cavity scheme in which an interacting dark-state-polariton condensate is coherently converted into a confined photonic Bose-Einstein condensate as the atom-cavity coupling is removed. The polariton mass, matter fraction, and particle number control the condensate occupation during preparation. Remarkably, changing the mass also modifies the condensate's response to repulsion through the spatial overlap of its orbitals, even when the entire single-particle spectrum is held fixed. Ideal mode-preserving conversion conserves the full natural-orbital occupation spectrum, while finite-time few-body calculations show that additional occupation changes during transfer are much smaller than those established during interacting preparation. Once decoupled from matter, the photons evolve under the free cavity Hamiltonian while retaining correlations acquired in the interacting gas. Interference between cavity modes produces oscillations in the photon density, while resonant pair correlations persist after interaction removal and distinguish the resulting photon state from a quadratic thermal state with the same one-body density matrix.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Quantitative Ultrasound (DeepQUS) for Multiparametric Hepatic Steatosis Assessment
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) has shown promise for liver fat quantification in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Incorporating multiple parameters has demonstrated the potential to outperform single QUS parameter measures. Here, we propose a deep learning-based multiparametric QUS framework that learns effective integration of multiple features from QUS measures to estimate pixel-wise hepatic fat fraction, enabling the detecting of heterogeneous fat accumulation within the liver. We developed a U-Net based network architecture to predict local fat fraction percentages, which takes 2D QUS maps as input and is trained with magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as the ground truth. We extracted 2D QUS maps (H-scan frequency, at-tenuation, Nakagami, and RF/envelope/log-compressed data) and tested various input configura-tions consisting of different combinations of the QUS parameters. We enrolled 30 patients with healthy livers or suspected/confirmed MASLD, and acquired ultrasound RF data, and validated our approach using the patient data. Among all tested input configurations, the model combining H-scan, attenuation, and Nak-agami parameters achieved the best performance, with a Spearman correlation coefficient (Rs) of 0.92 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98. The predicted fat fraction maps exhibited color changes concordant with the gradual increasing in MRI-PDFF, from normal liver to 45% fat ac-cumulation. These findings demonstrate that deep learning can integrate multiparametric QUS in-formation in a fully data-driven manner, providing a localized fat fraction map rather than a single whole-liver value. We anticipate that our deep learning framework can offer potential advantages for future assessment of heterogeneous disease development in liver for more complex, progres-sive liver diseases such as steatohepatitis.

papers.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
Quantum entanglement as a resource for self-organization and stabilization
papers.abstract: Can quantum entanglement generate macroscopic order that persists after the entanglement itself disappears? We establish such a mechanism in a driven-dissipative bosonic lattice, where local entanglement enables transport that amplifies spatial fluctuations into extended Turing patterns. For the full nonlinear dynamics with noise and disorder, we derive rigorous finite-time bounds on pattern intensity for all admissible separable evolutions, allowing arbitrary classical correlations. Quantum dynamics produces pattern intensities beyond these bounds during both formation and stabilization under noise. The excess intensity also provides a lower bound on the accumulated transport contribution beyond the separable limit. We further introduce an environment that responds to emerging order by suppressing local coherence and activating classical transport. The patterns then persist as local entanglement is lost, with both stages arising from a single time-independent Lindblad equation. These results show how transient quantum resources can establish persistent macroscopic order, opening new directions for harnessing self-organization in nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Ampère equations with Hölder continuous right-hand sides
Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
Numerical Stability Issues and a Mitigation Method in Switching Events Calculation Considering State Variable Discontinuities for EMT Simulation
papers.abstract: Some existing methods for switching events calculation considering state variable discontinuities for EMT simulation can encounter numerical stability issues, either over-stabilizing or destabilizing the studied power systems. This paper documents these issues in detail with a concrete example. The underlying mechanism of the issues are revealed via systematic analysis. A mitigation method for the issues is proposed. The convergence behavior of the method is analyzed. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. It is observed that the method also helps to improve the accuracy of the simulation results.

papers.title: Learning the NMPC with Stability Guarantees
papers.abstract: Although nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) is widely used, its online optimization is computationally expensive. Neural network approximations of NMPC can effectively reduce the online computational burden but generally lack stability guarantees. This paper proposes an approximate NMPC framework with guarantees of constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability. The approximation error is addressed through constraint tightening, and the resulting tightened NMPC is used to generate the training dataset of the approximate NMPC. The maximum allowable approximation error is prescribed a priori for the design of tightened NMPC and satisfied in a probabilistic sense through an iterative trial-and-error procedure alternating between network training and a posteriori verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a numerical example of a constrained nonlinear system.

papers.title: Analysis increments for model bias diagnosis and correction: Theoretical foundations
papers.abstract: A common method for diagnosing and correcting model bias in weather and climate prediction is based on analysis increments: the difference between the analysis and the forecast at each data assimilation cycle. Their time average is used to estimate and correct the bias, and machine learning is increasingly used to map the forecast state to the increments, giving a state-dependent correction. Despite its widespread use, the method lacks theoretical foundations. We first analyse a Kalman filter whose forecast model has a constant bias. We show what the averaged increment measures, and prove that iterating the correction removes all of the bias seen through the observations; for linear dynamics, no method can identify the rest. We then extend the analysis to state-dependent biases. For linear dynamics, each increment records the model error over the filter's memory, as seen through the observations. We use this to determine what the increments measure when averaged over a long period, averaged over periods with similar slowly varying conditions, and used without averaging, as in machine-learned corrections. Numerical experiments confirm the theory for a linear model and suggest that its main conclusions carry over to the nonlinear Lorenz '96 model, including for a correction learned by a neural network.

papers.title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
Design and Performance Evaluation of a Quad-panel Dual-isotope PET Imaging System
papers.abstract: In simultaneous dual-isotope PET, prompt-gamma-based separation is challenged by the low statistics of triple coincidences and the limited flexibility of coincidence logic for multi-energy event extraction. We designed and evaluated a compact quad-panel dual-isotope PET system without dedicated prompt gamma detectors. The system comprised four orthogonally arranged detector panels, each providing an effective area of 107.0 * 145.5 mm. GPU-accelerated software coincidence processing extracted double- and prompt-gamma-tagged triple coincidences from raw single-photon data. Triple-coincidence images were reconstructed with correlated-random-triple correction using the consistent delayed expectation-maximization method, followed by image-domain isotope separation using a spatially varying scaling factor. System performance was evaluated using phantom and in vivo studies, with emphasis on 68Ga/18F imaging because of the low prompt gamma yield. The system achieved energy resolutions of 15.7%, 12.9% and 10.2% at 511, 1077, and 1275 keV, and a timing resolution of 1.35 ns. In the 68Ga Derenzo, 1.6-mm rods were resolved in double-coincidence images, with 1.2-mm rods partially distinguishable, while 1.6-mm rods remained discernible in triple-coincidence images. The mean prompt gamma detection efficiencies along the three axes ranged from 8.19% to 9.31%. The system sensitivity was 1.12% for doubles with an energy window of 350-650 keV, and 0.068% for triples after random correction with a dual-energy window. The scatter fraction was 27.81%, and the NECR reached 83 kcps at 9.38 MBq for doubles and 106 cps at 21.42 MBq for triples. Phantom and in vivo studies demonstrated successful separation of 18F/68Ga and 18F/124I tracer distributions. By maintaining high-resolution and quantitative imaging performance, the system provides a preclinical platform for multitracer PET studies.

papers.title: Foreshortening of Polarizer Angles in Wide Field Polarizing Imagers
papers.abstract: The Polarimeter to Unify Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) is a very wide field polarizing imager covering a 90 degree diameter region of the sky, stitched together from four individual fields of view (FOVs), three of which are supported by Wide Field Imagers (WFIs) with 40 degree diameter individual FOVs. The science objective requires precise measurement of linear polarization. The WFI FOV is sufficiently wide that polarizer angles are foreshortened by projection effects relative to the line of sight of each pixel in the instrument, deviating from their nominal angular positions of -60, 0, and +60 degree relative to the instrument frame of reference. These angles are foreshortened by the very wide WFI field of view, changing their effective angle across the image plane - an effect that is analogous to similar challenges of polarimetric right/left channel separation in large-format 3D cinema, such as the IMAX format. Using a simple geometrical approach we estimated the perceived polarizer angle in the WFI FOV will vary by +/-2.5 degree for +/-60 degree and +/-3.5 degree for 0 degree polarizer angles. We present the effect of this deviation on the polarized brightness to be recorded by WFI, along with how optical distortion will shift the location of foreshortened angles. We also discuss the implications of this effect on upcoming technologies based on polarimetry across in wide fields.

papers.title: An Arbitrary-Order Distributional Finite Element Method for the Curl--Dev Grad Stokes System
Adaptive Quantum Metrology of Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: We develop a feedback-controlled quantum metrology scheme to probe weak gravitational waves (GWs) through their direct energy exchange with light. Adaptive SU(2) direction control, based on current estimates of the GW frequency and phase, allows the frequency shifts acquired in successive interaction intervals to add rather than cancel. The resulting persistent frequency difference is converted into an optical phase difference for interferometric readout. We further extend the scheme to elliptically polarized GWs using two transverse sensing channels separated by $45^\circ$ to probe the $+$ and $\times$ components independently. After the GW interaction, the two signals are mapped onto orthogonal polarization modes, enabling phase accumulation along a common path. We derive the corresponding quantum Fisher information matrix and find a $T_{\rm int}^2T_{\rm ph}^2$ scaling in the ideal coherent regime. For a fixed-photon-number probe, the sensitivity shows Heisenberg-like $1/n$ scaling in the ideal case.

papers.title: Data Center Power Flexibility Characterization: A DeepSets Reinforcement Learning Approach
Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
Combining rock typing and NMR logging to estimate permeability in complex carbonate formations
papers.abstract: Estimating intrinsic permeability from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logs is difficult in heterogeneous carbonates because a single calibration may not represent distinct pore systems. We evaluated whether flow-zone-indicator (FZI)-based rock typing improves empirical calibration of the modified Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) model in the Arbuckle Group, Kansas. The analysis used 470 depth-matched core-permeability and NMR measurements from the Wellington and Cutter wells. FZI calculated from measured permeability and NMR-derived porosity was grouped using K-means clustering. Six clusters were identified, but one singleton cluster was excluded, leaving five rock types for SDR calibration. Relative to the global model (without clustering), rock-type-specific calibration reduced testing root mean square log-transformed error (RMSLE) from 1.215 to 0.240-0.427 and increased coefficient of determination (CD) from -0.106 to 0.578-0.924. The fitted porosity exponents ranged from 0.053 to 0.521, indicating that porosity provided limited additional information in some rock types and that the SDR parameters should be treated as empirical calibration quantities. Because measured permeability was used to calculate the FZI before the within-cluster splits, these results represent conditional performance for samples with known FZI membership, not blind permeability prediction. Field implementation will require a permeability-independent method for assigning rock types.

papers.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
Odd Darcy Law: Odd Viscosity and Edge Currents in Porous Media
papers.abstract: We derive and numerically validate an odd Darcy law for chiral active fluids in porous media, in which an antisymmetric permeability tensor induces a flow transverse to the applied pressure gradient. We identify two distinct mechanisms leading to this odd response: odd viscosity in the fluid or the nonlinear coupling of edge currents to inertia. We then show how the transverse transport depends on porosity, boundary friction, and chirality.

papers.title: GlobalTap: Globally Diverse Beat Tracking Benchmark via Crowdsourced Tapping
papers.abstract: Existing beat-tracking benchmarks draw from a narrow range of musical cultures, predominantly Western, and are difficult to scale due to reliance on expert annotation. We address both limits with GlobalTap, a benchmark of 200 popular-music excerpts spanning 59 countries, annotated by 746 participants recruited across ten countries. The benchmark is created using a scalable online tapping pipeline that records taps via audio for high temporal precision, aggregates pooled tap times into consensus beat annotations, and computes intrinsic quality measures that flag perceptually difficult excerpts without requiring a reference. In a separate study on a different 240-excerpt validation set, tapped by an additional 733 participants, an independent group of 130 listeners rated how well the resulting beat tracks lined up with the music, and we detected no overall difference between our annotations and existing reference annotations. Crowd-derived annotations occasionally diverged from the references in phase and metrical interpretation, yet listeners did not consistently prefer the reference versions, suggesting that crowd-derived and existing reference annotations can reflect different perceptual or structural interpretations. The disagreements were often systematic rather than random, and metrical-level choices differed across the ten recruitment countries. We release GlobalTap together with open-source pipeline code as a listener-derived resource for evaluating beat-tracking systems on culturally diverse music.

papers.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
Virtual-Flow: Virtual Microphone-based Speech Enhancement via Semi-supervised Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Neural network-based virtual microphone estimation (neural-VME) synthesizes microphone signals at unobserved spatial locations from a limited set of real microphone (RM) physical recordings. This enables high-resolution arrays that improve spatial processing for downstream tasks such as speech enhancement. However, existing methods rely on supervised training with ground-truth signals captured at virtual locations, requiring datasets that scale with the number of virtual microphones (VM) and leaving open the question of how to design optimal large-array configurations. We propose Virtual-Flow, a flow-matching framework that implicitly generates VM signals conditioned on real recordings, without requiring ground-truth VM signals. We introduce a semi-supervised training strategy based on pseudo-VM targets constructed from time-delayed superpositions of real recordings. Virtual-Flow shows improved magnitude estimation in high-frequency bands, yielding richer spatial cues for beamforming.
