Experiments demonstrate that the proposed Virtual-Flow, combined with reflow distillation, outperforms existing neural-VME baselines in VM-based beamforming and achieves competitive end-to-end speech enhancement performance with low computational cost.

papers.title: On-the-Fly Reduced Bases Through the Lens of Augmented Krylov Methods
Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
Optimal Polynomial-Query Approximation for Consistent Submodular Maximization with Short Lookahead
Phase-Constrained Self-Supervised Reconstruction and Denoising for Ultra-High-Resolution MRI
papers.abstract: Ultra-high-field gradient-echo (GRE) MRI reveals fine anatomy with strong susceptibility contrast, but small voxels reduce signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), while susceptibility-induced phase variation and wrapping complicate reconstruction. These challenges are especially consequential for quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM), which requires denoising GRE phase without blurring anatomy or distorting phase. We propose a measurement-domain self-supervised learning (SSL) framework for joint reconstruction and denoising of complex-valued images from a single noisy acquisition. By splitting acquired k-space samples into input and held-out subsets, the method trains without clean or fully sampled references. An explicit phase-modulation operator, estimated from low-resolution phase and embedded in the unrolled network's encoding model, simplifies phase patterns encountered by the learned regularizer while preserving consistency with acquired complex k-space measurements. We evaluated ex vivo mouse brain MRI at 15, 18, and 72 um isotropic resolution; in vivo mouse brain MRI at 30 um isotropic resolution; and in vivo human brain MRI at 0.3x0.3x0.4mm3 resolution. Across controlled noise levels, SSL improved image-quality metrics in most conditions, preserved fine anatomy, and reduced error propagation into T2* maps and QSM. Ablation studies showed that phase regularization suppressed localized artifacts from rapid phase variation, while in vivo experiments demonstrated denoising with structural preservation. These findings support phase-constrained, measurement-domain SSL for high-resolution anatomical and quantitative MRI when clean references are unavailable.

papers.title: The Escobar Constant for Two-dimensional Disks
Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
papers.abstract: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

papers.title: When gene summaries reveal the answers: Gene Ontology circularity in gene embedding benchmarks
papers.abstract: A gene summary can contain the very annotations used to evaluate an embedding of its text. The Alliance of Genome Resources converts Gene Ontology (GO) annotations into sentences, which NCBI Gene displays and GenePT includes in its input. These summaries covered 6,172 of 19,256 human protein-coding genes (32.1%), including 58% of genes with one to ten linked publications. We embedded the same corpus with and without the generated summaries and refitted a function-prediction probe on each version. Among genes with one to ten publications, removal reduced the reported per-gene area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) by 0.078 with a linear probe (95% bootstrap interval 0.072-0.084) and by 0.033 with a multilayer perceptron. These estimates use a historical GO scorer that mishandled ties. The original predictions are unavailable for rescoring. A simple TF-IDF encoder also benefited from the summaries, as did models evaluated only on experimental annotations. Replacing generated summaries with UniProt function descriptions recovered much of the lost performance despite little verbatim overlap. UniProt also curates many of the evaluation labels. In mouse and yeast, we found a similar dependence on the source of the description. We introduce GeneProv to compare encoders on matched text and to examine how representation rankings change across GO recovery, non-GO endpoints and co-essentiality.

papers.title: The Effect of the U.S. Federal Production Tax Credit on Negative Energy Prices
papers.abstract: Negative prices frequently arise in electricity markets and production subsidies are commonly cited as a leading cause. Using data from the U.S. Eastern Interconnection wholesale electricity markets for the period 2000-2023, we document that at least 18 percent of the total hours with negative energy prices cannot solely be attributed to the federal production tax credit (PTC), a large, persistent production subsidy during the period of study. Next, we provide the first causal evidence that the PTC leads to negative energy prices. On average, increasing PTC-eligible wind generation by 1 percent increases the probability of a negative energy price by 3.4 percentage points. However, significant heterogeneity exists across electricity markets, and some markets show an effect that is an order of magnitude larger. Furthermore, the PTC explains only 10 percent of the observed negative prices that could potentially be attributable to it. Finally, we use the causal estimate to calculate a plausible value for the environmental benefits accrued from the PTC subsidy when energy prices are negative.

papers.title: Statopia: A Prover--Library Ecosystem for Automated Formalization and Proof Discovery in Statistics
papers.abstract: Theoretical results in statistics and machine learning rest on long, technically delicate proofs, and fluent arguments generated by large language models are not necessarily correct. Automated formalization makes such arguments mechanically checkable, and automated proving goes further by discovering machine-checked proofs for statements whose proofs are incomplete or missing altogether. Both require reconstructing assumptions from source materials, accessing specialized mathematical infrastructure and managing long proof developments. We present Statopia, an ecosystem that jointly develops Statopia Prover, an independent agent specialized for formalizing and proving results in statistics and machine learning, and Statlib, a Lean~4 library built with the prover and organized for automated use. The prover controls its own execution without relying on external coding agents. It is built for formal proof discovery and checking existing proofs. A natural-language proof, when available, guides its search but is not required: from a statement alone, the prover develops the argument itself and constructs a Lean proof. Its workflow integrates source preparation, statement review, library supported planning and proof construction. Dynamic proof dependency graphs and task groups support parallel, resumable proof development. Statlib's shared definitions and theorem interfaces are organized for retrieval and composition by agents, and its coverage of statistics keeps expanding. Verified results and usage feedback from the prover inform reviewed library updates, so that proof development drives this expansion. A cross-platform application provides an interactive workspace for uploading source files and running tasks locally or in the cloud.

papers.title: On Size-Biased Distributions and the Chainability of Positive Infinitely Divisible Distributions
Evaluating generative samplers for lattice field theory by scale
papers.abstract: Generative samplers for lattice field theory are commonly evaluated by their effective sample size (ESS). We show that a small global ESS need not imply inaccurate long-distance observables: errors spread over many short-distance modes can dominate this diagnostic. We introduce a scale-resolved diagnostic based on the overlap between coarse-grained model and target distributions. At the lattice cutoff, this overlap determines the asymptotic ESS fraction; lower cutoffs isolate long-wavelength errors. In the exactly solvable free theory, two samplers with comparable ESS yield a $32\%$ bias and no bias in the susceptibility, respectively. In two-dimensional $\phi^4$ theory near criticality, trained diffusion samplers show the same separation of scales: their path-weight ESS fraction falls rapidly over the volumes studied, while low moments of the magnetization remain close to their target values. Varying the reference parameters substantially changes infrared observables, with little effect on the log-weight variance. Given the target magnetization distribution, a marginal Metropolis test maintains an acceptance rate of order one in our tests. Combined with exact local updates, it reduces the remaining mismatch, although residual bias remains at finite relaxation length. In the free field, uniformly bounded relative errors in the proposal mode variances give a volume-independent bound on the number of updates needed for a prescribed accuracy of the chain's stationary mode variances at fixed correlation length. The target marginal must be supplied or computed separately; estimating it from the samplers' own weights can inherit the poor global overlap.

papers.title: Probing faint radio activity from cores to filaments in two $z=2.24$ protoclusters with uGMRT
papers.abstract: We present deep 1.26 GHz radio continuum observations of the two $z=2.24$ protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) to investigate their members' radio emission and its possible environmental dependence. Among 187 and 105 H$\alpha$ emitter (HAE) members in BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, we identify ten and two robust radio counterparts, respectively, together with five potential counterparts from forced photometry. Two HAEs and the massive quiescent galaxy QG1 in BOSS1244 show strong radio excesses relative to their H$\alpha$-based star formation rates (SFRs) and are identified as strong radio-excess AGN candidates. Median stacking of the remaining 173 and 102 radio-undetected HAE members yields positive signals at $2.8\sigma$ and $3.2\sigma$ in BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, respectively. The stacked radio luminosities are consistent with those expected from the median H$\alpha$-based SFRs, indicating that star formation can account for the average faint radio emission. After excluding the robust radio counterparts, we divided the HAE members by the projected distance from QG1 in BOSS1244 and from the filament spine in BOSS1542. The largest stacked radio luminosities are found toward the denser regions in both systems, but the differences are not statistically significant, and stellar mass shows no significant dependence on environmental distance. These results identify strong radio-excess AGN candidates among the individually detected members, while the faint HAE population is on average consistent with radio emission from star formation. The similar environmental ordering is suggestive but remains tentative. Deeper radio observations at multiple frequencies and higher angular resolution are required to determine whether this apparent trend reflects weak AGN activity or variations in radio emission associated with star formation.

papers.title: Local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations
An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization
papers.abstract: This work presents a 65 nm SoC for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation. The SoC performs low-noise in-ear EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A dedicated accelerator is developed, featuring a memory reuse technique to efficiently process long kernels required for low-frequency EEG feature extraction. A runtime dynamic quantization is incorporated, reducing model size by 3.88 times with only a 0.28% loss in accuracy. A sensitivity of 98.3% is achieved for deep sleep detection, enabling effective sleep modulation.

papers.title: Feasibility-Aware Learning for Network-Constrained Unit Commitment
papers.abstract: Learning-based approaches to network-constrained unit commitment (NCUC) usually still rely on an optimization solver to repair or complete their predictions, which limits the speedup they can deliver. This paper proposes FALCON-UC, a feasibility-aware graph learning framework that predicts commitment and dispatch jointly and produces final schedules without solving a mixed-integer program at inference time. It combines an LSTM--GraphSAGE predictor over a fully connected generator graph, a differentiable correction that embeds commitment-dependent dispatch bounds, power balance, and PTDF-based branch flows in training, and deterministic commitment, dispatch, and ramp-coupled reserve repairs at inference. On the 2383-bus system, FALCON-UC achieves $99.09\%$ commitment accuracy and a $0.4350\%$ mean absolute cost gap with all evaluated constraints within tolerance at $0.0562$ s per instance, a $2.27\times10^{3}$ speedup over the solver. MTLR R-SCUC-FL is slightly more accurate but still needs an optimization solver to complete each schedule, which takes $262.2$ s per instance, $4.67\times10^{3}$ times the FALCON-UC runtime. A label-only baseline without repair violates the balance and branch limits on every 2383-bus test instance, and FALCON-UC also meets all evaluated constraint tolerances on a 1354-bus system.

papers.title: Covariant Hamiltonian Gravity in Spherical Symmetry
papers.abstract: Building upon the covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, we construct the effective Einstein equation governing gravitational dynamics. For any prescribed one-parameter family of static, spherically symmetric metrics, this equation can be constructed such that the prescribed family constitutes their vacuum solutions. As an application, we construct generalized Vaidya solutions to the effective Einstein equation and show that the corresponding energy-momentum tensor takes precisely the standard Vaidya form. The results demonstrate that standard null dust sources can serve as matter source for dynamical black-hole geometries beyond general relativity, including regular black holes. Furthermore, this work suggests that quantum gravity corrections alone may not account for Hawking-like evaporation, as mass loss in the ingoing Vaidya solution necessarily requires a violation of the null energy condition within our effective framework.

papers.title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays
The Role of Small-Scale Flux Emergence in Pre-eruptive Magnetic Destabilization
papers.abstract: Recent high-resolution observations have reported the emergence of small-scale magnetic flux shortly before the onset of solar flares; however, their role in solar eruption processes remains unclear. In this study, we perform three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations to examine the effect of small-scale emerging flux on the eruption process. We construct a bipolar active region by extrapolating a potential magnetic field from a pair of sunspots and drive the system with sustained rotational motions to build up strong shear along the polarity inversion line. A small-scale emerging flux, amounting to approximately 0.6%-3.0% of the total magnetic flux and having a polarity opposite to that of the main sunspot, is then introduced at the center of the bipole. As a result, although no significant differences are found in the pre-existing magnetic field during the early phase with or without the emerging flux, the current sheet formed in the sheared field lines collapses more rapidly, and the reconnection-driven eruption is initiated earlier in the case with small-scale emerging flux. This result suggests that small-scale emerging flux accelerates the destabilization of the pre-eruptive magnetic configuration through enhanced current-sheet thinning and magnetic reconnection, leading to an earlier eruption onset. Furthermore, we find that the involvement of highly twisted field lines during the pre-eruption phase plays a crucial role in determining the eruption onset time.

papers.title: Study of the weak radiative decay $B_c^+\to B_u^{\ast+}γ$
papers.abstract: We investigate the rare radiative decay $B_c \to B_u^\ast\gamma$ within the Standard Model by using the instantaneous Bethe-Salpeter (BS) approach. The short distance (SD) $c \to u\gamma$ penguin, weak annihilation, and long distance (LD) vector meson dominance (VMD) contributions are all included. In the calculation of LD contribution, we use two scenarios, namely the decay width of $\rho$ being set to zero or kept as the experimental value, which gives $\mathrm{Br}_{\rm LD}=5.0\times10^{-9}$ and $7.3\times10^{-8}$, respectively, indicating an important role of $\Gamma_\rho$ in the calculation. The SD contribution is comparable in magnitude to the LD contributions, but one order larger than the annihilation contribution. This shows the $B_c \to B_u^\ast\gamma$ channel can provide an important way to study the flavor changing neutral current processes of charm quark.

papers.title: Is Dark Energy Inhomogeneous?
papers.abstract: The discovery of dark matter deficient galaxies motivates a fundamental question: Could sufficiently large regions of the Universe be deficient in dark energy as well? We investigate this possibility by developing a phenomenological framework that distinguishes genuine dark energy deficiencies from ordinary matter voids through nonlinear expansion, coherent peculiar velocities and density-momentum correlations. We show that a $10\%$ dark energy deficiency can suppress the expansion of a representative nonlinear void by approximately $2.7\%$, generating peculiar velocity residuals of order $60$-$100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ across scales of $30$-$50\, Mpc$. Intriguingly, we find that deficiencies of order $20\%$ extending over several hundred megaparsecs could also influence the locally inferred Hubble constant, potentially contributing to the $H_0$ tension, subject to stringent isotropy and dynamical consistency constraints. We identify observational strategies involving DESI, Rubin, peculiar velocity surveys, and cosmic void catalogues, opening a new avenue for testing whether the dark energy driving cosmic acceleration is truly homogeneous.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM
Dual Model Predictive Control through Sampling-Based Belief Propagation
A reachability criterion for spectrally factorable SPDC in coupled waveguides without periodic poling
papers.abstract: Producing spectrally pure photon pairs by spontaneous parametric down-conversion without periodic poling would broaden the choice of nonlinear materials. It requires optical modes that provide both phase matching and suitable group velocities. We derive a joint reachability criterion for a constant-cross-section coupler with a nonlinear main guide and a linear auxiliary. In a two-mode description, phase closure fixes the hybridization parameter that also determines the main-guide participation and the attainable group-delay ratio. This relation screens material and mode pairs and specifies detuning and participation targets for full-vector refinement. A first-order purity map connects the reachable delay ratio and bandwidth--length product to the photon-pair spectrum. A full-vector AlN/TiO$_2$ feasibility example satisfies direct phase matching with a ratio of pump--idler to pump--signal group-delay mismatches of $-0.899$ and yields a calculated unfiltered Schmidt purity of 0.789 over 5 mm. The criterion links phase closure, dispersion control, and nonlinear participation when assessing coupled-waveguide sources beyond periodically poled materials.

papers.title: Towards large-scale ab initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Efficient Sampling-based Quantum Computing Algorithms
papers.abstract: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) requires the calculation of highly accurate electronic-structure energies and nuclear forces at every time step, which can quickly become computationally expensive. Sample-based quantum diagonalization offers a route to such calculations on quantum hardware, but its use in AIMD simulations has so far been limited to active spaces of about 20 qubits. In these spaces, exact diagonalization is tractable, and the quantum circuits are typically built from standard coupled-cluster amplitudes. Here, we introduce SqDRIFT-AIMD, which combines randomized sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SqDRIFT) with analytical nuclear gradients. With SqDRIFT-AIMD, we obtain more accurate ground-state energies than the conventional coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) driven AIMD simulation for the $40$-qubit active space. We apply SqDRIFT-AIMD to study the dynamics of proton transfer in the Zundel cation, using circuits executed on IBM Heron r3 quantum processors. SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the $40$-qubit double-well PES and stay within a few m$E_\text{h}$ of CCSD at 52 qubits. The $40$-qubit SqDRIFT-AIMD trajectory tracks the SHCI-driven proton transfer to within $1.33$ mÅ and exhibits excellent total energy conservation, with a standard deviation of only $0.245$ m$E_\text{h}$. These results extend quantum-centric AIMD to active spaces beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

papers.title: A seven-element interval of power-semiring varieties
Two barriers for minimal time firing squads, with applications to four and five states
papers.abstract: A minimal-time solution of the firing squad synchronization problem synchronizes every line of n cells at time 2n minus 2. Six states suffice; whether five do has been open since 1987. Every line agrees with the half line until its right ends echo returns. For minimal time solutions with any number of states, we prove that cells at distance j behind the half lines front become time-periodic only after time (1.5 minus epsilon)j, for every epsilon greater than 0 and infinitely many j, and that the half line is never periodic in time and space on a wedge at its left border, hence not eventually regular in our sense. With certified satisfiability checks, we exclude four states using the lines of lengths 2 to 5 and parts of the next five, and show that every five state minimal time solution uses at least 15 non quiescent neighbourhoods on its half lines first 78 anti-diagonals. We give five state rules synchronizing exactly the lengths 2 to 14.

papers.title: Studying the Fullerene Nest: JWST Observations of the Planetary Nebula Tc 1. III. Tracing Fullerene-Linked Dust Variation
papers.abstract: We have observed the fullerene-rich planetary nebula Tc 1 with the MIRI/MRS on JWST. The mid-infrared spectra of this spatially resolved source reveal that the dust emission is not co-spatial with the fullerene emission. Three broad features can be distinguished: a 6$\unicode{x2013}$9 $\mu$m plateau, a 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau and the 30 $\mu$m feature. The 6$\unicode{x2013}$9 $\mu$m plateau does not change shape spectrally across the entire field of view, indicating it is produced by stochastically heated material. Spectral variations of the 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau reveal at least three distinct components, peaking at 9.5 $\mu$m, 11 $\mu$m and 12 $\mu$m respectively. SiC produces most likely at least the 11 $\mu$m component and we find evidence that the 12 $\mu$m component might be produced by SiC grains too. The variation in relative strength of these components across the field of view hints at dust processing taking place in Tc 1. The 9.5 $\mu$m component of the 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau has a strong correlation with the SiC component(s) and is thus likely produced by similar material.

papers.title: Spin Conductivity: Insight From Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract: The investigation on the spin conductivity has now been blooming in burgeoning altermagnetic materials. Here, an alternative and elementary derivation for the spin conductivity expression is presented. This is done within the context of perturbation theory. It indicates that our derived expression for the $\mathcal{T}$-even ($\mathcal{T}$ for time reversal) spin conductivity agrees exactly with those derived from the Kubo linear response theory and quantum kinetic theory. In addition, the expression for the $\mathcal{T}$-odd spin conductivity in the clean limit is exactly consistent with those presented previously. We show that the $\mathcal{T}$-odd ($\mathcal{T}$-even) spin conductivity arises from the contribution of zeroth-order (first-order) wave function correction. Our work provides some physical insight into the spin conductivity from the perturbation theory and shines more light on the charge-to-spin conversion mechanism in magnetic materials.

papers.title: Season by season causal analysis of the continuum and velocity-resolved H$β$ emission of NGC 5548
papers.abstract: We investigate possible causal influences in five historical seasons (1989-1993) of NGC 5548 using a version of the Synergistic-Unique-Redundant Decomposition (SURD) method adapted for this analysis, an information-theoretic causal discovery method for time series. Two four-variable sets contain the blue wing (B), core (C) and red wing (R) of H-beta together with either total H-beta (H) or the 5100 Angstrom continuum (F). We examine 7200 decompositions with common and unequal lags, two or three seasonal flux states, and base delays of 1-30 d. We rank the individual named components within each information family, reporting their amplitudes and simultaneous leakage. In 1989, unique continuum information about the core reaches 0.799 and 0.387 of target entropy for two and three states, with leakage 0.047 and 0.276. In 1992, the red-wing history supplies unique information about the future blue wing in both variable sets and both state counts, with peak target-entropy fractions 0.106-0.166. Distinct joint influences also emerge: for the 1991 core, the two-state S(F,B) and S(F,R) components contribute 0.187 and 0.125 at 20 d with leakage 0.087, although the unique continuum term vanishes. Strong core-wing redundancy identifies candidate inputs for simpler predictive models. Large late-lag leakage, reaching approximately 0.97 in the total set, identifies targets for additional driver measurements and richer temporal histories. The resulting seasonal map of individual, shared and joint influences complements the response delays and velocity structure measured by reverberation mapping, and provides specific causal hypotheses for the evolving broad-line region.

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Line-Search Quasi-Newton Method for Discounted Markov Decision Processes
Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
papers.abstract: Electronic band structures govern how crystals conduct electrons and absorb light. Density-functional theory (DFT) computes them through costly self-consistent iterations, while existing machine-learning models either predict isolated scalar properties or output Hamiltonians that still require DFT solvers. Here we present EpNet, a learned empirical pseudopotential for crystals spanning 63 elements across the \textit{s}, \textit{p} and \textit{d} blocks. An equivariant neural network builds its Hamiltonian from physics-motivated local potentials and nonlocal projectors. Trained solely on band energies, EpNet predicts complete band structures directly from atomic coordinates. On unseen chemical systems, its median errors are \winAll\ eV for band energies and \gapAll\ eV for band gaps. On 600,000 structures from an independent database, its band-gap errors are overall less than half those of existing models, at about 1\% of DFT cost. EpNet thus enables fast screening of electronic properties for materials discovery and electronic-structure simulations of large systems.

papers.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
Rescene-ESM: an Earth system model built around a frozen AI weather model
papers.abstract: Earth system models underpin climate projections, but their cost limits how many scenarios, ensemble members and impact pathways can be explored. Machine-learning weather models forecast as skillfully as physics-based models at a fraction of the cost, yet coupled to an ocean they have produced weak El Nino variability or have learned it from climate-model output, and none carries the climate through rivers to the people exposed to it. Here we present Rescene-ESM, an Earth system model whose coupler, YAHO, yokes a frozen 20.8-million-parameter AI weather model to physically formulated ocean, sea-ice, land, river, carbon and energy components constrained by observations. Adding the couplings one at a time shows what each contributes: over a climatological ocean the AI atmosphere varies from year to year by a third of the observed amount over the oceans, and an interactive mixed layer, an equatorial wave ocean, the residual of the observed sea surface temperature (SST) equation as stochastic forcing and the land's moisture flux raise this step by step and bring El Nino and its teleconnections, leaving the mean climate almost unchanged. The full model simulates about 1,000 years per day on one graphics processing unit, holds the observed climate for a thousand years without drift, reproduces the observed 1979-2022 global warming, carries forced change with a physically based structure around the frozen network (transient climate response 1.60 K), routes runoff to 212 river gauges with a median seasonal-cycle correlation of 0.79 and, driven by emissions, separates the heatwave exposure of an SSP1 and an SSP3 world by a factor of 4.7 in 2081-2100, three-quarters of it through the warmer climate.

papers.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
papers.abstract: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.

papers.title: Symplectic Normal Coordinates Flow for Generative Modeling of Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: In conditioned generative models of physical systems, the densities at different values of the conditioning parameters are often related through symplectic transformations. For stable linear Hamiltonian systems, there exists a symplectic transformation to "normal coordinates" such that the dynamics is reduced to rotations in each phase-space plane. This picture extends to the nonlinear case where, away from resonances, the Birkhoff normal form again consists of rotations in phase space, now with amplitude dependence. In this work, we introduce an invertible symplectic flow layer consisting of amplitude-dependent rotations in learned normal coordinates. We derive the condition under which the nonlinear rotation layer is symplectic and detail an architecture that guarantees it. Experiments are carried out on three conditional generative modeling problems: a synthetic chain of coupled nonlinear oscillators and two problems from accelerator physics. We show empirically that normalizing flows with the new layers achieve competitive or superior negative log-likelihoods compared to baseline flows, with gains that grow with the strength of the nonlinearity on the synthetic system.

papers.title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
papers.abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

papers.title: Non-log-concave $τ$-polynomials of regular graphs
Analysis of Solid Boron Injection for ITER
papers.abstract: Since ITER will now operate with a full tungsten divertor and first wall, the ITER Organization is considering boron wall conditioning schemes to getter oxygen and reduce tungsten sputtering to avoid excessive radiation to ensure that ITER can reach and sustain high- performance plasma operation. ITER has adopted Glow Discharge Boronization (GDB) in deuterated diborane (B$_2$D$_6$) as its main technique, which can only be performed in the absence of magnetic fields, but has also requested a study to determine how effective solid boron injection (SBI), which can be performed during plasma operation, using either an Impurity Powder Dropper (IPD) or a boron pellet injector, might be as a risk mitigation to achieving Q=10. Solid impurity injection has been used for decades as a wall conditioning technique on numerous tokamaks and stellarators around the world. The study presented here begins to assess SBI on ITER by first quantifying the boron source term across a particle size scan from 1 $\mu$m to 5 mm diameter and an injection velocity scan from 5 -- 200 m/s for several ITER plasma conditions: 1) Start of Research Operations (SRO) diverted L-mode, 2) Q=10 H-mode, and 3) low plasma current and low power limiter operation. Modeling of the ablation, transport, erosion and redeposition of solid boron is being carried out with the Dust Injection Simulator (DIS), the Neutral Gas Shielding (NGS), EMC3-EIRENE and WallDYN3D models. In the first steps presented here, the DIS and NGS models are compared for calculating the boron source term that is then used as input to EMC3-EIRENE and will later be used with WallDYN3D.

papers.title: Kinematic Total-Body PET Video Reconstruction via Hierarchical List-Mode EM and Validation-Adaptive Space-Time Regularisation
papers.abstract: Kinematic PET is introduced as an imaging task focused on visualisation of early radiotracer delivery and rapid multi-organ motion without gating. The proposed kinematic video reconstruction method uses 33-ms frames (~30 frames per second), initialised with 3D expectation maximisation (EM) time of flight (TOF) list-mode reconstruction, followed by cycles of a 2-stage update. These 2 stages are i) a hierarchical EM (HEM) update using multiple temporal pooling levels, and ii) a validation-adaptive space-time (VAST) regularisation update. HEM combines frame-specific EM corrections with corrections estimated from higher-count temporal blocks, slowing noise amplification for the ultrashort frames. VAST mixes each 3D target patch in a frame with source patches sampled nearby in space and time. It selects the candidate that best matches the mean of the corresponding patches in the two adjacent frames, with the unchanged patch also eligible. Optional temporal block sum correction uses the initial EM temporal sum as a reference to reduce loss of spatial detail. HEM+VAST was evaluated with a dynamic digital phantom, and demonstrated on human FDG data acquired on a Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra (28 - 58 s post-injection). At a background spatial coefficient of variation of 10%, the temporal full width at half maximum of the fastest phantom bolus was 151 ms with HEM+VAST, compared with 86 ms for the ground truth. The video frame rate FDG images reveal vascular and organ detail, radiotracer bolus passage and respiration-related multi-organ motion. Kinematic PET could complement conventional dynamic PET by supporting the development of image-derived physiological biomarkers and motion estimation for quantitative reconstruction. Future work should compare HEM+VAST with prior 4D PET reconstruction methods at the same 33-ms frame duration and matched noise levels.

papers.title: Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits
papers.abstract: Designing real-time control for nonlinear systems to track periodic orbits can be challenging, especially for complex and coupled dynamical systems (e.g., tethered kites), where the true model parameters are hard to obtain. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor. The approach combines the underlying periodic structure of the dynamics along with periodic state-input trajectory data to learn physically consistent linear predictors (in lifted/observable space). We leverage Floquet theory, which studies the stability of periodic orbits in nonlinear systems, to obtain the periodic stability information of a given orbit via a monodromy matrix (i.e., the state transition matrix over an entire period). Subsequently, we impose open-loop monodromy constraints to learn Floquet-parameterized linear predictors using a least-squares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) formulation, thereby constraining the search space and aiding in Koopman learning. We then utilize these linear predictors to design a model predictive control (MPC) law for tracking periodic references. Finally, we evaluate the designed framework on a cartpole system under periodic forcing and compare it against a purely data-driven baseline.

papers.title: Bridging Gaps with Tensor Networks: From the Haldane Gap and Beyond
papers.abstract: Proofs generated by large language models are often difficult to understand, generalize, or formalize directly. Here we verify, digest, and formalize OpenAI's computer-assisted proof of a uniform gap in the periodic spin-1 Heisenberg chain using tensor-network diagrams and Lean 4. Reading the partition-function network along space and imaginary time shows how finite-ring bounds propagate across doubled lengths and inverse temperatures to all longer even rings, sharpening the spin-1 bound from the same finite inputs by a factor of 19 to $\Delta_L > 0.0729$ for all even $L \geq 36$. We identify reflection positivity as the general condition behind the proof and certify uniform gaps in seven additional spin chains and ladders. More broadly, digesting machine-generated proofs into transparent physical mechanisms yields sharper bounds, broader theorems, and reusable formal verifications.

papers.title: Almost sharp global well-posedness and low-regularity blow-up for the two-dimensional periodic Zakharov system
Quark- and hadronic-level CPT violation phenomenology of neutral-mesons at at $d=5$ of the SME
papers.abstract: This article summarizes an investigation of the connection between the hadron-level scalar effective field theory treatment of Lorentz symmetry violation in neutral-meson oscillations and the corresponding quark level $d=5$ nonminimal SME approach. The correspondence between the quark-level $a^{(5)}$ term is identified to first order in CPT violation (CPTV) based on the expectation that C, P, T symmetries and the spontaneously broken chiral symmetry of QCD should hold for both formalism. These can be related to the phenomenological parameter describing possible CPTV in the meson oscillations. A general result facilitating searches for kaons is given.

papers.title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
Agents Propose, Code Verifies, Humans Decide: Verified Agentic Ingestion of Heterogeneous Scientific Tables into Relational Databases
papers.abstract: Public scientific datasets rarely arrive analysis-ready. They arrive as messy folders of wide matrices, long tables, spreadsheets, and per-cohort files whose keys and encodings differ, and every reanalysis must reconnect them first. A coding agent can automate this, but its mistakes can look plausible, and without an audit trail, a mistake that corrupts data can go uncaught. We present an AI-assisted ingestion pipeline built on one rule: LLM agents propose, deterministic code verifies, and humans decide. Narrow agents see compact, citable evidence about the files, never the data, and return typed proposals. A verifier with 39 check types tests each proposal against that evidence in two loops, one for the schema's structure and one for its meaning, and a human reviewer approves the schema and the load. Code compiles PostgreSQL DDL, reshapes the data, quarantines rows it cannot place, records provenance, and reconciles every staged row against the database. On four public biomedical datasets, one held out from development, 9 of 20 first proposals failed a check and every failure was caught: the loops repaired eight, and a one-line reviewer edit fixed the ninth. All 45.1 million values loaded with zero reconciliation gap. Discovering a dataset's structure took 4-7 LLM calls and preparing its data at most one more, costing under $0.50 per dataset. In a separate test, each of nine planted data errors was quarantined with a reason or recorded in an audit log.

papers.title: Exact sampling beyond Fock inputs and linear optics: photon-number superpositions, photonic matrix-product states, adaptive and non-linear circuits
papers.abstract: Clifford and Clifford's algorithm samples single-photon boson sampling exactly, one output mode at a time, by adding the input photons in a uniformly random order. We extend this construction to other input states and to adaptive and non-linear circuits. It applies whenever non-negative weights on output prefixes and input sets satisfy one marginal identity, a set-chain lemma: the random-order sampler is then exact at one weight evaluation per candidate mode, and it gives the posterior over the hidden input set. We build four exact samplers on it. For sources in a superposition of vacuum and one photon, the weights are rectangular permanents on an offset input set, and the cost has the exponent of single photons under loss. For photonic matrix-product states of bond dimension $\chi$, a gap-by-gap Kraus contraction turns each weight into a short sum of squared amplitudes. For adaptive linear optics, the chain starts from the posterior given the adaptive counts and rejects chains that contradict them. For a single-mode non-linear phase the identity fails, and rejection from linear branches is exact with acceptance $1/\|c\|_1^2$. All four samplers agree with strong simulation on small instances, and cost models put adaptive sampling with up to three adaptive modes within $10\%$ of single photons and a non-linear site at $\varphi=\pi/2$ at about $4\times$.

papers.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
papers.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

papers.title: Jacobi fields and Jacobi sections for semisprays on Lie algebroids: transverse variations and equivalences
Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels
Demonstration of High fmax (> 80 GHz) in Recessed-Gate and Passivated $\mathrm{Al_{0.60}Ga_{0.40}N}$ Channel RF HEMTs
papers.abstract: In this work, ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) $\mathrm{Al_{0.60}Ga_{0.40}N}$ channel high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) with an $\mathrm{Al_{0.81}Ga_{0.19}N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al_{0.86}Ga_{0.14}N}$ back barrier were fabricated. The devices featured a recessed T-gate structure and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ passivation. Scaled devices achieved a cutoff frequency ($f_{\mathrm{T}}$) of 35 GHz, a maximum oscillation frequency ($f_{\mathrm{max}}$) of 82 GHz, and an average breakdown field $> 3 \mathrm{MV/cm}$, while maintaining a reasonable current collapse of $\sim 20\%$ under a 40 V drain bias in pinch-off condition. Devices with larger dimensions demonstrated a high off-state breakdown voltage of 883 V and an $f_{\mathrm{T}}$ of 24 GHz, yielding a high Johnson's figure of merit ($\mathrm{JFOM}$) of 21.19 $\mathrm{THz \cdot V}$. Across all device geometries, a high $I_{\mathrm{ON}}/I_{\mathrm{OFF}}$ ratio exceeding $10^6$ was observed with drain and gate leakage currents strictly below $10^{-6} \mathrm{A/mm}$. This work demonstrates an optimized design for $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel RF HEMTs and their excellent potential for X- to Ka-band applications.

papers.title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
papers.abstract: This work investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson interferometry within the nonminimal Standard-Model Extension. Employing methods of chiral perturbation theory for mass dimension d=5, a connection between the quark-level and the meson effective pseudoscalar Lagrangian is established. The resulting phenomenological signatures in neutral-meson oscillations with particular focus on the detector geometry are explored. This analysis permits the interpretation of such CPT tests within the d=5 quark sector of the Standard-Model Extension. Existing data are used to extract first constraints on two coefficients and to estimate achievable sensitivity gains over published bounds of up to 18 orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Evolutionary games on networks with negative edge-based environmental feedback
papers.abstract: Environmental feedback can fundamentally alter the game payoff structure underlying the evolution of cooperation. How feedback-evolving games interact with population structure under non-weak selection remains incompletely understood. We study an evolutionary game on networks in which each edge has a binary environmental state that determines the payoff matrix used by the two connected individuals. By assumption, cooperation tends to improve the local environment, which in turn favors defection, thereby creating negative feedback between strategies coupled with the environmental condition. We analyze the model under strong selection using a mean-field approximation, a pair approximation that tracks both strategy pairs and edge environments, and agent-based simulations. In well-mixed populations, the feedback can generate bistability between full cooperation and full defection, as well as sustained oscillations arising through a Hopf bifurcation. Sparse networks (i.e., with low nodes' degrees) can eliminate bistability, suppress oscillations, and produce stable intermediate levels of cooperation. The pair approximation captures these effects and generally agrees more closely with simulations on sparse networks than the mean-field approximation. Our results show that edge-based environmental feedback and network structure, such as density of edges, interact to determine whether the fraction of cooperators stabilizes or oscillates over time.

papers.title: Kinematically Unrestricted Flat Space Scattering from AdS$_{d+1} \times$ S$^p$/CFT$_d$
papers.abstract: We construct scattering states for scalar fields with generic kinematics from CFT operators in the flat space limit of AdS/CFT. The states can have momentum along the compact $S^p$ directions of $AdS_{d+1}\times S^p$, which is achieved by scaling to large R-symmetry charge and choosing a particular parameterization for the R-symmetry polarization. These states allow for the construction of an unrestricted S-matrix from the flat space limit of CFT correlation functions, which we check for various tree level interactions. We also describe a generalization of the Mellin space formalism which incorporates the compact momentum, and we discuss some possible implications for flat space holography.

papers.title: Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
Weak $λ$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mrówka spaces
A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
A Witness for Quantum Correlations Using Nonlinear Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The ability to detect and quantify entanglement in molecular systems is essential for understanding their quantum correlations and to evaluating molecules as platforms for quantum technologies. Here we show how signals from existing spectroscopic techniques can provide sufficient information to witness entanglement. The main ingredient is a spectroscopic map from admissible quantum states to a finite-dimensional space of signal coefficients, which are expectation values of state-independent effective observables. The molecular response model and measurement protocol determine the effective observables for a fixed system bipartition, and the spectroscopic map defines sets of joint expectation values compatible with all admissible quantum states and their separable subset. We illustrate the construction of the effective observables and their expectation value sets using rotational invariants and the spectral structure of optical signals. Fluorescence dynamics and photon coincidences provide a complementary example. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for entanglement certification with established spectroscopic techniques.

papers.title: Toward universal excited-state machine-learned potentials: a local excitation Hamiltonian for size consistency and transferability
papers.abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials could make excited-state simulations across chemical space routine, but excitation energies, unlike ground-state energies, are not sums of atomic contributions. The excited states of noninteracting molecules are the union of their states, which pooled multistate readouts reproduce at best for the lowest state. We introduce LEH-MACE, whose excitation energies are the eigenvalues of a local excitation Hamiltonian assembled from atom-centred blocks, so this union holds exactly. We generated TD-DFT energies and forces for about 300,000 equilibrium, thermal, and excited-state geometries of over 100,000 molecules. LEH-MACE's advantage over direct readouts grew with the distance from the training data and was largest above $S_1$, with about half their $S_2$ and $S_3$ errors for long conjugated oligomers. For molecule pairs, only LEH-MACE kept its single-molecule accuracy, while a softmin readout remained superior for $S_1$ dynamics of larger chromophores. Exact size consistency is thus one step toward such potentials.

papers.title: ProtLink: Sequence and Multispecies Graph Context for Protein Interaction Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-protein interactions (PPIs) from sequence alone is difficult, while known interaction networks may provide informative biological context. We introduce ProtLink, a sequence-conditioned graph-learning framework that combines frozen ESM-2 representations with protein interaction topology and orthogroup-mediated connections between species. We compare sequence-only models, GraphSAGE, a homogeneous graph transformer, and a heterogeneous graph transformer (HGT) for human PPI prediction. In an initial edge-level comparison, three-layer multispecies HGT with ESM-2 650M features achieves an average precision (AP) of 0.980 under random negative sampling, compared with 0.951 for the homogeneous transformer; its AP decreases to 0.878 with two-hop-preferred negatives. In controlled three-seed experiments, three-layer full-graph HGT obtains an AP of $0.9701\pm0.0022$, exceeding an orthogroup-only model ($0.9435\pm0.0094$). The corresponding two-layer comparison shows little additional benefit from non-human PPI edges, consistent with the greater message-passing depth needed to transmit their information. For human proteins excluded from training interactions, multispecies HGT achieves $0.8335\pm0.0094$ AP versus $0.6482\pm0.0052$ for a sequence-only pair model. These results identify the value, depth dependence, and limits of evolutionary graph context while distinguishing prediction of held-out edges from generalization to held-out proteins.

papers.title: Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model
papers.abstract: For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.

papers.title: The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density
Sensitivity of jet and dijet observables to medium effects in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV using X-SCAPE/JETSCAPE
papers.abstract: Establishing jet quenching in small collision systems, such as high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions at the LHC, is challenging because the expected modifications are small and can be obscured by event-selection effects, multiparton interactions, and multijet production. We examine the response of several jet and dijet observables to medium-induced changes in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV using the JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE framework. First, a simplified Bjorken-expanding brick medium is compared with a vacuum reference for several brick lengths and strengths of transport coefficients. Second, separately generated realistic vacuum and medium samples with fluctuating initial conditions and event-by-event hydrodynamic evolution are compared after selecting the highest-activity 20% of events. Full anti-$k_T$ jets are reconstructed with $R=0.2$ and $R=0.4$. The observables are dijet invariant mass, leading- and subleading-jet transverse momentum, folded azimuthal separation, dijet asymmetry, Soft-Drop groomed jet radius, and groomed mass. In the brick calculation, the dijet-mass spectrum shows the clearest ordered response: departures from the vacuum reference generally increase with brick length and strength of transport coefficient and are more visible for the narrower jet radius, while the jet-$p_T$ and dijet-asymmetry changes are smaller and no clear azimuthal broadening is resolved. In the selected realistic events, the ungroomed medium-to-vacuum ratios remain close to unity but contain localized kinematic differences, together with a modest increase of the mean dijet asymmetry. The groomed-radius and groomed-mass ratios show localized differences but do not exhibit a persistent angular narrowing or mass redistribution. These findings quantify the sensitivity of the studied observables to medium-induced jet modifications in the present pp calculations.

papers.title: Learning Actionable Information Landscapes for Multimodal Active Sensing in Hawkmoths
papers.abstract: Animals integrate information across sensory modalities to guide exploration, suggesting that they maintain internal estimates of where actions are expected to reduce uncertainty. However, how such action-conditioned information maps are learned from multimodal sensory experience remains unclear, as previous studies have been largely confined to unimodal sensing frameworks. We introduce a multimodal predictive-coding framework for learning uncertainty-reduction maps from visual and mechanosensory observations in hawkmoth flower interaction tasks. A variational generative model trained on simulated environments recovers modality-specific information landscapes over the action space, capturing how visual patterns, surface geometry, and mechanosensory cues shape the value of exploratory actions. These learned maps are consistent with several features of hawkmoth behavior, including nonzero tracking offsets, probing along visual patterns, and geometry-dependent exploration. Applying the model to behavioral data from flower tracking and nectary search, we find that natural trajectories tend to occupy regions of high uncertainty reduction in these learned maps. Building on these observations, we develop an uncertainty-gated lexicographic algorithm that switches between information gathering and reward exploitation based on perceptual uncertainty. In nectary search, uncertainty gating improves learning relative to exploit-only, $\epsilon$-greedy, fixed-time, and uncertainty-calibrated non-lexicographic controls, with better generalization and robustness to sensory and curvature shifts. These results link information landscapes learned through generative modeling to biological sensing and embodied exploration.

papers.title: Cause-specific structural nested cumulative survival time models for competing risks, with application to the Antibody Mediated Prevention trials
papers.abstract: The Antibody Mediated Prevention (AMP) trials randomized participants to VRC01, a broadly neutralizing antibody, or placebo; the primary analysis estimated prevention efficacy against overall HIV-1 acquisition and against acquisition of VRC01-sensitive strains. All participants were offered daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and PrEP uptake in a trial may differ substantially from uptake in other settings. It is therefore of interest to estimate the effect of oral PrEP on acquisition of VRC01-sensitive and VRC01-insensitive strains, as well as the counterfactual cumulative incidence of such acquisition under no or limited PrEP uptake. To address these questions, we extend the structural nested cumulative survival time model (SNCSTM), a causal survival model for time-varying treatments, to a cause-specific version. We show that the cause-specific SNCSTM is closely related to the Fine--Gray subdistribution hazard model, and we study identification under two frameworks. The first, based on sequential ignorability, applies when the time-varying treatment is distinct from the randomized assignment, as with oral PrEP use in AMP. The second, based on an instrumental variable, applies when the time-varying treatment represents compliance with the randomized assignment, and it accommodates unmeasured confounding between the time-varying treatment and event time. Under both frameworks, we propose consistent and asymptotically normal estimators of the structural parameters. We apply the methods to HVTN 704/HPTN 085, one of the two AMP trials, to estimate the effects of oral PrEP use and of VRC01 infusions administered every 8 weeks on acquisition of VRC01-sensitive and VRC01-insensitive HIV-1 strains. We also estimate the counterfactual strain-specific cumulative incidence curves under no oral PrEP use and under full adherence to the scheduled VRC01 infusions.

papers.title: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
papers.abstract: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-V\theta)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $\kappa/2\pi$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8\pi GT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-V\theta)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-V\theta$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.

papers.title: Choosing the basis to compare multivariate distributions: bases, copulas and optimal transport
papers.abstract: We study the choice of an orthonormal basis for comparing two probability distributions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ through their one-dimensional projections. We show that two distributions have a common copula in a given basis if and only if their optimal transport can be performed componentwise along the directions of that basis. This motivates the notion of componentwise related distributions and leads to a structural analysis of the bases in which such a representation is possible. In particular, we establish an essential uniqueness result for the corresponding orthogonal decomposition and characterize elliptical families through equality in Gelbrich's bound within location-scatter families. For general distributions, we consider the maximum, over all orthonormal bases, of the sum of the squared quadratic Wasserstein distances between the corresponding one-dimensional projections. We prove that the resulting quantity is a metric, induces the same topology as the quadratic Wasserstein distance, and lies between the Gelbrich and Wasserstein distances, with equality in the upper bound precisely for component-wise related distributions. We also derive first-order conditions for an optimal basis and establish stability and almost-sure consistency of empirical optimal bases. Simulations and examples illustrate the computational feasibility and competitive performance of the proposed procedures and suggest new applications of copulas to multivariate distributional comparisons.

papers.title: The Herzog--Schönheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
authors: Moungi G. Bawendi (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)
papers.abstract: Collective excitonic interactions in supramolecular assemblies offer opportunities for efficient light harvesting and directed energy transport. Here, we demonstrate efficient energy transfer from two-dimensional silica-encapsulated TDBC J-aggregate sheets to covalently attached ATTO 590 molecular acceptors. Silica encapsulation preserves the J-aggregate excitonic properties while enabling acceptor functionalization at a defined separation from the donor plane. Steady-state donor quenching and acceptor sensitization yield energy-transfer efficiencies of 75-81% in solution, while time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal donor lifetime shortening. We develop a generalized Forster resonance energy-transfer model for an extended planar donor coupled to localized molecular acceptors, predicting an inverse fourth-power dependence of the transfer rate on donor-acceptor separation. Using experimental spectroscopic data and estimated structural parameters, the model predicts an energy-transfer rate of 4.77 x 10^10 s^-1, approximately ten times faster than the intrinsic donor decay rate, corresponding to a theoretical energy-transfer efficiency of approximately 91%. These findings provide a framework for developing hybrid excitonic architectures for light harvesting.

papers.title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
papers.abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordström black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.

papers.title: Toward a theory of Evaluability
papers.abstract: Machine learning models, particularly large foundation models, are increasingly evaluated along multiple axes that are relevant for their usage. In addition to accuracy measures appropriate for the specific task of interest, measures capturing safety, calibration and fairness properties are often of interest. The classical approach to these problems assumes that the test set has been held out from the training process, an assumption that is increasingly harder to justify for large foundation models. In this work, we formalize a notion of evaluability without this assumption, and ask if it is feasible to evaluate black-box models in settings where our test samples may have been used during training. We study this problem under different settings, capturing different levels of access to the model. We first study the natural setting, where the evaluator only looks at the output of the model on the test set. We fully characterize the class of distributions where accurate evaluation is possible, and show tight upper and lower bounds on the sample complexity of evaluation. Our results show that black-box evaluation in this setup is feasible if and only if the distribution is close to being small support. We then consider evaluation algorithms that can query the model on additional inputs and demonstrate connections to self-correctors studied in program testing. Using these, we show that a small amount of query access can increase the power of the evaluator for natural distributions and concept classes.

papers.title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
papers.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $\Delta E_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~\mu\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. We discuss strategies to improve photon indistinguishability, including radiative-rate engineering, charge stabilization, and more selective excitation. Our results combine MOVPE growth, deterministic device integration, and telecom C-band emission, providing a route toward scalable semiconductor quantum light sources for fiber-based quantum networks.

papers.title: The forces at hand: social learning is permissive, not instructive, for the evolution of phenotypic plasticity
papers.abstract: Evolution can favour a trait for two reasons: an instructive cause makes selection favour the trait; a permissive one lets it persist once selection no longer removes it. The distinction matters most for phenotypic plasticity and its replacement by inherited behaviour, genetic assimilation, the Baldwin effect. Social learning is credited with favouring plasticity on evidence that cannot tell the two apart: how much plasticity remains at the end of a simulation. Here we show, analytically and computationally, which role it plays in a minimal model of learning and evolution. Writing expected fitness as a function of plasticity, we find that environmental change is the only source of benefit from plasticity, and the social channel enters only its cost. Simulation confirms this: in a static environment selection against plasticity never reverses sign at any channel strength; when the environment changes, it reverses at a threshold the channel lowers, and without the channel the population collapses before reaching it. Social learning is permissive, not instructive: it supplies the means to be plastic, never the reason. For the debate over whether plasticity leads evolution, this is one case settled by measurement: environmental change directs, socially inherited information permits, and neither suffices alone.

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
Holomorphic Isometric Embeddings of the Unit Disk into the Symmetrized Bidisk
An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
papers.abstract: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined by terminal DC voltages and line resistances, which inherently limits the capability of changing individual line currents for essential grid services such as power flow management and overloading prevention. To address these two limitations, DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC power flow controllers (DCPFCs) have been developed. The conventional DCCBs are two-port devices installed in series with DC lines at their terminals in an MTDC converter substation, so that any fault current flowing through the line can be rapidly cleared. Additionally, a DCPFC can be installed at line terminals to adjust terminal voltages and power exchanges among adjacent lines. As a result, for a substation that connects to multiple lines, it needs to host multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, which significantly increases the cost and footprint of both the substation and the MTDC grid. To this end, this work proposes an integrated equipment combining multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, called the interline multiport DCCB with DCPFC, which can reduce the number of components and enhance the economic feasibility of MTDC networks. This paper presents the topology, operation principles, and component selection procedures of the proposed equipment, and compares it with the state-of-the-art technologies. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results validate the fault interruption and power flow control performance of the interline multiport DCCB with PFC.

papers.title: Tidally-induced vertical asymmetries in the LMC bar and disk
papers.abstract: Past observations and simulations have shown that the bar in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) may be tilted with respect to the disk plane, and that the outer LMC disk could be warped. These studies propose that the tilted bar and the warp in the LMC are induced by the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) pericentric passages. We analyze and quantify the effect of the SMC passage on the vertical position and kinematic asymmetries of both the bar and disk, as a function of different impact parameters or initial conditions. We used seven representative simulations from the KRATOS suite of $N$-body simulations of the LMC, SMC and Milky Way (MW) system for this analysis. To classify bar particles and analyze the bar and disk separately, we adopted a classification method based on persistent homology. To quantify the vertical asymmetries in the bar and disk of the LMC-like galaxy, we applied Fourier decomposition. We constructed Gaia DR3 mock catalogs to study whether the observed vertical asymmetries in Gaia DR3 are caused by astrometric uncertainties. We detect strong $m = 1$ vertical asymmetries in the bar and disk of the LMC-like galaxy for all interacting simulations after the pericentric passage of the SMC-like galaxy, indicative of a warped bar and disk. We also detect $m=2$ vertical asymmetries in the bar of the LMC-like galaxy for some simulations, indicative of a buckling bar. We conclude that the SMC passages induce vertical asymmetries in both the bar and the disk of the LMC, compatible to those measured in Gaia DR3. Tidal interactions naturally give rise to a warped and buckling LMC bar, and a warped LMC disk. Comparison between our results and Gaia DR3 suggest that models with a higher mass ratio between the SMC and the LMC may be favorable for reproducing the observed tilt of the LMC bar, and that the most recent SMC pericentric passage occurred at most 210 to 300 Myr ago.

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms
Superconductivity and Polar Metallicity in Atomically Thin Nitride Superlattices
papers.abstract: The integration of polar and superconducting materials in the atomically thin limit typically results in a competition that suppresses the superconducting order. Here, we challenge this conventional view by employing first-principles calculations to investigate 1:1 superlattices composed of alternating atomically thin layers of TiN/AlN and {\delta}-NbN/AlN. Contrary to the expectation that dense insulating barriers would quench superconductivity, we find that the polar interface can coexist with a superconducting state. We observe that the transition temperature (Tc) of TiN is enhanced by nearly 2 K over its bulk value, while {\delta}-NbN maintains a relatively high Tc exceeding 20 K. We demonstrate that this resilience arises from the formation of a polar metal, where the strong internal electric fields of the AlN layers are partially screened by a charge redistribution within the nitride layers. This screening mechanism, along with the geometric confinement, creates a quasi-two-dimensional electronic environment, establishing these superlattices as a novel platform for exploring the coexistence of structural inversion-symmetry breaking and superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit.

papers.title: Inference for Non-Probability Samples Using Error-Prone Auxiliary Information
papers.abstract: Non-probability samples are a potential source of rich information for making statistical inferences. However, these datasets often suffer from quality issues, in particular selection bias. The data from a non-probability sample may be combined with auxiliary information from the population or from a reference probability sample to address this bias.
