Across all tested noise models and data sizes, regularization consistently reduces the median realized control cost relative to the corresponding controller without covariance regularization, with reductions of up to 35%.

papers.title: Temperature-Driven Evolution of Magnetization Dynamics in Cobalt-Doped Fe$_5$GeTe$_2$
papers.abstract: Understanding magnetization dynamics in metallic van der Waals ferromagnets is essential to uncover their magnetic interactions and evaluate their potential for high-frequency spintronics applications. In this study, we investigate the temperature-dependent magnetization dynamics of a single crystal of cobalt-doped $Fe_{5}GeTe_{2}$ (CFGT) using broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy. At high temperatures, the FMR response is dominated by a single broad resonance that shifts toward lower magnetic fields upon cooling. Fits to the frequency dependence of the resonance field and linewidth yield an effective $g$ factor of approximately 2.45 and an effective Gilbert damping parameter of approximately 0.15 near room temperature. The effective magnetic anisotropy evolves strongly with temperature, with an increasingly pronounced easy-plane contribution upon cooling toward 200 K. Below approximately 200 K, an additional resonance emerges and evolves into a distinct two-mode response that persists to the lowest measured temperature of 25 K. The two branches exhibit different temperature dependences of their resonance fields and linewidths, and the emergence of the additional mode is not accompanied by a comparably pronounced anomaly in the static magnetization. These results reveal a dynamical crossover in CFGT that is not readily apparent from bulk magnetometry and highlight the sensitivity of FMR to the magnetic behavior of chemically substituted van der Waals ferromagnets.

papers.title: Jais 3: Introducing Arabic-centric Agentic AI
authors: Sheikh Khalid bin Khalifa Al Nahyan
papers.abstract: We present Jais 3, a fleet of six open, Arabic-centric agentic language models ranging from 0.9B to 375B parameters. Jais 3 is built to complete tasks for Arabic speakers, not only to answer questions in plain text: it is trained to plan multi-step tasks, call tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, operate a terminal, search the web, and read, edit, and produce PDF, spreadsheet, and presentation files, while communicating with the user in Arabic. Instead of pretraining from scratch, we adapt each model of the fully open K2 Horizon fleet to Arabic through continual pretraining, followed by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), final token preference optimization (FTPO), and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We combine natural Arabic text with translated, transliterated, and synthetic Arabic, and replay the base model's own training data to keep its reasoning, agentic, and English abilities. Jais 3 covers Modern Standard Arabic and the major regional dialects, follows instructions with Arabic-specific constraints, and inherits the 512K-token context window of K2 Horizon (all models except the 0.9B). To our knowledge, its 375B model is the largest open Arabic-centric language model to date. For evaluation, we revisit how Arabic models are assessed, moving to fully generative evaluation on audited Arabic benchmarks. Across model sizes, Jais 3 matches or outperforms open-weight models of comparable size on Arabic and agentic benchmarks, with particularly strong agentic capabilities and Arabic instruction following, and far fewer hallucinations. We release the weights and the checkpoints from every training stage of all six models, together with samples of the training data, the data recipes and training configurations, the training logs, the audited benchmarks, and the evaluation code.

papers.title: Lower-Level Agnostic Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization is a fundamental framework for machine learning problems, where an upper-level (UL) objective depends on the solution of a nested lower-level (LL) problem. Existing bilevel algorithms typically assume that the LL objective is available for evaluation, differentiation, or unrolling. However, this assumption can fail when the LL response is produced by a black-box solver, simulator, adversary, or learned predictor. In this paper, we study LL agnostic bilevel optimization, where the UL learner has access only to an approximate LL solution $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ and cannot query the LL objective, its gradients, Hessian/Jacobian information, or the procedure that generates the LL response. We propose LeGo-BiO, a coordinate-wise pseudo-hypergradient method that estimates the missing Jacobian $\nabla _{\mathbf{x}}\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ using finite differences of $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\cdot)$. For each UL coordinate, LeGo-BiO constructs a decision vector subject to 1-sparse updates, thereby isolating the corresponding Jacobian column needed in the UL gradient computation. This avoids the directional-projection limitation of full-parameter response differences and, unlike derivative-free/zeroth-order approximations of the entire UL gradient, preserves the available first-order gradient information with respect to the UL variables for more accurate UL gradient evaluation. We establish convergence guarantees for LeGo-BiO in both deterministic and stochastic settings under an LL error-bound/Polyak-Lojasiewicz-type condition, without requiring LL strong convexity. Our bounds yield an $O(T^{-1})$ rate in the deterministic setting and an $O(T^{-1/2})$ rate in the stochastic setting when the LL approximation error decreases geometrically. Experiments demonstrate competitive performance of LeGo-BiO despite being agnostic to the LL objective.

papers.title: Local Pitch Angles of Galactic Structures in Nearby Galaxies with JWST: I. Spiral Arms and Interarm Substructures in Disk-Dominated Systems
papers.abstract: We present a spatially resolved study of spiral arms and feather substructures in seven nearby galaxies observed with JWST. Using eight images per galaxy, from four NIRCam and four MIRI filters, we combine a two-dimensional Fourier transform (2D-FT) with a circular-window correlation method to measure both global and local pitch angles. The 2D-FT identifies the dominant azimuthal mode and the corresponding $p_{\rm max}$, allowing us to reconstruct the spiral pattern and define arm and interarm masks. We then apply cosine filters with different pitch angles and window sizes in the $(\ln (R),\theta)$ plane to map the pitch-angle distribution across multiple spatial scales. NIRCam images provide the most robust measurements of the main spiral pattern, whereas MIRI data reveal dusty interarm features, particularly feathers, with greater contrast at the smallest window size ($D_w=0.25$). Across the sample, the main arms typically have $|\alpha|\simeq15^\circ$--$30^\circ$, while feathers show systematically larger values, often above $50^\circ$. These results demonstrate that pitch angle is scale dependent and that different structural components within the same galaxy can occupy distinct angular regimes. NIRCam and MIRI therefore offer complementary views of spiral structure, with the former tracing the large-scale stellar backbone and the latter exposing finer dust substructures. Together with the companion study of barred galaxies, this work provides a common framework for using local pitch angles to investigate distinct dynamical environments in nearby galaxies.

papers.title: Turing Instability of a Closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus Model
A panchromatic photometric and spectroscopic modeling of SN1987A from 200 to 800d
papers.abstract: Type II supernovae (SNe) at 1-3yr after explosion can document not only the preSN mass loss history of massive stars but also the chemistry of the inner ejecta rich in metals and eventually molecules and dust. With the aim of modeling SN1987A, we present a grid of radiative-transfer models of Type II SNe at Zsun/3, covering an initial mass range between 11 and 21Msun, a fixed ejecta kinetic energy of 1.2e51erg, and ~0.08Msun of 56Ni. The influence of metallicity at such late times is found to be relatively weak. In this model set, the [OI]6330A flux at 1-2yr varies non-monotonically with Minit. It first rises with Minit due to the growing O abundance but drops for M>17-19Msun due to the higher ejecta density, with little change to the rest of the optical spectrum. Assuming CO molecules account for 90% of the cooling in the C/O shell leads to a 10-20% reduction in the [OI] flux, equivalent to an O(1Msun) reduction in Minit at M<19Msun. The fractional [OI] flux rises from 200 to ~600d but decreases beyond. We obtain a good agreement to SN1987A for all Minit apart from [OI], which appears in the optical as the only discriminant between models. The 13Msun model yields the best match, from UV to IR, but a higher Minit may result with allowance for strong CO and SiO cooling. Past 500d, a growing amount of dust below ~2000km/s is essential to account for the ~1.5mag optical excess fading relative to predictions from decay power. Adopting 0.1mic silicate grains, we find a dust mass of 1e-4Msun at 600d rising to a few 1e-3Msun at 700-800d. We also found that the 200-800d International Ultraviolet Explorer spectra of SN1987A are all contaminated by a background hot star, which also causes the relative UV brightening past 500d. Such contamination may complicate the interpretation of more distant SNe II at >~2yr once or if they fade to O(1e5Lsun) [abridged].

papers.title: Multi-GPU MoE Inference with Adaptive Expert Offloading
papers.abstract: Modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference is constrained by GPU memory. This constraint is mitigated by expert offloading, which stores part of the model's weight in host memory and executes on demand. Though MoE architecture has computation sparsity, more GPUs are needed for serving increasingly larger frontier models. However, existing expert offloading systems overlook this need and fail to scale performance with additional GPUs. We present AdaOffload, a general and efficient multi-GPU hybrid expert execution framework that effectively handles heterogeneous hardware and workloads. We co-design GPU-CPU parallelism and GPU-CPU co-execution for decode and prefill with online workload observation that adapts to different hardware, workload, and batch size heterogeneity. We evaluated AdaOffload on five different platforms with varying GPU capability (L4, Pro6000, B200), number of GPUs, CPU capability, and NUMA topology on three different frontier open-weight models (284B to 753B). AdaOffload achieves $1.9\times$ to $15.5\times$ throughput speedups across different models over state-of-the-art systems.

papers.title: $B\to$ invisible decays as probes of light new physics
papers.abstract: Rare $B$ decays with missing energy probe heavy particles contributing to $b\to s\nu\bar\nu$ and new light states produced on shell. We discuss both possibilities in light of the Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+\Emiss$. Fits to the missing-mass distribution favour a two-body contribution near $2.1\,\GeV$, while scalar and fermion pairs of masses around $0.4$-$0.6\,\GeV$ remain viable alternatives. Extracting their couplings would profit from additional measurements, including the $B\to K^*\Emiss$ rate and longitudinal $K^*$ polarization, together with invisible $B_s$ decays which constrain scalar-pair interactions. We discuss how an aligned Higgsed $U(1)'$ model can realize the single-vector explanation through a vector-like top partner. Loop-induced electroweak mixing makes visible $Z'$ decays unavoidable, requiring an additional invisible channel to evade dimuon searches. We show that a light dark fermion can provide this channel and also account for the observed dark matter abundance through resonant thermal annihilation.

papers.title: Rethinking How to Leverage Cheap Physics for Data-Efficient Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Neural operators learn mappings from PDE inputs, such as initial conditions and coefficient fields, to the corresponding solutions. Once trained, they can rapidly predict solutions for new inputs. However, obtaining input-solution pairs for supervised training often requires expensive numerical simulations, whereas PDE inputs and governing equations provide inexpensive physical information. This raises a question: how can cheap physical information reduce the need for labeled solutions? A natural approach is to use physics to select inputs for labeling, but our acquisition experiments show no consistent advantage over random sampling. This observation motivates exploring an alternative: using cheap physics to improve neural operator initialization before supervised training. We propose Physics-Informed Initialization (PI-Init), a simple yet effective method that pretrains neural operators on unlabeled inputs using physics-informed losses and retains the learned parameters for supervised fine-tuning on the labeled dataset. A linearized analysis shows that pretraining can improve downstream prediction accuracy by reducing initialization errors that limited labeled data cannot effectively correct. Experiments across diverse PDE benchmarks and neural operator architectures demonstrate improvements in predictive accuracy, out-of-distribution generalization, and label efficiency. Representative results show error reductions of up to 62.7% at the same label budget and comparable or better accuracy with 90% fewer labels, relative to supervised-only training.

papers.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
Randomized Greedy MIS Is Fast at Every Node of a Tree
papers.abstract: The Randomized Greedy MIS (RGMIS) algorithm computes a maximal independent set (MIS) by processing the vertices in a uniformly random order and greedily adding each vertex to the independent set whenever possible. Despite its simplicity, this algorithm has proved effective in a range of parallel, distributed, and dynamic settings. For sufficiently small maximum degree, Nguyen and Onak (FOCS~'08) and Yoshida, Yamamoto, and Ito (STOC~'09) showed that a recursive simulation of RGMIS can be used to estimate the sizes of matching and vertex cover in sublinear time. The key subroutine in their approach is the following local query procedure: given a vertex $v$, to determine whether $v$ belongs to the MIS, recursively evaluate the neighbors of $v$ that precede $v$ in the random order. If any such neighbor is found to belong to the MIS, the procedure immediately concludes that $v$ is not in the MIS; otherwise, it concludes that $v$ is in the MIS. For graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$, Nguyen and Onak showed that, in expectation over the random ordering, this procedure makes $O(\exp(\Delta))$ recursive calls from a worst-case starting vertex. No better upper bound is known even for trees. We prove that on trees, from \textit{any} starting vertex, this recursive RGMIS procedure makes $\mathrm{poly}(\Delta)$ recursive calls in expectation.

papers.title: Control of Linear Dynamical Systems with Operational Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper presents a method for designing servo-controllers that enforce operational constraints on multi-input multi-output linear time-invariant dynamical systems. The proposed method introduces a control augmentation that complements a baseline controller to ensure forward invariance of state/output trajectories within prescribed box constraints. The derivations of the control design are based on the Nagumo Theorem, the Comparison Lemma, and principles from min-norm optimal control akin to the theory of Control Barrier Functions. Importantly, an explicit piecewise-linear feedback control law is derived, which provides continuous enforcement of constraints without online optimization, enabling rigorous stability and robustness analysis via classical linear systems theory. Extensions to handle estimation errors in output feedback and integral action in proportional-integral control are provided. Theoretical results are validated through flight control simulation studies that demonstrate input/output constraint satisfaction, robustness to disturbances, and closed-loop stability. The proposed method offers a mathematically rigorous, practical, and analyzable alternative to common heuristic or optimization-intensive constrained control strategies.

papers.title: Density Matrix Renormalization Group Method for Core-excited Electronic States
papers.abstract: We present the formulation and implementation of the Core-Valence Separation (CVS) approximation within the Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) framework for the simulation of core-level X-ray spectra. Two symmetry implementations are developed and assessed, identifying a scheme that preserves spin symmetry and remains applicable to multiple core orbitals. Benchmark calculations for BeH$_2$ and [Fe(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{2+}$ demonstrate excellent agreement with conventional multi-configurational methods for excitation energies and spectral intensities, while enabling substantially larger active spaces. Using quantum information theory measures, we show that the CVS constraint suppresses core-occupation fluctuations without significantly altering core--valence entanglement, providing a diagnostic for its applicability. Furthermore, we introduce a reference-free second-order perturbative correction that systematically reduces errors introduced by the CVS approximation. Finally, a generalized multi-core formulation enables the simultaneous treatment of excitations from different core shells. These developments establish CVS-DMRG as an accurate and computationally efficient approach to core-level spectroscopy of strongly correlated systems.

papers.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee
papers.abstract: In recent years, singular-spectrum-based optimizers have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to preserve the matrix structure of neural network gradients, thereby enabling geometry-aware optimization. However, most singular-spectrum-based (SSB) approaches remain centralized, limiting their use in distributed learning infrastructures that exploit massive parallelism. Distributed SSB optimization is still at an early stage, with open questions about convergence guarantees and communication efficiency. To fill this gap, we propose the Distributed Momentum-based Spectral Estimator (DisMUSE), an efficient distributed SSB optimization framework for both data-center and federated settings. Using Muon-style exact orthogonalized momentum as the spectral update, DisMUSE integrates a recursive variance-reduced momentum estimator and achieves an $O((KT)^{-1/3})$ convergence rate, where $K$ and $T$ denote the number of nodes and local iterations per node, respectively. This rate matches the best-known rates for variance-reduced nonconvex distributed optimization. Building on this variance-reduced framework, we study two extensions. First, our DisMUSE method with finite Newton-Schulz (NS) iterations preserves the same convergence order under a uniform normalized support-spectrum condition, up to a multiplicative factor. Second, we develop a communication-efficient variant based on low-rank (LR) momentum transmission and quantify the error it introduces to the stationarity bound, characterizing the trade-off between accuracy and communication cost.

papers.title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part II: The Nonlinear Construction
Laplace approximation of the parameter posterior with embedded error for efficient uncertainty quantification of expensive model calibrations
papers.abstract: In practical engineering, there is a clear need for uncertainty quantification (UQ) of models used in design because forward UQ puts probabilities on performance predictions. However, without surrogate building, most forward engineering models are too expensive for traditional UQ methods like Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our goal is to provide inexpensive, approxi- mate UQ that can be applied after an expensive traditional least squares fit, where the UQ handles both uncorrelated noise and parameter variance as in the embedded-error treatment developed by Sargsyan, Najm, and Ghanem (2015). After developing the basic theory to connect a Laplace-like approximation to Bayesian calibration, we compare the proposed method to black-box variational inference in terms of cost and fidelity. Then we demonstrate the method on real-world calibration of solid material models.

papers.title: Compact Greek Language Models from Scratch: Pretraining 500M- and 1B-Parameter Decoder-Only Transformers
papers.abstract: We present two compact decoder-only language models trained from scratch exclusively on Greek text: LexisLM-1B (1.09B parameters) and LexisLM-500M (502M parameters). Both use a dedicated 32k byte-level BPE tokenizer and a 22B-token pretraining corpus drawn primarily from Greek Wikipedia and FineWeb2. Both models complete the 22B-token schedule, with best held-out perplexities of 9.77 for LexisLM-1B and 11.31 for LexisLM-500M. Evaluation of both models on Greek-translated ARC, MMLU, and TruthfulQA shows above-chance performance on ARC-Easy, while ARC-Challenge and MMLU remain near chance. We also perform supervised fine-tuning of both models on Greek instruction data, primarily EuroAlpaca, reaching held-out instruction perplexities of 7.12 for LexisLM-500M and 6.37 for LexisLM-1B. The report describes the tokenizer, data preparation, training, and evaluation methods, providing a foundation for further work on compact Greek language models.

papers.title: Reaching separated flow states by release and recapture with learned latent feedback
papers.abstract: Targeting a prescribed flow configuration rather than an aerodynamic coefficient is challenging because the desired state may lie outside the natural attractor. We demonstrate cluster-based control in a learned vorticity representation for two-dimensional flow over a NACA0015 airfoil at $Re=500$ and $\alpha=15^\circ$, using a localized streamwise momentum source near the leading edge. An actuation-enriched ensemble is compressed with a variational autoencoder and partitioned into macrostates. We optimize a continuous feedback law interpolating macrostate-dependent amplitudes without an explicit latent dynamical model. For an attached target, the optimized law approaches constant forcing, arrests vortex shedding and maintains the attached state. For a strongly separated target, the law instead establishes attachment, withdraws actuation so that the natural separation transient carries the flow through the target, and restores forcing to recapture attachment. Over the evaluation horizon, the closed-loop trajectory revisits the target approximately every three shedding periods. Companion open-loop calculations isolate the arrest, release and recapture processes.

papers.title: Synaptic Dendritic Neuron Model (scDNM) for Cell Type Classification in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data
papers.abstract: Cell type classification in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, and transcriptionally similar cell types. We developed scDNM, an adaptation of the dendritic neuron model incorporating learnable synaptic thresholds, a supervised gene pool, staged training, and ensemble prediction. Six binary classification tasks were constructed from the Paul15, PBMC3k, and Nestorowa datasets. All models were evaluated using leakage-free nested cross-validation, with feature selection, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning performed independently of the outer test folds. scDNM ranked first in three of six tasks (including one tie) and achieved the best mean accuracy rank (2.00), followed by XGBoost (2.75), Random Forest (3.33), logistic regression (3.33), and SVM (3.58). In a six-class PBMC3k experiment, scDNM achieved 95.997% accuracy and 0.944 macro-F1, compared with 94.243% and 0.914 for SingleR. Garnett returned only Unknown labels and was treated as a zero-coverage technical outcome. Ablation analysis supported the contributions of dendrites and synaptic thresholds. However, XGBoost achieved higher mean binary-task accuracy (96.20% versus 95.32% for scDNM), and across-task rank differences were not statistically significant. These findings demonstrate that scDNM is competitive for scRNA-seq cell type classification, although broader independent validation is required.

papers.title: Symplectic Reck: In-Situ Learning of Gaussian Quantum Operations
papers.abstract: Programmable photonic circuits are a natural platform for physical learning, where hardware parameters are trained directly from measured feedback. We propose a physical learning algorithm and architecture for continuous-variable quantum systems where a photonic circuit is trained in situ to invert an unknown lossless Gaussian quantum operation. We prove that a generic symplectic matrix $S\in\mathrm{Sp}(2N,\mathbb{R})$ admits a decomposition into a triangular array of two-mode symplectic gates on neighboring modes, followed by single-mode symplectic gates. We then introduce the symplectic Reck mesh, which physically realizes this factorization, generalizing the unitary Reck mesh widely used in optical neural networks. When placed after an unknown Gaussian unitary, the mesh is trained in situ by nulling local response blocks one at a time using optical probes and measurements. We identify a local condition number that quantifies the squeezing required for a nulling step and its sensitivity to measurement error. We numerically demonstrate finite-shot training and robustness to systematic gate-calibration errors. Our work extends self-configuring optical networks from unitary to symplectic transformations, bringing physical learning to continuous-variable quantum photonic hardware.

papers.title: Linear Convergence of Nesterov's Acceleration for All Momentum Parameter
Real Intermediate States in Dark Matter Freeze-In from First Principles: Single Mediator
papers.abstract: We investigate the treatment of real intermediate states (RIS) in freeze-in production of $s$-channel Dark Matter (DM) with unstable mediators, as such models feature a double-counting issue when decay and annihilation collision terms are simply added within the semi-classical Boltzmann approach and a finite width is used for the regularization of the resonance. While several ad-hoc RIS-subtraction schemes are available to mitigate this problem, a first-principles treatment in this context is so far missing. We therefore start from the Closed-Time-Path (CTP) formulation of non-equilibrium Quantum Field Theory and present a CTP-based description of $s$-channel freeze-in pair production of a single scalar, fermion or vector DM species. In addition to being intrinsically free of non-unitary overcounting, the CTP ansatz also has the advantage of systematically capturing thermal corrections known to be important for DM freeze-in. Separate evolution equations assuming a single scalar or vector mediator in thermal equilibrium with the surrounding bath are presented. The exact propagators of the unstable mediators are approximated by resumming one particle irreducible (1PI) self-energy diagrams generated by bath particles and are evaluated with their full mass and momentum dependence in contrast to the commonly adopted Hard Thermal Loop limit. The CTP relic densities are compared numerically with those obtained using the most common RIS-subtraction schemes for two example $s$-channel freeze-in models, demonstrating the phenomenological relevance of a consistent RIS treatment.

papers.title: Large-D approach to nearly critical holographic matter and Yang-Mills deconfinement
papers.abstract: We study a systematic expansion of dynamical black hole solutions in a class of five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton theories that are holographically dual to nearly critical, strongly coupled four-dimensional field theories. The expansion is motivated, through dimensional reduction, by the large-D limit of pure gravity, where D is the number of spacetime dimensions. At leading nontrivial order, the Einstein equations reduce to a closed set of non-relativistic hydrodynamic equations in four dimensions, as first shown in our previous letter; these equations generalize the large-D effective theory of black branes. We derive the thermodynamics and hydrodynamics of the system from black hole thermodynamics and the holographic dictionary, and show that the energy-momentum tensor extracted from the near-boundary geometry is conserved precisely when the effective equations hold. We analyze planar, cylindrical, and spherical domain walls between coexisting phases, as well as non-equilibrium steady-state walls with nonzero momentum flux. We also show how the near-horizon geometry can be completed by a holographic flow to an asymptotically AdS5 region. Finally, as an application to the confinement-deconfinement transition of Yang-Mills theory, we construct the domain wall between the confined and deconfined phases in improved holographic QCD, compute its surface tension, and compare it with recent lattice results.

papers.title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that transformer architectures trained with discrete denoising diffusion and decoded via guided test-time beam search can learn to recover the prime factors of semiprime integers directly from data. Our approach establishes a new frontier for learning-based semiprime factorization, successfully factoring 68-bit integers-a substantial advance over the prior 56-bit state of the art. While computationally less efficient than classical factoring algorithms, our model requires no domain-specific number-theoretic priors and learns purely from training examples. In practice, the diffusion model acts as a generative prior, identifying promising factor candidates where exact verification or lattice-based post-processing can complete the factorization. Furthermore, we derive empirical scaling laws relating approximation quality to training data volume, model size, and test-time computation. In contrast to language, problem size is the key driver of scaling behavior. Achieving a fixed accuracy on a held-out test set requires compute that scales exponentially with bit length. Consequently, our findings pose no threat to security, as the projected compute cost required to factorize cryptographically relevant integers remains prohibitive.

papers.title: New Astronomical, Meteorological and Geological Study of the "Torre Spaccata District" - VII district of the Municipality of Rome
papers.abstract: This study, part of the NGICS (New Italian City Geological Study) project, analyzes 25 years of multi-disciplinary data to assess long-term environmental, climatic, and geological trends in Torrespaccata, an urban district within Rome's Seventh Municipality (VII Administrative District). Specifically, it investigates the temporal evolution of Heating Degree Days (HDD) by comparing the historical stationary climate period (1961-1989) with the recent multidecadal interval (1990-2014). Statistical analysis reveals a clear climatic transition: while the pre-1989 period showed a stationary trend (m = -1.14 HDD/year), the modern era exhibits a sharp decline in heating demand, characterized by a negative trend of -11.52 HDD/year (R2 = 0.511). This significant reduction of 80.14 HDD between the two periods is robustly validated via Welch's t-test (t = 3.045, p = 0.0039). Concurrently, interannual variability increased by 29.8%, driven by the synergistic feedback between global warming and the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. Furthermore, the correlation between climatic anomalies and local geological events is evaluated using robust statistical imputation to mitigate uncertainties caused by data gaps. These findings provide critical insights into long-term anthropic and natural changes within the urban ecosystem.

papers.title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
RigidGS: Geometry-Aware Object Decoupling for Rigid-Body Interaction in 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Interactive VR/MR applications demand photorealistic 3D representations that support real-time rendering and object-level manipulation. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves high rendering quality, it represents scenes as unstructured, monolithic primitives. Existing object-aware 3DGS methods jointly optimize geometry and semantic states but suffer from two key failure modes: noisy foundation-model masks on complex geometry, and label-geometry coupling, in which co-optimized identity gradients mislabel boundary Gaussians. We introduce RigidGS, an end-to-end pipeline that decouples geometric learning from object identity. We propose a depth- and temporally-aware mask refinement module that addresses two complementary SAM2 failures: over-inclusion on thin structures and under-inclusion on multimodal-depth objects. We then determine object identities entirely upstream via COLMAP projection voting and freeze them during training, directing mask supervision solely toward geometric optimization. Refined masks alone substantially improve competing methods, yet a residual gap in label-geometry coupling persists that our fixed-identity design eliminates. RigidGS outperforms prior object-aware 3DGS methods on LLFF/NVOS, Mip-NeRF~360, and iNeRF360, improving segmentation and boundary IoU by 7.7 and 14.5 points on LLFF/NVOS. Finally, RigidGS enables real-time rigid-body manipulation on Meta Quest~2 without mesh extraction. Our code and project page are available at this https URL .

papers.title: BO-Arena: An Evolving Benchmark for High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimisation
papers.abstract: High-dimensional Bayesian optimisation (HDBO) is an increasingly crowded field with new methods proposed at every major conference, making it ever harder to answer a deceptively simple question: "Which method is currently state-of-the-art?" In this paper, we question the efficacy of benchmarking practices in the field, and find them to be systematically ineffective: multiple published works fail to benchmark against the strongest available baselines, or even include incorrect implementations of key methods. Without a shared reference implementation, such errors are difficult to detect during peer review. We therefore introduce BO-Arena, an actively maintained and extensible package providing canonical implementations of state-of-the-art algorithms, which allows researchers to develop new methods and benchmark them rigorously. Using BO-Arena, we find that what currently drives performance in HDBO is even simpler than previously thought. We use these insights to propose a new algorithm which is competitive with the state of the art on problems with many observations, without resorting to the complex GP approximations used in recent methods. Finally, we question whether there is currently sufficient evidence that any more complex method outperforms a simple Gaussian process baseline for HDBO.

papers.title: Physics-Based Differentiable Beamforming for Deep Learning-Based Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound is widely used for vascular imaging because it is non-invasive, real-time, and cost-effective. However, its spatial resolution remains limited by diffraction to an order of the acoustic wavelength. This limitation is particularly restrictive for imaging of the microvasculature and high-resolution vector-flow-imaging. In this work, we present a multi-channel physics-based deep learning approach to super-resolve monodisperse microbubbles directly from multi-channel radio-frequency (RF) data. We also present a novel image-based metric for model evaluation. The proposed pipeline combines a learnable deconvolution network with a differentiable beamforming layer, enabling a direct deconvolution of the microbubble (MB) signature prior to image formation. By operating on multi-channel RF data, the method aims to improve localization robustness in the presence of dense microbubble populations and deconvolve the lateral direction in a relatively low-frequency regime (1.7 MHz) where MBs exhibit nonlinear behavior. The model is trained and evaluated on simulated data using monodisperse lipid-coated MBs over a broad range of acoustic pressures and microbubble densities. The proposed method improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the single-channel approach. It achieves sub-wavelength axial and lateral resolution while slightly improving robustness to dense microbubble populations outside the training domain. It also demonstrates generalizability across transmit configurations without requiring explicit training on each transmit configuration.

papers.title: Questions of minimality for DDMOGs and cycle ornaments
Two-Timescale Receive Combining for Fronthaul-Constrained Uplink XL-MIMO with Visibility Regions
papers.abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) arrays are hard to deploy in virtualized radio access networks, because the fronthaul data rate grows with the number of antennas when the radio unit forwards every antenna sample. We propose a two-timescale receiver that allocates the per-user combining ranks under the fronthaul stream budget from the channel statistics. The radio unit applies the long-timescale transform, after which the distributed unit applies a minimum mean-squared-error receiver in the reduced dimension. For disjoint visibility regions, we prove that the reduced-dimension receiver decouples across users. We characterize the sum-rate loss to second order and show that the greedy allocation, which we call saturating capture, minimizes its leading term. In simulations, the allocation gains over a uniform-rank baseline, matches a budget-trimmed threshold rule at a small number of users and exceeds it as the array and the user count grow. The gain grows with the heterogeneity of the per-user eigenvalue profiles and vanishes for identical profiles. Under out-of-cell interference offset by at least half a window width, the gain survives with clean covariances, which window-restricted estimation keeps for disjoint windows.

papers.title: Test beam results for machine-learning-based reconstruction of resistive silicon sensors
papers.abstract: The advent of Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs) and AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) as candidate technologies for four-dimensional tracking has moved part of the reconstruction burden onto the analog waveforms of the sensor, in which the charge shared between electrodes encodes the impact position well below the electrode pitch. Recovering that position is a continuous, non-linear inverse problem. Transient Current Technique measurements characterize this problem at fixed injected charge and high signal-to-noise, whereas a minimum-ionizing beam adds Landau fluctuations in the deposited charge under detector operating conditions. We report test beam results for full-waveform reconstruction of an AC-LGAD of 500 $\mu$m pitch read out on a $2\times2$ pad matrix, exposed to the 120 GeV pion beam of the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and read out alongside a six-plane MIMOSA-26 telescope. The telescope is aligned, and its per-plane resolutions are calibrated in situ, giving a track pointing resolution of about 2.5 $\mu$m per axis at the device, so that the measured residual is the sensor response rather than a convolution with the reference. We then compare two analytic estimators, the parameter-free charge-imbalance formula and a fitted linear matrix inversion, with the topology-agnostic transformer developed for resistive silicon sensors. Over the full active pad, the transformer reaches a median total position with up to factor 3 improvement. Within the charge-sharing core, the three methods converge to the floor of this sensor at the achieved signal-to-noise.

papers.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. Conventional routing selects one model per prompt, while fixed ensembles cannot adapt their composition and cost to individual requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing. At the core of both methods, PISA combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities. Building on these estimates, PISA-E jointly selects ensemble composition and cardinality under an explicit cost--quality preference that can be adjusted at inference time without retraining. A tractable ensemble-success surrogate and efficient candidate selection enable this extension without ensemble-specific training. Across four LLM routing benchmarks under in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions, PISA achieves the highest macro-average cost--performance hypervolume among the evaluated single-model routers in both settings. Meanwhile, PISA-E achieves the highest macro-average task performance among the evaluated ensemble approaches when prioritizing response quality, surpassing the strongest competitors by 2.09 and 2.87 percentage points under ID and OOD conditions, respectively. At selected lower-cost operating points, it also exceeds the strongest ensemble competitors' macro-average task performance while reducing average inference cost by approximately 36% and 25%, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of prompt-adaptive capability estimation for both single-model routing and selective ensembling.

papers.title: Lightweight Neural Prediction for MDCT-Based Perceptual Audio Coding
papers.abstract: Perceptual audio codecs often use predictive coding to further reduce signal redundancy. Rather than learning the entire codec pipeline end-to-end, we insert a small neural network as a drop-in, deterministic predictor in an otherwise conventional codec: the network estimates the next Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) coefficient block from a short context of reconstructed blocks, and the encoder transmits the quantized residual. We compare Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictors against a non-predictive baseline and a per-line Normalized Least Mean Squares (NLMS) linear predictor (similar to the MPEG-2 AAC Main Profile predictor). The CNN consistently outperforms the MLP, the linear predictor, and the baseline in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), noise-to-mask ratio (NMR), and MUSHRA evaluation scores. Using a 512-sample analysis window (w = 512), our neural predictors recover, and the CNN exceeds, the coded quality obtained by the non-predictive baseline after quadrupling the analysis-window length to w = 2048, at substantially lower algorithmic delay. The CNN uses only 0.13M parameters (roughly 20x fewer than the MLP) and has a decoder real-time factor (RTF) of ~0.10 on a consumer CPU.

papers.title: Strong Connectivity Oracle for Multiple Failures via Rooted Flow-Augmentation
papers.abstract: We present a significantly improved $k$-fault-tolerant strong connectivity oracle, one of the most basic data structures on a directed graph $G$ that, given any set $F$ of failed edges of size $|F|\le k$, answers whether $G \setminus F$ is strongly connected. For every constant $k$, our oracle only uses $n^{1+o(1)}$ space and $n^{o(1)}$ query time. No prior result can achieve $o(n^{2})$ space and $o(n)$ query time, \emph{even when $k=2$}. Previous oracles either require $\Omega(n)$ query time [BCR18], or $\Omega(n^2)$ space [vdBS19]. Our main technical contribution is a \emph{rooted} version of the highly successful flow augmentation technique, which may be of independent interest. Given a directed graph $G$, an integer $k$, and a source vertex $s$, we can sample a set of edges $A$ such that each minimal $s$-rooted cut of size at most $k$ becomes an $s$-rooted min-cut in $G + A$ with probability $2^{-poly(k)}n^{-o(1)}$.

papers.title: A Geometric Construction of the Radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam Processes
Flexible Edge Cover: A Disjunctive Programming driven Approximation
papers.abstract: We introduce the flexible edge cover problem, denoted FLEX-EDGE-COVER: the input here is an undirected graph with non-negative edge costs along with a partition of the edges into safe and unsafe edges, non-negative integers $p$ and $q$, and the goal is to find a minimum cost subset of edges such that each vertex has either at least $p$ safe edges incident to it or at least $p+q$ total edges incident to it. We show that FLEX-EDGE-COVER is APX-hard in simple bipartite graphs. A greedy approach leads to a $2$-approximation in all graphs. We show that the $2$-factor can be improved in simple graphs via a novel disjunctive programming-based LP formulation. AI-tools were used in the analysis of our rounding algorithm. Our motivation for introducing and investigating FLEX-EDGE-COVER is its close connection to the Flexible Graph Connectivity problem (denoted $(p,q)$-FGC) which has garnered much recent attention. For $(p,q)$-FGC, we develop a tighter LP-formulation via the disjunctive programming approach. We hope that our disjunctive-programming based LP and rounding algorithms for FLEX-EDGE-COVER will serve as a starting point towards a constant factor approximation for $(p,q)$-FGC.

papers.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach
papers.abstract: Stochastic bilevel optimization provides a general framework for many machine learning applications, such as hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic reinforcement learning. However, most existing bilevel optimization methods treat matrix-valued gradients as flattened vectors and perform optimization in the resulting vectorized space, ignoring the matrix structures common in modern neural networks. Moreover, the lower-level (LL) problem curvature can induce significant spectral imbalance in the upper-level (UL) geometry. Such limitations of existing bilevel optimization methods motivate us to develop BiMuon, a geometry-aware stochastic bilevel optimization method that integrates implicit hypergradient estimation in bilevel optimization with Muon-style orthogonalized updates at the UL. To our knowledge, BiMuon is the first stochastic BLO method with Muon-style orthogonalized matrix updates and an $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ iteration-complexity guarantee, matching the best-known rates achieved by Muon-type methods based on matrix parameterizations. To improve computational and parallel efficiency for models with multiple matrix parameters, we further study BiMuon for blockwise diagonal matrix approximation and derive a relative stepsize allocation rule based on UL progress and blockwise LL sensitivity. We evaluate BiMuon on representation learning and blockwise bilevel optimization, providing empirical support for our methods.

papers.title: Fast Accurate Quantum Monte Carlo without Metropolis Adjustment
papers.abstract: In quantum systems, physical quantities of interest can be expressed as expectation values of a probability distribution, which allows their estimation by Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. This approach, an instance of Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), plays a central role in obtaining predictions of system properties relevant to condensed matter and high energy physics. The use of Hamiltonian dynamics to design a Markov kernel, known as Hybrid or Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), is widespread in quantum applications. In this context, it is standard to use an HMC kernel that is ``adjusted'' with the Metropolis-Hastings (MH) criterion, so that estimates of expectations converge to their true value in the limit of infinite sample size. However, recent work in computational statistics suggests that an \emph{unadjusted} HMC kernel can be significantly more efficient, while safely maintaining an asymptotic bias which is small relative to the error arising from the variance of the finite sample size. We adapt this approach to the QMC setting, focusing on a challenging and high-dimensional \emph{spin-fermion} model of a quantum phase transition. We find that unadjusted methods outperform adjusted HMC in terms of effective sample size per gradient call, while retaining accurate results.

papers.title: Projected Neural Additive Models as Universal Approximators
papers.abstract: Neural additive models (NAMs) offer interpretability but lack expressivity due to their rigid additive structure, whereas multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) achieve universal approximation at the cost of transparency. We establish the first theoretical foundation for projected neural additive models (PNAMs), which augment NAMs with a learnable linear transformation $\boldsymbol{T}$ to capture cross-variable interactions. While standard NAMs cannot approximate even the simplest interaction term $\chi_1 \chi_2$ because their cross-derivatives are identically zero, we prove that PNAMs are universal approximators and characterize the minimum number of projections required for exact polynomial representation. Furthermore, we derive an approximation rate of $\mathcal{O}(M^{-s / (N - 1)})$ for $\mathcal{C}^s$ functions (i.e., functions with $s$ continuous derivatives), where $M$ denotes the number of projections and $N$ the input dimension; this rate is known to be optimal for ridge function approximation. To recover interpretability from the projected inputs, we introduce structured sparsity regularizers and post-hoc symbolic regression techniques that enable global input ranking, parameter pruning, and the conversion of learned bases into compact analytical expressions. Experiments on knot theory invariants, MNIST, and phase field fracture mechanics demonstrate that PNAMs match or surpass similar architectures in accuracy while discovering salient features and yielding symbolic models with orders of magnitude fewer parameters.

papers.title: GSynPEF: A Privacy Evaluation Framework for Synthetic Graphs
papers.abstract: It is often desirable to generate and release synthetic graphs, which resemble real-world data, in a privacy-preserving way. While substantial progress has been made in designing private graph synthesizers (PGS), opportunities remain for more explicit connections between synthesizer models and privacy evaluation, and better accounting for output variation. This paper proposes GSynPEF, a practical framework for empirical evaluation of privacy and utility in settings for which a real-world graph is given as input and output synthetic graph(s) are observed. Our framework links a broad class of graph synthesizers (both statistical and deep-learning based) with privacy metrics, expanding evaluation dimensions to practical utility and risk, through empirical analysis of multiple actual outputs. The framework accommodates both an Exact Solution scenario, where synthesizer behavior is directly observable, and a Monte Carlo Approximation scenario where only synthetic outputs from a black box synthesizer are available. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets and seven widely used graph synthesizers demonstrate framework's versatility, enabling privacy evaluation for different attack goals (e.g., to infer an edge or node) and capabilities (e.g., observing one or multiple synthetic graphs). We analyze evaluation results by examining the relationship between graph statistics and synthesizer design choices, providing insights for data curators in PGS selection and researchers for improved PGS design.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Correlation Clustering with Vertex Updates in Polylogarithmic Update Time
papers.abstract: We present a fully dynamic algorithm for correlation clustering that supports \emph{vertex} insertions and deletions while maintaining an $O(1)$ approximation in polylogarithmic amortized update time. This resolves an open problem of vertex deletions posed by a recent line of work on dynamic correlation clustering. We adopt the min-disagreement objective for correlation clustering, i.e., given a signed complete graph $G=(V,E^+\cup E^-)$, we want to minimize the total number of $(+)$ edge crossing clusters and $(-)$ edges within clusters. The input is given in the adjacency list model, where each update inserts or deletes a node along with its full set of $(+)$ neighbors. Our main technical contribution is a fault-tolerant sparse-dense decomposition framework which unlike the existing decomposition-based frameworks allows for structural inconsistencies as long as the induced cost is bounded. We also show a separation between explicitly maintaining the (stronger) sparse-dense decomposition and maintaining a constant-factor approximation to correlation clustering, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Current-voltage characteristics of layered cuprate superconductors with intrinsic Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: A brief review of the results for the current-voltage characteristics study in highly anisotropic cuprate superconductors is presented, considering the existence of the intrinsic Josephson effect in multilayer HTSC compounds. We analyzed the observations of multi-branch current-voltage characteristics for current in the c-direction both for the hole-doped and electron-doped cuprate SCs wich conveniently viewed as a strack of intrinsic Josephson junctions, where the CuO2 layers serve as superconducting plates and the buffer layers as dielectric interlayers. It was shown that the tunneling characteristics of intrinsic Josephson junctions in optimally doped p- and n-type cuprates indicate a predominantly d-wave symmetry of the order parameter, demonstrating high conductivity in the subgap regime: U < 2delta/e. The analysis carried out confirms the theoretically predicted power-law dependences U ~ I^gamma with gamma = (0.33 - 0.50) in the hole-doped Bi- and Tl-compounds, which is typical for SCs with monotonic dx^2-y^2 - wave symmetry of the order parameter and with gamma = (0.70 - 0.76) for electron-doped SCs with a non-monotonic d-wave symmetry within the framework of the two-band/two-gap model.

papers.title: ATLAS: A Multi-Procedure Benchmark and Context-Aware Model for Surgical Anatomy Segmentation
authors: Ronald L. P. D. de Jong
papers.abstract: Recognizing anatomical structures during minimally invasive surgery (MIS) could support intraoperative navigation and improve patient safety, but progress is limited by small, single-procedure datasets and by segmentation methods developed for natural scenes. This work addresses both limitations through a new dataset and model. First, we introduce ATLAS-120k, a clip-level semantic segmentation dataset of 121,018 annotated frames from 100 surgical videos, covering 14 laparoscopic and robot-assisted procedures and 41 classes. Annotations were created with a pipeline that combines manual labeling, tracker-based propagation, and review by surgeons. Second, we propose ATLAS (Anatomy Recognition with Context Learning using Foundation Representations), a video semantic segmentation model for surgical anatomy recognition. ATLAS builds on in-domain foundation-model embeddings and adds context queries for the procedure and surgical phase, together with query propagation between frames for short-term memory. ATLAS outperforms state-of-the-art natural-image and in-domain foundation models in both segmentation accuracy and temporal consistency, achieving a Dice score of 0.70 with ViT-L while running in real time at 76.2 FPS. Ablations show that the context queries improve accuracy and that query propagation improves temporal consistency. ATLAS also generalizes well, matching a dedicated model zero-shot on CholecSeg8k and improving phase recognition on AutoLaparo over SurgeNet initialization. The model weights, dataset annotations, and annotation tool are publicly available at this https URL .

papers.title: A Note on the Hardness of Partially Dynamic Max Flow
papers.abstract: We study the fine-grained complexity of partially dynamic max flow in capacitated graphs. Assuming the combinatorial 4-clique hypothesis, combinatorial algorithms require $\Omega(n^{2-o(1)})$ amortized update time. Thus, recomputing max flow after each update is optimal up to subpolynomial factors for combinatorial algorithms in dense graphs. The previous conditional lower bound was $\Omega(n^{1-o(1)})$ amortized update time under SETH or the OMv hypothesis and applies to all algorithms [Dah16].

papers.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability. Privacy constraints and instance-level reporting hinder the collection of diverse abnormal cases and frame-level labels, while repeated retraining for new centers increases computational cost. We introduce EvoDiff, a generative active learning framework that integrates diffusion modelling with information-theoretic objectives, evolutionary search, and curriculum-based sampling to select informative samples across heterogeneous US datasets. EvoDiff formulates sample selection as a generate-to-retrieve process, in which diffusion-based optimization in feature space guided by information gain produces synthetic probes, and only the real unlabeled samples retrieved by these probes are annotated and used for downstream training. Across six benchmarks covering fifteen datasets and 16,696 images, we evaluate EvoDiff on convolutional network and transformer-based foundation model. EvoDiff approaches fully supervised performance with substantially fewer labels, outperforms active learning baselines, and improves foundation model generalization under cross-domain external validation on unseen cohorts. A reader study with six radiologists indicates the potential to support clinical annotation workflows, with a model-based estimated 24% to 84% reduction in annotation workload at matched downstream performance.

papers.title: Open-Source Multi-Fidelity EMT Modeling of Data Center Loads for Power System Studies
papers.abstract: Characterizing data center-grid interactions under rapid load fluctuations requires electromagnetic transient (EMT) models that capture fast converter and control dynamics. This paper develops a modular multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD. The modular design supports flexible assembly of subsystem models for different power supply configurations. The multi-fidelity design incorporates switching models, average-converter models, and reduced-order models to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency according to analysis needs. The model also provides a systematic controller tuning procedure and supports control mode switching. Comparative simulations demonstrate how this data center load model responds to both grid-side and load-side disturbances and assess the accuracy and computational efficiency of models with three fidelity levels. The model is publicly available on GitHub.

papers.title: The Storage View Of KV Cache: Characterizing Cache Behavior Across LLM Workloads
papers.abstract: Modern LLM serving increasingly extends KV caches beyond GPU memory into host DRAM, SSDs, and remote storage, yet these stores remain largely governed by workload-agnostic policies such as LRU and fixed TTLs. We ask what execution context is needed by storage to make retention, reclamation, and placement decisions across heterogeneous workloads. We characterize KV-cache reuse, lifetime, and footprint at block granularity across 11 production and public traces spanning chat, API serving, RAG, coding agents, tool-using agents, and multi-lineage workflows. We examine reuse sources, recurrence timing and frequency, useful lifetimes, and storage consumption. Across workloads, KV state takes two recurring forms. Single-session state is reused within one execution: its footprint grows as sessions deepen and accumulates across concurrent sessions; it can remain useful through long idle periods but loses value at session completion. Multi-session state recurs across sessions of the same workload, outlives individual sessions, and spans hot prefixes and a large infrequent tail. While prior systems often exploit application-, agent-, or workflow-specific knowledge, our results suggest that three generic signals (a workload identifier, a session identifier, and session completion) expose much of the structure needed for KV-storage management. Trace-driven comparisons show that workload-specific recurrence estimates retain up to 22% more within-session hits and reduce dead state by up to 40%; a session completion signal eliminates the fundamental idle-time reclamation tradeoff for single-session state; and session-aware reuse classification identifies shared state 4-700x more selectively than request-level access counts. These results motivate a small cross-layer interface for workload-aware KV storage without application-specific semantics.

papers.title: Optimizing one-dimensional lithographically defined nanowires in semiconducting heterostructures
papers.abstract: One-dimensional nanowires can host remarkable electronic properties and are central to studying quantum transport. Although heterostructure-defined confinement combined with gate-defined potentials can greatly reduce the effects of impurities as measured via electron mobilities, the realization and interpretation of novel effects at this scale are complicated by disorder. Experiments on lithographically defined one-dimensional nanowires therefore do not exhibit ideal behavior. Using theoretical and computational models, we predict that optimizing the geometry of split gates in semiconducting heterostructures will lead to higher-quality channels for transport measurements. Further, we show that this optimization is essential for resolving features of interest such as the Rashba-induced spin gap. This new approach to lithographically defined conduction channels provides better energy resolution and is less susceptible to disorder.

papers.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
papers.abstract: Today's LLM-based agents are vulnerable to deception by users and other agents. Defending against deception requires Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning to infer the beliefs and goals of others as well as modeling tactics based on communication theory. To enable training models to detect deception, we adopt the well-known deception game, Avalon. We present a corpus, AVCORP, of 5,000 annotated utterances from 250 games of Avalon. AVCORP includes (1) 37 tactics mapped to a 4x4 behavior matrix, and (2) reasoning traces capturing abductive hypotheses, suspicion levels, and nested ToM beliefs. We train Qwen3-8B on AVCORP and evaluate it on 25 held-out games and 20 games played by humans. On held-out games, our best trained detector outperforms its untrained baseline and frontier models (GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Pro), matching Claude Opus 5.5. On human games, every trained detector exceeds the untrained model in F1 score across all rounds.

papers.title: ASCENT: Scale-Complementary External State for Frozen Long-Context Language Models
papers.abstract: External state should become more valuable as a reader becomes more capable, yet long-context evaluations measure memory utility at a single model scale. This paper formulates scale complementarity: the absolute gain from external state increases when reader capacity and a compact state budget are jointly scaled. ASCENT realizes this principle with a target-blind causal writer, nested typed state, and a bounded query-conditioned readout; every language model remains frozen. Under log loss, the value of a nested refinement equals its target-relevant conditional information; a full factorial makes the reader-by-state interaction identifiable. Official 16K BABILong experiments show Qwen2.5 accuracy gains of 10.50, 78.88, and 82.63 percentage points at 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3B parameters, with both adjacent directional contrasts significant after family-wise correction. At 7B, Foundation accuracy rises to 33.25% while four-slot ASCENT answers every question, which caps the gain at 66.75 points; the 3B-to-7B accuracy increment is -15.88 points [-20.55, -11.20]. The accuracy-side claim is therefore established from 0.5B to 3B; the 7B conclusion rests on the non-saturated negative-log-likelihood factorial. A three-model by three-state factorial yields co-scaled negative log-likelihood gains of 0.388, 2.099, and 7.406 nats at 1.5B, 3B, and 7B; all interaction and gain contrasts retain positive simultaneous lower bounds. Five public 7B-8B readers obtain 66.75-85.63 point gains, and ASCENT exceeds task-trained retrieval checkpoints at the two larger shared scales. Controls, baselines, systems accounting, matched-hardware reproduction, and a cross-architecture sensitivity analysis accompany the experiments. The results establish scale-complementary external state under the evaluated benchmarks, metrics, and state schema.

papers.title: CXR-CMFA: A Cross-Modal Feature Aggregation Network for Chest X-Ray Pathology Classification
papers.abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) interpretation remains challenging because subtle pathology can be obscured by overlapping anatomy, image-quality variation, and limited visual evidence in isolated radiographs. Although image-only deep learning models provide useful baselines, they discard the complementary diagnostic context available in radiology reports, while large vision-language models can be computationally expensive for practical deployment. This paper presents CXR-CMFA, a lightweight cross-modal feature aggregation network for binary CXR pathology classification. The proposed framework combines a dual-stream visual encoder, using EfficientNet-B0 for global anatomical representation and DenseNet-121 for local pathological detail, with a TF-IDF-MLP report encoder. Two fusion modules integrate these modalities: the Dual-Modal Spatial Attention Module (DMSAM) uses the report embedding to gate global and local visual features, and the Cross-Modal Gated Feature Fusion (CGFF) module learns per-instance weights for visual and textual contributions. Experiments on the MIMIC-CXR benchmark, using the provided train, validation, and test splits, show that CXR-CMFA achieves 93.45% accuracy, 99.88% precision, 91.8% recall, 95.7% F1-score, and 99.19% AUC on the held-out test set. The model produces only four false positives among 984 normal test cases, supporting its suitability for high-specificity screening workflows. An ablation study further demonstrates a 22.47 percentage-point AUC improvement over the global-image-only variant, confirming the value of adaptive cross-modal fusion. These results indicate that compact report-conditioned fusion can provide strong discriminative performance without relying on large pretrained language models.

papers.title: Hidden memory above the Neel temperature programs antiferromagnetic order in Cr2O3
papers.abstract: Control of antiferromagnetic order is central to magnetoelectric and antiferromagnetic spintronic devices. In the prototypical magnetoelectric antiferromagnet Cr2O3, domains are conventionally selected by simultaneous application of electric and magnetic fields during cooling through the Neel temperature (T_N) or at a fixed temperature below T_N. Here, we show that antiferromagnetic order can instead be programmed by electric-field conditioning entirely in the paramagnetic state above T_N. By measuring the magnetoelectric coefficient (alpha_zz) of bulk Cr2O3 crystals under different thermal and field histories, we find that a sufficiently large electric field above T_N establishes a reversible state that persists after the field is removed. Subsequent magnetic-field cooling with no applied electric field produces a single-domain state with the opposite Neel-vector orientation from conventional magnetoelectric field cooling. The electrically induced state can be reversibly written, erased, and allowed to relax at high temperatures, demonstrating a long-lived internal electric bias that governs domain selection. The observed behavior is consistent with a metastable surface-associated polar state that may generate this internal bias. These results reveal an unexpected coupling between electrically programmed memory and antiferromagnetic domain formation in Cr2O3.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
How light interacts with matter, revisited
papers.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. From this single picture we obtain the blue of the sky and the white of the clouds, transparency and the refractive index, the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem, reflection and the colours of thin films, why metals reflect and what gives metals and semiconductors their colours, polarizers, Brewster's angle and birefringence, the working of mirrors, lenses, microscopes and the eye, the propagation of a few-cycle pulse through a slab, Cherenkov radiation, amplification and second-harmonic generation. Feynman's arrows are made quantitative with the sheet method, and coupled-dipole simulations show the incident wave being cancelled and replaced inside the medium. The connection with quantum theory is discussed where the classical picture stops: the photon, spontaneous emission and the forbidden lines of the aurora, vision and photosynthesis, and the sum over paths. The text is addressed to undergraduate students and their teachers, and to any reader curious about the physics behind everyday optical phenomena; derivations are collected in separate panels, and the animations and the Python codes used for the figures and simulations are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Where Did the Evidence Go? Diagnosing Proof-Set Loss in Long-Term Conversational Memory
papers.abstract: Long-term conversational question answering can require several separated dialogue turns that support an answer only together. We introduce EviCover, a retrieval approach designed to retain this complementary evidence. It converts questions into observable evidence requirements, checks requirement coverage using retrieved source identifiers, and selects turns jointly. We track annotated support sets - the benchmark-labeled dialogue turns associated with each question - through retrieval, reranking, and final answer-generation context. We evaluate the baseline memory pipeline on generated, human-verified LoCoMo conversations and human-written REALTALK conversations, and examine EviCover on REALTALK's 108 multi-hop questions. Compared with the hybrid lexical/dense baseline, support-turn recall among 60 candidate turns rises from 0.526 to 0.575, and recall in the final ten-turn context rises from 0.349 to 0.379. The evidence funnel identifies separate discovery and selection failures, while paired answer evaluation shows that greater evidence recall does not yet establish a correctness gain. This analysis locates where complementary evidence is lost and distinguishes evidence retrieval from its use in answer generation.

papers.title: Capturability-Aware Footstep Planning in Cluttered Environments: A Recursively Feasible Sequential MPC on Axis-Aligned Safe Corridors
papers.abstract: A fundamental aspect of humanoid footstep planning is to jointly guarantee obstacle avoidance and locomotion stability. This paper presents a capturability-aware sequential Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for Linear Inverted Pendulum (LIP)-based humanoid footstep planning in the presence of obstacles. The proposed method combines obstacle avoidance with capturability constraints through safe corridors constructed as sequences of intersecting rectangles, yielding a sequential MPC framework with recursive feasibility guarantees for the LIP-based planning layer. The planner autonomously adapts to constrained scenarios, switching to in-place walking when obstructions---such as doors assumed to be open during planning but unexpectedly found to be closed during execution---block forward motion. Performance is largely independent of the prediction horizon, allowing high success rates while keeping the computational cost low. The approach is validated in high-fidelity simulations with the humanoid robot Digit, demonstrating a practical solution for capturable humanoid footstep planning in cluttered environments.

papers.title: Key Institutional Considerations for Designing Effective Independent Verification Organizations
papers.abstract: Independent verification organizations (IVOs) have emerged as a popular, bipartisan solution for facilitating high-quality independent evaluations of AI technologies. But momentum is outpacing design: there is emerging consensus on the necessary operating conditions for robust IVOs, but little discourse on institutional and policy specifications to ensure those conditions are met. IVOs are currently envisioned primarily as a mechanism operating at the AI frontier and model level to evaluate catastrophic risks. Little work has yet been done on how to establish or enforce an IVO ecosystem that is equipped to handle myriad risks (i.e., beyond catastrophic ones) and operate at the system and application level across the deployment and use stages of the AI lifecycle. This paper argues that IVO design should ensure the capacity for evaluating AI models, systems, and applications in context for both frontier companies and enterprise companies & AI-adopting organizations. Additionally, this paper provides early considerations to advance IVO discourse from normative to operative, and from existential to everyday risks. Drawing from existing institutional constructs in financial services, education, public health, and science, we outline key considerations on whom IVOs serve, what access they require, how they interact with external governing structures, how they are funded, and how they fit into the wider assurance ecosystem. Much of the structure and knowledge necessary to holistically design IVOs and their ecosystem does not yet exist, even as companies rush to ink agreements with their chosen evaluators.

papers.title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
Pion and kaon electromagnetic form factors in a flavor-dressed contact interaction: the role of Nf-screening on dynamical chiral symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: We compute the electromagnetic form factors of the pion and the kaon in a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose effective coupling depends on the number of active light flavors Nf , so that dynamical chiral symmetry breaking is screened as Nf grows toward the chiral transition. The calculation uses the rainbow-ladder truncation of the Schwinger-Dyson and Bethe-Salpeter equations with proper-time regularization, and it includes the dressed quark-photon vertex obtained from its own inhomogeneous Bethe-Salpeter equation in the same truncation. At Nf = 2 the model reproduces the established contact interaction values of the meson masses, decay constants and condensates, and the charge radii rpi = 0.447 fm and rK = 0.417 fm, which undershoot experiment by about one third, as is known for this class of interactions. We therefore restrict every comparison to Q2 less then or equal to 0.6 GeV2, confront it with the NA7 data and with one-loop chiral perturbation theory, and focus on the response to Nf . Both radii grow monotonically with Nf , and the growth survives every variation of the screening function and of the infrared confinement scale that we test. The growth is carried by the quark core rather than by the vector-meson dressing: between Nf = 2 and 6 the bare-vertex contribution to <r2pi> rises from 0.097 to 0.226 fm2, while the dressing contribution moves from 0.102 to 0.127 fm2 even though the rho pole drops from 0.93 to 0.70 GeV. The finite strange mass slows the kaon response only moderately.

papers.title: AutoEMatic: Runtime-Adaptive Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Automatic Exponent-Mantissa Refinement
papers.abstract: Existing LLM post-training quantization techniques determine precision before inference begins, yet the precision a model requires varies dynamically across prompts, layers, and inference phases. We present AutoEMatic, a full-stack co-design that adapts the precision of weights, activations, and the KV cache at runtime. A lightweight policy selects each layer's precision at every prefill and decode step from two runtime signals: the entropy of the next-token distribution and the magnitude of each layer's update to its hidden states. This runtime adaptation is made practical by AutoFP, a multi-scale floating-point format that derives 2-, 4-, and 6-bit precisions from a single NVFP4 base format. We realize AutoEMatic on two targets: GPU kernels that execute AutoFP on NVFP4 Tensor Cores, and an accelerator whose vector MAC datapath executes all AutoFP formats natively. Across reasoning and agentic benchmarks, AutoEMatic improves accuracy by up to 21.7% over NVFP4 and matches group-scaled FP6 accuracy on most benchmarks, using 4.9 bits per weight versus 4.5 for NVFP4. On GB300 GPUs, AutoEMatic retains approximately 90-98% of NVFP4 decode throughput across the evaluated configurations. Furthermore, the AutoEMatic accelerator reduces latency by 1.6-2.3x and energy by 7-23% compared to an accelerator with NVFP4-only datapath at iso-accuracy.

papers.title: Probing deformed nuclei: Experimental insights into excited states of $^{152,153,154}$Gd isotopes through fusion-evaporation reactions
papers.abstract: The rare-earth region has been the focus of various studies aiming at the understanding of nuclear structure and providing information on the details of the reaction mechanism. The Gd isotopes belong to this group of nuclei and despite the available spectroscopic information, several open questions about their structure still exist, such as the inter-band transitions related to shape evolution or branching-ratios in deformed states. In addition, production cross sections of different reactions to Gd isotopes are largely unknown. In this work, we report on an experimental attempt to populate the excited states in the isotopes $^{152,153,154}$Gd by employing the heavy-ion fusion reaction $^{18}$O+$^{138}$Ba $\rightarrow$ $^{156-x}$Gd + $xn$ in the 58-64 MeV energy range (center-of-mass). The experiment was conducted at the 9 MV FV Pelletron Tandem at the Horia Hulubei National Institute for Physics and Nuclear Engineering, employing the ROSPHERE array.
