Because the correction term of $F_q$ is affine, $F_q$-regularization at strength $\gamma$ is Tsallis regularization at temperature $\gamma/q$. Over the reals, chip-firing connects all configurations of equal degree, so the Jacobian enters transport only through integrality. We introduce the transport defect, the worst-case cost of steering $d$ chips towards a target by chip-firing, and prove $1/d\le\delta_{\TV}(D)\le(d-r(D))/d=(g-1-r(K-D))/d\le\min(1,g/d)$ whenever $g\ge1$; vertex multiplicities give a lower bound and an equality criterion. A regularized topological gap $\Gamma_{q,\gamma}(D,E)$ tends to the chip-move defect as $\gamma\to0$, lies in an explicit window, has a high-temperature slope given by Tsallis coupling entropies, and admits a positive regime if and only if $g\ge1$. Dual potentials certify exactly the convex relaxation of a linear system; the remainder is an integrality gap. Zeros in optimal plans occur only for $q>1$, by a mechanism different from the sign change of $\Gamma$. Exact computations on $1784$ divisor classes find the rank bound $(d-r(D))/d$ attained in $1769$ of them, an observed frequency. Experiments on honeycomb and Erdős--Rényi networks with $10^2$ to $10^5$ nodes test the statements on regularized plans, not $\Gamma$; over $10^3\le n\le10^5$ their transport costs are consistent with growth like $n^{1/2}$ and $\log n$, respectively.

papers.title: Persistent A-homotopy of Complex Networks
papers.abstract: We study how loop classes in a network change when cycles up to a prescribed length are declared contractible. The resulting sequence of quotient groups contains the fundamental group of the clique complex at length three and the graph $A$-fundamental group at length four. Its mod-two abelianisation has a barcode whose death scales are the lengths in a minimum cycle basis. This separates the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations and provides a computable connection between persistent $A$-homotopy and persistent homology. We illustrate the construction on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks and nine benchmark networks. Filling the plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the fundamental group of the torus. In the Watts--Strogatz simulations, the normalised largest death scale falls below the normalised mean path length over the sampled range, while most clique-homology classes survive the square relations at small rewiring probabilities. The power grid has fewer surviving classes but a longer tail of death scales than five degree-preserving randomisations. We also examine connectivity graphs of maximal cliques in ego networks. Explicit certificates establish non-trivial $A$-classes even though the original ego clique complexes are contractible. The group construction and its linear summary answer related but distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permit.

papers.title: A Positively Curved Seven-Manifold Without Effective Smooth Circle Actions
On the multivariate hypergeometric function $F_K^{(L)}$, I
How Many Demonstrations Does a VLA Need? On the Sample Efficiency of VLA Finetuning
papers.abstract: Pretrained vision language action (VLA) models show strong zero-shot performance, but are rarely deployed directly and are often first post-trained on demonstrations from the target setting. Yet VLAs are typically compared by zero-shot or full-data fine-tuned success, revealing little about the data and compute required for adaptation. We study adaptation efficiency for six VLAs ($\pi_{0}$, $\pi_{0.5}$, and GR00T N1-N1.7) on four LIBERO suites, varying both demonstrations and training steps. This reveals differences hidden by full-data fine-tuning: models within two points on the full LIBERO-Spatial dataset differ by up to $3\times$ in success with 50 demonstrations. $\pi_{0.5}$ needs $2$--$5\times$ fewer demonstrations than $\pi_{0}$ and is the most sample-efficient model at every budget, with the largest gap on the long-horizon suite. Within GR00T, N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6 and N1.7 on three of four suites, despite their stronger zero-shot performance. We study one pretraining factor behind these differences by freezing the VLM during finetuning: this severely degrades the $\pi$ models, whose VLM is jointly trained with the action expert during pretraining, but barely affects GR00T models. Finally, validation loss on held-out demonstrations tracks closed-loop success within a suite, but understates how much more sample-efficient $\pi_{0.5}$ is than $\pi_{0}$.

papers.title: Strong unique continuation on Riemannian manifolds for degenerate elliptic operators with convexified weights
Local Aronson-Bénilan estimates for the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on collapsing manifolds
A liquid implant that grows into a stable scaffold in situ
papers.abstract: Endovascular embolization requires materials that can pass through narrow microcatheters yet form stable, conformal occlusions within irregular vascular lesions, but reconciling these competing requirements remains challenging. Here we report a wirelessly activated liquid precursor whose final architecture is constructed only after target localization. A gallium-based liquid metal containing iron microparticles and gas microcavities remains deformable, magnetically navigable, and retrievable before activation. Wireless induction heating activates the internal reactive microenvironment, coupling gas-driven microcavity growth with oxidative mineralization of newly generated gallium interfaces to form a porous, self-supporting scaffold. In aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation models, activation enabled durable occlusion, aneurysm-neck healing, and six-month stability in a porcine aneurysm model. These findings establish post-delivery construction as a strategy for creating stable therapeutic implants from minimally invasive liquid precursors.

papers.title: SceneShifter: Training-free Multi-Scene Temporal Control for Audio-driven Human Animation
papers.abstract: Although audio-driven human animation has achieved impressive realism, it still lacks effective Multi-Scene Temporal Control: orchestrating background transitions at precise timestamps while preserving a coherent foreground subject. We show that this challenge stems from the diffusion transformer's self-attention mechanism, and addressing it requires two capabilities: (1) Semantic-Aware Temporal Decoupling, which isolates background attention across scenes while retaining cross-scene foreground attention for subject consistency; and (2) Foreground Motion Localization, which accurately tracks the foreground subject across latent frames, especially under large motion. To address these challenges, we introduce SceneShifter, a training-free framework for precise multi-scene control in audio-driven human animation. SceneShifter guides spatio-temporal self-attention by suppressing cross-scene attention among background tokens while preserving cross-scene attention among foreground tokens. To support this guidance under large motion, SceneShifter extracts dynamic foreground masks from the self-attention layers and heads that best capture subject trajectories. We further introduce SceneShifterBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate scene-timing accuracy, foreground preservation, and visual quality under large motion, multiple subjects. Experiments show that SceneShifter achieves frame-level scene timing, strong subject preservation, and high visual quality, outperforming existing baselines. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: A four-view smartphone video dataset of a robot-held flexible strip, with camera poses and a 3D LaGSplat baseline
papers.abstract: This note describes a multi-view video dataset of a deformable object driven by a measured input, with the measured pose of every camera, and a first 3D result obtained on it with LaGSplat. LaGSplat learns from video a low-dimensional latent state that is both the generalized coordinate of a learned dissipative Lagrangian and the conditioning variable of a Gaussian Splatting decoder; fitting the decoder in 3D calls for synchronized multi-view footage, which the original paper only had from synthetic renderings. Here a robot arm moves a flexible strip by oscillating along a one-dimensional path, and four iPhones, three fixed and one handheld, film it for ten minutes. The videos are synchronized, the cameras are posed from the scene, and the position of the gripper is given per frame as the input of the system. LaGSplat fitted on this data with the gripper acceleration as a forcing term renders held-out views at 26 to 33 dB PSNR and runs as a real-time interactive demo in a web browser. Dataset, checkpoints and training code are public.

papers.title: HippoMamba: A Mamba-augmented network for hippocampal segmentation and serial volumetry in Alzheimers disease
papers.abstract: Hippocampal atrophy is among the earliest structural markers of Alzheimer's disease, and reliable hippocampal segmentation across serial MRI visits is a prerequisite for measuring it. We present HippoMamba, a network that combines a 3D convolutional encoder and decoder with a Mamba selective state space block at the bottleneck, designed to process one or more MRI visits of a subject. On the Medical Segmentation Decathlon hippocampus dataset (260 subjects, five-fold cross-validation), HippoMamba obtained a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.8861 $\pm$ 0.0094, the highest among six convolutional and transformer-based methods trained with the same folds and patch size, and its per-subject Dice was significantly higher than that of each method (Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests, $p \leq 0.013$). Its mean 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (1.45 mm) and average surface distance (0.44 mm) were the lowest of the compared methods, although they did not differ significantly from those of Attention U-Net, and the Hausdorff distance did not differ significantly from that of SegResNet. Without retraining, the five-fold ensemble was applied to 600 T1-weighted sessions from 150 participants of the OASIS-3 cohort. In sessions meeting a registration quality criterion, predicted hippocampal volumes ranked consistently with FreeSurfer volumes (Pearson r = 0.778, 95% CI 0.699 to 0.838; ICC(3,1) = 0.772) but were systematically smaller by about 27%. In a pre-specified analysis of participants followed for at least two years, annualised volume change derived from per-visit segmentation was moderately correlated with that of FreeSurfer (r = 0.503, 95% CI 0.319 to 0.659), with a larger mean rate. These results support the use of HippoMamba for hippocampal segmentation and for ranking hippocampal volume within a cohort, with absolute volumes and rates of change interpreted relative to the reference method.

papers.title: HALMES: Knowing When to Intervene in LVLM Hallucination Mitigation
papers.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in multimodal tasks. Nevertheless, their outputs remain prone to object hallucinations that are inconsistent with visual content. Contrastive decoding, as a training-free inference-time mitigation approach, typically intervenes in the output distribution at every decoding step. However, such indiscriminate full-stage intervention may disrupt originally correct generations and even induce new hallucinations. To address this issue, we first analyze the relationship between internal attention features and hallucinated token segments in LVLMs, revealing that hallucination-related abnormalities already emerge progressively in preceding token segments. Based on this observation, we propose HALMES, a lightweight plug-and-play module that identifies hallucination precursor segments from attention features during generation and selectively triggers contrastive decoding. HALMES can be integrated with various full-stage contrastive decoding methods, transforming indiscriminate intervention into on-demand targeted correction. Extensive experiments across different LVLM architectures and multiple benchmarks show that HALMES further improves the hallucination mitigation performance of existing contrastive decoding methods while reducing the negative impact of full-stage intervention on normal outputs, validating the importance of modeling and selectively intervening on hallucination-prone segments.

papers.title: MAPA: Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation for Latent Dataset Distillation in 3D Medical Classification
papers.abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) synthesizes a small training set from a large one, but applying it to 3D medical classification is constrained by the memory and optimization costs of synthesizing full volumetric samples. Under a storage-equivalent budget, distilling in the latent space of a frozen autoencoder reduces this cost and fits more synthetic samples (prototypes) than in voxel space. However, class-level matching, such as distribution matching, causes prototypes to concentrate in dense latent regions while underrepresenting sparser intra-class regions, a consistent imbalance that we term prototype concentration. To address this, we propose MAPA (Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation), a latent distillation method that spreads prototypes across intra-class modes while preserving class-level matching. MAPA marks these modes with fixed anchors estimated by clustering the real latents and distributes prototypes over them through a soft assignment, together with a lightweight anti-collapse regularizer and curriculum weighting that stabilize the optimization. Across five 3D medical classification tasks, MAPA improves the aggregate balanced accuracy by +4.2 points over the strongest latent baseline while using the same number of prototypes. An exploratory severity analysis on MosMedData suggests improved worst-stratum recall without loss of normal-case specificity.

papers.title: RadAI: Gaze-Intention Fusion Pipeline for Attention-Guided Educational Videos in Chest X-Ray Interpretation
papers.abstract: Chest radiograph interpretation errors often arise from failures in visual search: although trainees may correctly identify an abnormality once pointed out, they frequently fail to fixate on the relevant region, while expert search strategies (where radiologists look, in what sequence, and for how long) remain largely implicit. Eye movement modeling examples (EMME), which replay a recorded expert's gaze over the image, have been shown to improve novice detection of findings on chest radiographs, but producing one requires an eye-tracking session on that specific case, so teaching sets are limited to recorded sessions by experts. In this work, RadAI is presented, the first end-to-end framework for transforming predicted radiologist gaze into narrated instructional videos, enabling scalable gaze-guided training without collecting new eye-tracking data. Given only a chest X-ray and its report, RadAI predicts an expert fixation sequence, associates each interval of that sequence with the diagnostic finding it pursues, extracts the corresponding image region, and renders the result as an EMME-style video in which each highlighted finding is narrated with synthesized speech. RadAI is evaluated on 97 cases from the EGD-CXR dataset, assessing whether the highlighted regions correspond to annotated abnormality locations. We position this work as a framework for scalable generation of educational content for residents and medical students in the field of radiology.

papers.title: DiffusedSplitFed: Latent Diffusion-based Obfuscation for Reconstruction-Resilient Split Federated Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL), Split Learning (SL), and Split Federated Learning (SplitFed) enable collaborative medical image analysis without sharing raw patient data. However, intermediate features and gradients exchanged during SplitFed training may reveal sensitive information through reconstruction attacks. To address this vulnerability, we propose \textbf{DiffusedSplitFed}, a SplitFed framework that integrates Latent Denoising Diffusion Models (LDDMs) at client--server split points to obfuscate transmitted representations while preserving segmentation performance. Three architectural variants (V1--V3) are developed using different combinations of dual conditioning and global feature fusion to investigate trade-offs among reconstruction resistance, segmentation accuracy, and computational complexity. Experiments on three medical imaging datasets (HAM10K, Blastocysts, and FHPsAOPMSB), supported by multiple independent runs and paired statistical analyses, demonstrate improved resistance to the evaluated image reconstruction attacks compared with Baseline SplitFed, while maintaining competitive segmentation performance. Comparisons with existing diffusion-based segmentation methods further demonstrate competitive segmentation accuracy under the evaluated settings. A conditional convergence analysis is also provided to characterize the effects of LDDM-induced gradient perturbations and local optimization on training. These findings highlight the potential of latent diffusion-based representation obfuscation for reconstruction-resilient collaborative medical image segmentation. The implementation is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Confusion-Adaptive Margin Learning for Handwritten Letter Recognition: A Controlled Study on EMNIST Letters
papers.abstract: Handwritten character recognition systems can achieve high accuracy while retaining concentrated errors among visually similar classes. Motivated by residual letter confusions in earlier geometry-based recognition work, we investigate whether these errors can be addressed through the training objective. We introduce Confusion-Adaptive Margin Learning (CAML), which constructs a sparse weighted confusion graph from a discovery partition held out from pilot training and applies pair-specific cosine-separation constraints during final training. CAML adds no classifier, routing rule, or inference-time parameters. We evaluate CAML on EMNIST Letters against a strictly matched cross-entropy CNN baseline, using the same architecture, final training data, deterministic augmentation, optimizer, and checkpoint selection. Eight confusion pairs are targeted: I/L, G/Q, U/V, R/V, D/O, C/E, I/J, and H/N. On the official clean test set, accuracy changes from 95.6346% to 95.6731%, and macro-F1 from 0.956326 to 0.956724. Mean accuracy across ten predefined corrupted conditions increases from approximately 95.3812% to 95.4303%; symmetric errors within targeted pairs decrease from 614 to 605 (1.47%). The global differences are small and not statistically reliable. CAML fixes 124 baseline errors but introduces 116 new errors on clean data (exact McNemar p=0.6515), and no corruption-specific difference remains significant after Holm correction. Thus, CAML does not establish global superiority, but shows that a leakage-controlled, pair-specific margin objective can alter targeted error structure with limited overall benefit for an already strong classifier.

papers.title: Hierarchical Design of Ambidirectional LCE Sheets for Three-State Gaussian Shape Morphs
papers.abstract: Modulation of surface curvature is a commonly exploited strategy to achieve adaptability within natural and synthetic systems where structure governs function. While Gaussian curvature of inextensible surfaces is fixed, surfaces made of extensible materials can adapts their Gaussian curvature under strain, unlocking capabilities such as locomotion, dynamic coloration, and tunable stiffness. This feature is commonly exploited to develop soft actuators capable of complex functionalities; however, traversing the entire spectrum of Gaussian curvature was previously difficult to achieve without the use of multi-material constructs or spatially varied stimulus fields. In this work, we present a strategy for generating a diverse range of dynamic Gaussian shape morphs using multiphase liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) as ambidirectionally deforming building blocks. Taking advantage of the materials sequential contraction and elongation during phase transitions, we design and investigate the deformation response of radially aligned flat LCE sheets which consecutively morph into negatively and positively curved flat surfaces in response to monotonically increasing temperature. We then investigate the influence of mesoscale asymmetry and macroscale geometry on curvature magnitude and bending symmetry, thereby demonstrating that a single form factor can be programmed to undergo a rich library of deformation behaviors. Finally, inspired by the strategy of cephalopods to couple mechanical deformability to dynamic optical properties, we fabricate a structurally colored LCE sheet which couples its dynamic Gaussian curvature to a dynamic color-changing response. This approach offers a route toward adaptive structures capable of multistate shape reconfiguration for applications in soft robotics, deployable systems, and responsive surfaces.

papers.title: Video-DCI: How Far Are VLM Agents from Human Viewers in Direct Video Corpus Interaction?
papers.abstract: Humans answer complex visual questions by inspecting short moments, updating what they know, and redirecting attention toward missing evidence. Existing video benchmarks, however, often provide the relevant video, evaluate only final answers or isolated localization, or permit textual shortcuts, leaving multi-round visual evidence seeking underexplored. We introduce Video-DCI, a diagnostic benchmark and functionally matched human-agent protocol for Direct Video-Corpus Interaction. It comprises DCI-Loc for temporal evidence localization and DCI-QA for end-to-end discovery, retention, and composition of cross-video evidence. In DCI-QA, videos within each pool are topically related, yet every answer requires hidden temporal evidence from multiple videos. Given only the question and video pool, humans and agents iteratively inspect bounded local windows, retain supporting evidence, and answer with cited temporal spans. Human trajectories provide reference curves for evidence acquisition and use across rounds. Experiments reveal a consistent retrieval-to-grounding gap. On DCI-Loc, frontier VLMs often retrieve and expose the reference moment, yet convert far less of this exposure into precise final citations than the human reference. On DCI-QA, the loss begins earlier and compounds across videos. Ablation studies further confirm that iterative search outperforms one-shot retrieval. Multi-round search is therefore necessary but insufficient: current agents accumulate candidates and observations more readily than precise, jointly sufficient evidence.

papers.title: Manufacturing Complex Structures Through Interfacial Self-Organization
papers.abstract: Conventional manufacturing constructs three-dimensional geometries through localized material deposition, removal, or shaping, with fabrication effort greatly increasing with geometric complexity. Here, we introduce a manufacturing approach in which target geometry is encoded into sparse wireframe scaffolds that guide liquid self-organization through interfacial forces. We apply a computational framework that approximates arbitrary target geometries using constant-mean-curvature surface domains and extracts their boundaries to construct the scaffolds. Under neutral buoyancy conditions, curable liquids injected into these scaffolds self-organize into the prescribed geometries, which are subsequently solidified into mechanically isotropic structures with optically smooth surfaces. We demonstrate the fabrication of complex anatomical models and topology-optimized structures featuring intricate branching geometries, internal cavities, and integrated materials. This approach opens new possibilities for scalable fabrication of complex geometric designs.

papers.title: Counting Events, Not Seeing Them: Diagnosing and Repairing the Readout Failure in Video LLMs
papers.abstract: Video LLMs fail conspicuously at counting how many times an object crosses the screen, a failure attributed to missing object permanence. Using construction-grounded synthetic testbeds with independently validated labels, we show this attribution is incomplete: the count signal is present but unread - linear probes decode per-window presence at 93% while global count decoding collapses to a duration confound. Concurrent work reports the same representation-output dissociation for repetition counting; we show that in exit-and-reappear event counting it is repairable: two readout-directed repairs (episode-localization supervision and a discrete event-symbol side channel) raise same-object counting from 46.7% to 65.0% (oracle 66.7%) on a chance-33% benchmark across 7B-30B systems. Transfer to an independent factory costs nothing, and an audit of the measurement apparatus exposes four data-integrity failures that had obscured the boundary. A real-video audit (REALCOUNT, n=18, blind-audited) shows the boundary persists - best 55.6% at chance 33.3% - and symbol transfer fails zero-shot. A 1-epoch in-domain adaptation bench is negative (six levers at 28-50%), but a 3-epoch schedule shows this is budget-limited for the symbol channel: with a 3-epoch schedule and sequence-disjoint oracle timelines the reader reaches 94.4% on REALCOUNT, and with the deployed detector's timelines a 2-epoch run reaches 72.2%. The residual gap is detector evidence and the reader's match to detector noise, not reader capacity: a frozen-feature boundary probe finds the signal weak (AUC 0.62 over a 0.51 permutation control) and non-transferring across clips (0.77 within-clip vs. 0.62 across windows).

papers.title: Rapid Antigen Detection Tests Empowered by Cholesteric Spherical Reflectors for Expanded Capabilities
papers.abstract: While Rapid Antigen Detection Tests (RADTs) have proved their value in point-of-care detection of respiratory diseases, their poor-contrast readout limits their use at early stages of infection where viral concentrations are low, and most RADTs test only for one disease, leaving a sick patient ignorant in case of a negative result. We explore the potential of Cholesteric Spherical Reflectors (CSRs) as enhanced optical labeling probes for RADTs, leveraging their circularly polarized reflections to maximize contrast by background subtraction and thereby lower the analyte concentration required for detection. Moreover, we demonstrate how the ease in tuning the CSR reflection color and the freedom to choose between right- and left-handed circularly polarized reflection allow us to design CSRs to distinguish optically between multiple diseases, eventually enabling RADTs capable of screening for a set of multiple diseases in a single test. We develop a method for functionalizing CSRs with appropriate antibodies and we propose a new type of RADT specifically designed for use with CSRs as detection label, demonstrating that the comparatively large size of CSRs (tens of microns in diameter) does not prevent viral analytes to tether them to an antibody-coated test surface. The strength of the optical CSR signal quantitatively reflects the antigen concentration.

papers.title: Interception Focusing of Colloid Transport in Granular Porous Media
authors: Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Sciences
papers.abstract: Colloid transport and retention in environmental granular porous media underlie groundwater resource protection from, and remediation using, biological and non-biological nano- and micro-particles (colloids). During transport, colloids periodically intercept grain surfaces and translate along them at separation distances across several tens of nm corresponding to the secondary minimum between the opposing forces of longer-range of van der Waals (VDW) attraction and shorter-range electric double layer (EDL) repulsion. Relatively weak diffusive translation of colloids supports their continued translation in secondary minimum association until they are expelled to bulk fluid at rear flow stagnation zones on grain leeward sides. We herein show that this dynamic focuses colloids into a network of fluid streamlines (incomplete mixing lamellae) that enhances their subsequent likelihood of interception with downgradient grains, i.e., increases the so-called collector efficiency (typically denoted by Greek letter eta). Interception focusing of colloids in granular porous media explains well-observed outcomes of colloid transport under environmental conditions, including nonmonotonic nonexponential profiles of retained colloids and the non-Markovian nature of extended tailing of low colloid concentrations following initial elution. Interception focusing is a fundamental process that distinguishes colloids from solutes and renders inapplicable to colloids the assumption that is often invoked for solutes of complete pore scale mixing in granular porous media.

papers.title: Two-dimensional liquid-like order in a confined population of swimming Eudorina colonies
papers.abstract: Swimming microorganisms accumulate at boundaries, but the spatial statistics of the resulting layers are rarely measured. We report a population of colonial green algae, of order 71 $\mu$m across, that accumulates against the rigid upper wall of a closed 1-2 mm chamber and holds a two-dimensional non-contacting arrangement for about 105 min. The pair correlation function has a first shell at $r/\bar{D} = 1.73$, $g = 4.8$; a hard-disc null at the same area fraction reaches only $g = 2.1$, so the ordering is not excluded volume alone. Nearest-neighbour separation is $1.80 \pm 0.13$ diameters. The bond-orientational order parameter is $\langle|\psi_6|\rangle = 0.456$ against 0.385 for the null, only 36% of interior colonies are six-coordinated, and the orientational correlation $g_6(r)$ decays over 1.5 diameters with $\eta_6 = 1.31$ against the hexatic bound of 1/4: the arrangement is a two-dimensional liquid, not a crystal or a hexatic. Colonies execute a persistent random walk with reorientation time 1.4-1.7 s at Reynolds number $\sim 9\times 10^{-4}$. Breakup begins at 127 min. Thermal convection is excluded on Rayleigh-number grounds. Caveats: the length calibration is nominal rather than metrological, and this is a single population observed once. All data and code are deposited.

papers.title: A Model Organism for Studying Unverbalized Evaluation Awareness
papers.abstract: Large language models can recognize when they are being evaluated and change their behavior accordingly, undermining the reliability of safety benchmarks. Evaluation awareness (EA) is usually measured by having an LLM judge scan reasoning traces for explicit statements of recognition, but this signal is increasingly unreliable. Recent frontier-model system cards report a drop in verbalized rates between releases, which is indistinguishable from awareness that has gone unverbalized. Interpretability methods could detect such unverbalized evaluation awareness (UEA) in individual interactions, but lack instance-level ground truth. Asking the model alters the input, and dataset labels do not reveal whether it recognized a particular prompt as an evaluation. We address this gap with a model organism. Using synthetic document fine-tuning, SFT, and DPO, we train Qwen3.5-27B to emit a marker (a designated token) in its final response when it recognizes an evaluation, while suppressing the marker and verbalized awareness in its reasoning. The marker largely tracks the evaluation concept as it can be strongly modulated by evaluation framing in the system prompt. When not told whether it is being evaluated, the organism recognizes evaluations from test-question cues, mirroring what its base model often verbalizes. Using the marker as a label, we benchmark linear probes, the Jacobian Lens, and Activation Oracles, built on the base model and blind to the marker. None recovers the label reliably. These results suggest that current interpretability methods are not yet reliable UEA detectors, even when recognition relies on simple cues. Our model organism offers a testbed for improving them.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning of formation energies and band gaps in hybrid perovskites through SHAP analysis and SISSO modelling
papers.abstract: Accurate and interpretable property prediction is essential for exploring hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. Here, we combine machine-learning screening with SHAP analysis and SISSO descriptor discovery. Using 4,456 compounds, optimized XGBoost models achieved test-set $R^2$ values of 0.99 for formation energy and 0.93 for band gap and were applied to over 180,000 candidates. Comparison across approximately 17,000 common compounds revealed broadly overlapping distributions from XGBoost and CGCNN but substantially lower predictions from UPET, suggesting potential limitations in its transferability to hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. SHAP analysis and correlation-based pruning retained eight primary features for each property, from which SISSO derived expressions comprising four nonlinear descriptors. These expressions couple molecular and inorganic properties for formation energy and emphasize relative atomic sizes and B-site characteristics for band gap. This framework supports efficient candidate prioritization and interpretable analysis of learned structures-property relationships in hybrid perovskites.

papers.title: Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays Derived from a U-Net Segmentation Model
papers.abstract: Pneumonia killed more than 740,000 children under the age of five in 2019, and it can be difficult to recognize on chest radiographs (CXRs): opacities may be faint in early disease, may sit behind the equally bright heart shadow, and may resemble other lung conditions. Most deep learning systems treat pneumonia detection as a yes-or-no classification task. This paper asks whether a model trained on a harder task, segmenting pneumonia pixel by pixel, can be turned into an effective detector for the simpler task of deciding whether an image contains pneumonia at all. The hypothesis is that the detailed supervision of segmentation forces the network to learn where and what the disease looks like, producing a better detector than training for detection alone. A U-Net was trained to segment pneumonia on the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge dataset of 26,684 radiographs, whose rectangular bounding boxes were converted into pixel masks. The data are heavily imbalanced: 22.5% of images are positive, and only 2.6% of pixels fall inside a box, so focal loss with {\alpha} = 0.25 and {\gamma} = 2 and dropout were needed for the model to learn. On the harder segmentation task, the model reached a pixel-level F1 score of 0.45 on a held-out test set of 2,668 images. Applied to the simpler detection task, the same model reached a precision of 0.71, recall of 0.52, and F1 score of 0.60, with 91% specificity, and consistent scores on the development set. These results show that a segmentation-trained model transfers to detection while also showing where the suspected disease is. A direct comparison with a classifier trained only for detection on the same data is needed to confirm whether the segmentation-first approach is better, and is the main direction for future work.

papers.title: MedToolFault and MedGuard: evaluating and improving clinical agent reliability
papers.abstract: Clinical agents must retrieve patient-specific evidence and correctly update records despite unreliable tool responses. We introduce MedToolFault, a fault-injection benchmark linking six tool-failure classes to answer correctness, required state changes and forbidden mutations in public clinical-agent tasks. We also introduce MedGuard, a tool-layer method that verifies read evidence and attributes ambiguous writes through public interfaces. Across 127,861 formal episode evaluations, we assess fault recovery, mechanism controls, task expansion, constrained tool budgets and external question answering. Across nine model configurations, unguarded agents fail in 32.2-67.8% of fault-injected evaluations on tasks each configuration solves without faults. MedGuard improves paired safe success by 13.7-46.6 percentage points on these tasks.

papers.title: Topic-Aware Multi-Task Mental Health Classification with Active Learning-Based Stepwise Relabeling for Social Media Conversations
papers.abstract: Mental health conditions affect millions of people worldwide, yet many cases go undetected until they reach a critical stage. Social media platforms like Reddit have become spaces where people openly share their experiences, but the support is often provided by individuals without clinical training. Existing multi-task approaches jointly model emotion and sentiment for mental health classification but frequently rely on noisy labels generated by pre-trained models and overlook topic information as a useful signal. This paper introduces two key contributions: First, an existing Core Fusion Network framework is extended by adding Topic alongside existing Mental Health Condition, Emotion, and Sentiment Classification tasks, with topic labels derived from the therapist-client interactions in the CounselChat dataset. Second, an Active Learning-based Stepwise Relabeling approach is proposed to refine a small subset of noisy emotion and topic labels using pre-trained models in two stages: targeting medium-uncertainty samples first, followed by high-uncertainty samples. The predictions above a confidence threshold (0.7) are accepted to prevent error propagation. The experiments are conducted on the SuicideWatch and Mental Health dataset of 54,412 Reddit posts collected from five mental health subreddits, evaluating domain-specific transformer encoders including MentalBERT and MentalRoBERTa. The proposed Active Learning-based Stepwise Relabeling, when applied to Core Fusion Network with MentalRoBERTa, improves Mental Health Condition by 0.09%, Emotion by 0.51%, Sentiment by 0.35%, and Topic Classification by 1.57% over the baseline Core Fusion Network. The results suggest that the proposed framework significantly reduces label noise in multi-task mental health classification, and that topic information provides additional context.

papers.title: An Alternative Proof of the SPR Synthesis Theorem for Polynomial Segments of Arbitrary Order
Rethinking Supervision Targets for Multimodal LLM Unlearning: Less Private Information, Reduced Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can memorize and reproduce sensitive information from their training data, posing significant privacy risks. Their ability to encode knowledge across both textual and visual modalities further complicates the selective removal of such private information. Many existing methods guide model unlearning by training the model toward constructed labels or output distributions, which we refer to as supervision targets. However, these methods often suffer from a trade-off between forgetting effectiveness and model utility. We identify supervision target limitations as a key factor in this trade-off and empirically show that targets containing more private information lead to insufficient forgetting, while larger distribution shifts from the original output distribution are associated with greater utility degradation. Motivated by these findings, we propose FFN-Perturbed Self-Distillation (FPD), which starts from the teacher's original output distribution as a zero-shift reference and selectively perturbs FFN activations associated with private information across textual and visual modalities. By precisely reducing private information from the teacher's original output distribution, FPD constructs supervision targets with less private information and reduced distribution shift. Extensive experiments on S-MLLMUn Bench demonstrate that FPD achieves a better forgetting-utility trade-off than existing methods.

papers.title: DramaGrow: A Regime-Aware Benchmark for Auditing LLM Judges of Multi-Episode Drama
papers.abstract: LLMs can now draft complete multi-episode dramas, and LLM judges are increasingly used to evaluate them. Assessing the reliability of these judges is difficult because drama quality encompasses specification-backed errors, reproducible preferences, and legitimate disagreement among human raters. Most existing evaluations reduce these cases to a single score from one judge call and leave tie calibration, call-to-call variation, and the vote margin underlying the human reference unreported. We introduce DramaGrow, a regime-aware benchmark and audit protocol for AI-generated Chinese five-episode drama. The benchmark assigns verifiable constraint violations, four-of-five preferences, and within-panel disagreements to separate denominators and evidence rules. It contains 800 episodes, 120 byte-preserving interventions, and 1,155 blinded five-rater records, including a frozen extension with 114 supermajority pairs and 21 disagreement pairs. On the frozen sets of 114 preference pairs and 35 constraint interventions, the repeated absolute-score rubrics yield overlapping performance, with mean accuracies of 53.8-55.8% and three-call agreement of 29.8-32.5%, and their accuracy falls from 71.6-71.9% to 34.8-37.1% as the tie band widens. DirectPair-GLM reaches 85.1% preference accuracy, 89.5% constraint F1, and 81.9% Detect+Locate on the same items, and exact subpanel enumeration identifies four-of-five as the smallest stable human vote margin. Evaluation protocol, tie calibration, judge-call variation, and panel margin therefore affect performance as much as rubric design. We will release the specification packages, scripts, interventions, anonymized human votes and rationales, frozen judge runs, and analysis code.

papers.title: Efficient Learning of Differentiable MPC Policies on the GPU via Smoothed ADMM and First-Order Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Differentiable model predictive control (MPC) enables structured, constraint-aware policies to be optimized end-to-end. However, learning MPC policies faces two bottlenecks: (1) nonsmooth sensitivities at active-set transitions and (2) expensive policy evaluation, since each requires an optimization solve. We first introduce SmoothedTurboMPC, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver combining sequential quadratic programming (SQP) with a log-barrier-smoothed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) inner solver. Its design enables smooth gradients, exact sensitivities at convergence, and efficient execution on GPUs. Second, to efficiently train MPC policies, we pair our solver with first-order reinforcement learning (FORL) using Short-Horizon Actor-Critic (SHAC), which reuses rollout MPC solutions instead of repeatedly re-evaluating them. Comparisons with state of the art solvers show that the approach achieves up to $4.4\times$ higher end-to-end training throughput. On a vehicle racing task, our method achieves higher returns than MPC PPO with a $46\times$ speedup, training on 3.3 million transitions in only 7 minutes. Finally, we use the framework to train a more reliable MPC racing policy via RL with domain randomization, and validate it on a full-scale race car. We integrate our advances into the open-source TurboMPC solver.

papers.title: How Many Examples, and Which Ones? A Study of In-Context Learning for Natural Language Inference
papers.abstract: Natural language inference (NLI) is a fundamental task of natural language processing and crucial for evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of AI methods. Research has mostly focused on encoder or encoder-decoder architectures. However, the field of decoder-only Large Language Models (LLMs) remains underexplored. While prior work has mainly investigated complex sampling and prompting techniques, the effectiveness of a minimalistic prompting approach is yet to be examined in decoder-only LLMs. In this work, we examine and provide a comprehensive benchmark of LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and Phi 4) in this domain, across the MNLI, QNLI and SciTail datasets. The performance of these models was evaluated using zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies with simple and direct prompts. The results of the article indicate that LLMs generally perform exceptionally well when they are provided with a simple, straightforward prompt, challenging the notion that complex prompting techniques are always required for NLI tasks. Additionally, we find that the choice of demonstration label in one-shot prompting significantly affects performance for most models, with entailment-primed examples performing best. Our findings also show that the use of a few representative examples, in the case of few-shot, produced performance comparable or superior to prompts with higher example counts, although the efficacy of the prompting techniques is model and dataset-dependent. Moreover, our simple prompting approach consistently matched or outperformed more elaborate methods such as ICS and MCQ-based prompting.

papers.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
papers.abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. Furthermore, we develop Kullback-Leibler-aware AoInt Synchronization (KL-AoIntSync), which accumulates output-distribution changes using client-specific unlabeled probes, whereas Parameter-aware AoInt Synchronization (Param-AoIntSync) uses a server-broadcast scalar parameter change. Then, we establish pathwise guarantees with fixed client distributions, action sets, and utilities. The numerical results show that calibrated Param-AoIntSync reduces joint synchronization cost by 6.15% relative to an Instant-Parameters policy while performing comparably to KL-AoIntSync.

papers.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?
papers.abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents get actively adopted for autonomous research, they must not only reason over existing evidence, but also design informative experiments, allocate resources, analyze sequential observations, and decide when to stop and make conclusions. Yet these capabilities remain poorly measured. We introduce Causal-Discovery-Bench ( this https URL ), a verifiable sandbox with configurable structural equation models and resource constraints to evaluate sequential experimental design and causal discovery without domain-semantic cues. Across 3,802 episodes with 13 models from 5 vendors, we analyze agent behavior along 40 metrics in seven families. Agents' performance exhibits a four-level difficulty hierarchy spanning single-experiment design, sequential exploration of causal relationships, resource-aware experimentation balancing cost and statistical power, and autonomous resolution of conflicting evidence. We identify a substantial performance gap between causal inference from correctly curated evidence and navigating causal discovery through autonomous experimentation: Analyzing agents' action trajectories attributes 94.5% of their mistakes to experimental design rather than to inference, which is further consolidated with ablation studies. Relaxing resource constraints alone does not reliably resolve failures in sequential discovery. In contrast, basic statistical tools substantially improve performance across multiple model families, while advanced tools provide little additional benefit when models lack prerequisite lower-level capabilities.

papers.title: BIBIMBAP: A Benchmark for Instructional BIM-Based Automated Programming
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are emerging as natural-language interfaces for Building Information Modeling (BIM), successfully achieving information retrieval, but no benchmark exists to evaluate their ability to edit Industry Foundation Classes (IFC). We introduce BIBIMBAP, a Text-to-BIM benchmark with 100 curated tasks covering Create-Read-Update-Delete (CRUD) operations across spatial, geometric, topological, numeric, and conceptual categories. Each task includes a natural-language prompt, an IFC model, expected structured outputs, and test scripts for automated evaluation. Baseline results show limited performance (best: 50.2%) and frequent failures in constraint preservation and spatial reasoning, with some correct outputs achieved despite flawed reasoning.

papers.title: Preference-Augmented Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Sensitive Navigation
papers.abstract: Ensuring safe and reliable navigation under diverse sources of uncertainty remains a central challenge for autonomous systems. Within distributional reinforcement learning (DistRL), Implicit Quantile Networks (IQN) have attracted interest for navigation under uncertainty because they enable risk adaptation through flexible quantile sampling. Existing approaches, however, typically use a fixed or randomly sampled Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) level during training and adjust the risk level during deployment using hand-tuned hyperparameters or external sensor signals. This scalar-CVaR formulation confines learning to a narrow family of tail-risk preferences, creating a mismatch between training-time preference exposure and deployment-time risk adjustment. We instead represent variations in risk preference as shifts in quantile-weight distributions and expose the agent to diverse preferences through preference-guided exploration. At deployment, we optimize against the worst-case preference distribution to derive a conservative policy that accounts for multiple risk profiles. This reduces hyperparameter tuning and reliance on limited sensor signals under partial observability. Experiments across simulated environments and vehicle platforms show that our method reduces collisions while improving task success.

papers.title: On transportation of constrictions on phase-lock areas of overdamped Josephson junction by means of isomonodromic deformation of the associated special double confluent Heun equation
Specific, cumulative and reversible odour learning in a whole-brain connectome model of Drosophila
papers.abstract: Whole-brain models of the fruit fly built from the FlyWire connectome can predict how neurons respond to a stimulus, but they keep every synapse fixed and so cannot learn, while models that do learn simulate only the mushroom body. I made the synapses from Kenyon cells (KCs) to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) plastic in a whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire model of the FlyWire connectome, under a rule in which dopamine weakens each synapse in proportion to how strongly its KC fired. Odours reached the KCs through the connectome's mapped olfactory wiring, and punishment was delivered by driving the 12 PPL1 dopamine neurons at 100 Hz. Pairing an odour with punishment lowered the response of approach MBONs to that odour from 11.3 to 0.3 Hz in all five noise replicates of one simulated brain, while unpaired and never-paired odours and controls with the rule switched off or scrambled changed little. A second odour paired on the already trained brain was learned at 85.5% of the strength reached by a naive brain, and approach MBONs ended with weak responses to both odours. With a timing rule in which dopamine arriving before the odour strengthens a synapse, a simulated fly body driven by the model unlearned and relearned in four of four cycles, whereas the first rule got stuck after one; backward pairing alone was too weak to reach behaviour. All results are for aversive learning; reward learning could not be tested because, at the synaptic weight and synapse floor used here, sugar input does not recruit the reward dopamine neurons. Learning depended on an authored plasticity rule, an injected punishment signal and other authored choices detailed in Methods; given these choices, the odour-specificity of learning followed from the structure of the connectome.

papers.title: Sharp Logarithmic Bounds for Vilenkin-Fejér Kernels
MAGE: Towards Generalizable Multi-timescale EEG Representations
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) data plays an important role in understanding human brain activity, with various major applications. While current approaches, which largely build on EEG foundation models, have demonstrated strong performance across datasets and tasks, they typically rely on a fixed temporal scale. This design choice limits their ability to capture characteristics of neural dynamic behavior, often spanning across multiple timescales, which are naturally captured in EEG recordings. To address this limitation, we propose MAGE (\textbf{Multi-timescale Adaptive Generalization for EEG}), a foundation model that dynamically adapts to capture and integrate information across different timescales. Specifically, MAGE combines two key mechanisms: (i) a novel multi-timescale attention mechanism, capable of learning representations across multiple temporal scales and (ii) a trainable aggregation module, that dynamically identifies and adapts to the most informative timescale of the input signal. Experimental results across seven datasets demonstrate that MAGE consistently outperforms existing EEG foundation models while using substantially fewer parameters. Moreover, our results support the hypothesis that different downstream tasks benefit from distinct temporal scales. All source code will be released.

papers.title: Implementing Set-Theoretic Types
papers.abstract: Set-theoretic types provide a rich type algebra that supports unrestricted unions, intersections, and negations, together with a decidable type constraint-solving algorithm known as tallying. These types are particularly well suited for typing dynamic languages, where functions often exhibit both generic and overloaded behavior. However, the complexity of their implementation has hindered their widespread adoption. In this paper, we introduce a modular representation for set-theoretic types and revisit the algorithms for subtyping and tallying. We compare our approach with the historical CDuce implementation and evaluate the performance impact of some optimizations and design choices.

papers.title: Why Today's Internet Cannot Support Tomorrow's Immersive Experiences: Insights from the NSF Workshop
papers.abstract: Immersive computing is poised to become a major paradigm for future human-computer interaction (HCI), enabling spatial and embodied experiences across applications such as education, healthcare, manufacturing, emergency response, and scientific discovery. However, today's Internet and computing infrastructure were not designed for real-time, multi-user, sensor-rich, and privacy-sensitive immersive applications. They require coordination across sensing, representation, compression, networking, edge/cloud computing, rendering, security/privacy, and human experience. This report summarizes key findings from the NSF Workshop on Networking and Systems Challenges in Immersive Computing. The workshop brought together researchers from networking, systems, extended reality (XR), artificial intelligence (AI), graphics, HCI, security, privacy, and applications to identify challenges and opportunities. We conclude that immersive computing cannot be enabled by isolated advances in network bandwidth, device capabilities, AI models, or rendering alone. The field needs end-to-end architectures that adapt to user behavior, application requirements, resource constraints, and social expectations. We organize the agenda into six themes: networked systems for immersive computing; real-time edge-cloud orchestration for XR applications; AI for immersive experiences; privacy, security, and trust in XR systems; human-centered design and user experience in XR; and scalable infrastructure, testbeds, and open ecosystems for XR. We further identify key research questions, future trends, risks, ten-year success metrics, and action items for academia, industry, government, and research community. The report calls for coordinated investment in open platforms, reproducible benchmarks, privacy-preserving systems, and human-centered evaluation to build trustworthy, scalable, and broadly impactful infrastructure.

papers.title: On the Seven-particle Clusters of Lennard-Jones and Thomson
Fairness Explanations Improve Fairness In Human-AI Decision Making: an empirical evaluation of parole decision-making
papers.abstract: Both humans and AI exhibit systemic biases, yet little is known about how interface design can foster fairness in hybrid human-AI decision-making. This paper introduces a method for extracting fair data samples from biased datasets and adapts a fairness-explanation technique to highlight potential AI bias during decisions. We conducted a within-subjects study (n=48) where non-experts made decisions across three conditions: independent human judgment, unexplained AI assistance, and AI assistance augmented with visual ethnic-bias explanations (Fair-XAI). To isolate effects, the AI conditions provided systematically balanced recommendations. Results show that fairness explanations significantly reduced both sex and ethnic bias compared to human-only decisions. Fair-XAI also marginally improved fairness over balanced AI recommendations while enhancing task performance. These findings demonstrate that fairness-centered explanation interfaces can meaningfully shape user behavior, providing concrete design insights for developing equitable and accountable human-AI systems.

papers.title: Autonomy Is Absent, Not Eroded: An Observational Study of User Autonomy in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
papers.abstract: Does prolonged interaction with Large Language Models reduce users' observable autonomy during conversation? We test this degradation hypothesis by scoring user autonomy across 2,877 multi-turn conversations (46,952 turns) from WildChat and validating on 500 conversations from LMSYS-Chat-1M. Our core finding is a null result: population-level autonomy remains stable throughout conversations, only 4.7% of conversations show meaningful decline, and an apparent decrease at later turn positions is explained by survivorship bias. Instead, the dominant pattern is not erosion but absence: 80.8% of conversations exhibit zero or low autonomy throughout. When autonomy engagement occurs, it is self-reinforcing (persistence doubles from 40% to 85% over consecutive turns). These findings reframe the problem: the risk is not that LLMs progressively degrade users' observable autonomy, but that most users never engage in independent reasoning during the interaction.

papers.title: Grounding Insight: An Artificial Affect Signal for Human-Centric Explainability of RL Agents
papers.abstract: In Human-Interactive Robot Learning (HIRL), human teachers assess learning progress by observing agent behavior. However, Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents often fail to express learning progress in human-interpretable ways, leading to suboptimal or counterproductive teaching. This work proposes "Insight": a human-interpretable affective signal grounded in the RL process. It is specifically designed to address the "Absence of learning" human teacher mental model misalignment - the misconception that a failing or exploring agent is broken, underpowered or not learning at all - by signaling an agent's "Aha!" Insight moment. The signal is derived from the absolute Temporal Difference (TD) error making it easily implementable in other RL agents. To ground this signal, five design criteria were formulated: Relevance, Interpretability, Faithfulness, Scalability, Generalizability. The structural construct validity was assessed through simulation, examining micro and macro dynamics and event-related sensitivity. Micro dynamics reveal that Insight captures meaningful learning events at the appropriate time and magnitude. Macro dynamics demonstrate that the signal follows the agent's learning phases and reflects overall progress. Event-related sensitivity shows, the signal distinguishes the saliency of environment interactions, such as positive rewards versus "trauma-like" negative events. These results demonstrate that technical RL dynamics can be effectively packaged into human-like affective substrates to close the teacher-learner loop.

papers.title: VIVID: Bringing Tool-Augmented Agents into Enterprises
papers.abstract: Tool-augmented large language model agents connect natural-language requests to enterprise services, yet their operational viability depends on reliable execution, organizational control, and system responsiveness. We present VIVID, a deployed tourism-management agent system designed to study these requirements in a real enterprise environment. On an audited dataset of 283 queries, its Qwen3-8B configuration achieves 59.06\% strict end-to-end success across the evaluated decision stages, indicating useful but bounded autonomous capability. Stage-wise KV-cache eviction reduces mean latency by 34.4\%, while targeted optimization reduces the mean latency of the five slowest measured business tools by 81.1--92.3\%. In a three-month deployment serving more than 1,500 personnel, VIVID reduced average per-order processing time from approximately ten minutes to under two minutes, with a final-task error rate below 1\% after human-in-the-loop control. These results show that enterprise agent viability requires system-level consideration beyond isolated tool-calling accuracy.

papers.title: Cellery: Gradual, Composable Structure for Spreadsheets
papers.abstract: Structure in spreadsheets is typically restricted to ranges of cells and flat tables. However, replacing the open-ended two-dimensional grid with a more structured alternative risks limiting users' freedom and impeding exploratory workflows. How can we enable expressive structure in spreadsheets while preserving their flexibility? We propose a model that allows users to gradually add structure on top of the traditional grid. To identify common structural patterns, we conducted a content analysis of 30 real-world spreadsheets. Based on our findings, we developed Cellery, a novel spreadsheet system that makes these structures explicit. In Cellery, users gradually define the structure of their spreadsheets using named groupings of cells, composing together four structural primitives: Atoms, Lists, Tables, and Blocks. Once defined, users can directly manipulate structures, dynamically reference them in formulas, and incorporate them in reusable abstractions. We evaluate Cellery with an expressiveness study reproducing spreadsheets from our sample, demonstrating that it is capable of representing types of structure that traditional spreadsheets cannot. In a preliminary user study of five participants, we find that they successfully use Cellery to design spreadsheets with explicit structure, and we uncover opportunities for further work on the formula language.

papers.title: Personalized Alignment of Language Models with Human Value Profiles
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for subjective tasks such as seeking advice, where there is often no single correct answer. Yet dominant alignment methods learn a single behavior policy that applies uniformly across users, limiting their ability to reflect individual value priorities. We propose personalized value alignment, a framework for adapting model responses to users' stable value profiles rather than to personas, demographics, or task-specific preferences used in prior personalization work. Our approach represents users through Schwartz value profiles and selects which of their values are relevant to each query before applying targeted prompting, activation steering, or LoRA-DPO. We create a dataset of 1,501 value-tension scenarios and evaluate over 152 diverse value profiles sampled from a nationally representative survey. Value-targeted methods outperform no-personalization, demographic, and full-profile prompting baselines, indicating that gains come from focused conditioning on query-specific value priorities rather than mere exposure. We further find that steering effects are not uniform across users: alignment gains vary by where a user's priorities fall in the value space. Combining targeted prompting with activation steering or LoRA-DPO yields the strongest personalization while keeping logical quality within adequate range.

papers.title: Made in the Image of the Creator? AI Use in Creative Work Reduces Authenticity, Love & Other Psychological Benefits
papers.abstract: Across psychological, philosophical, and theological traditions, creations have been understood as being "made in the image of their creator" - they reflect the person who made them. The rise of generative artificial intelligence, however, has blurred the throughline between creator and creation. Across three experiments (one pre-registered, U.S. and U.K. samples; N = 651), we examined differences in creator outcomes associated with AI-assisted versus human-only creative work. Compared with human-only work, AI-assisted work was associated with significantly lower self- and identity-relevant indicators, including authenticity, self-creation connection, positive affect, and intrinsic motivation, and with higher levels of the "existential ick" emotions of disgust, guilt, and shame. Additionally, we found that the authenticity gap was statistically mediated by the creators' perception that their AI-assisted work contains less of their love, above and beyond differences in perceived effort, uniqueness, quality, and expensiveness. We also ruled out effort justification as an alternative explanation. Together, these findings suggest that AI reshapes not only how creative work is produced, but also the extent to which creators experience their work as an authentic expression and extension of themselves.

papers.title: Puzzles to Paradigms: A Survey of Human--Agent Collaboration in Scientific Innovation
papers.abstract: Agentic AI systems are increasingly embedded in scientific workflows, including literature synthesis, hypothesis generation, tool use, writing, and peer review. However, existing surveys and evaluations often emphasize task performance while underexamining how humans and agents coordinate under different epistemic conditions of scientific work. This survey introduces CSCW$\times$Kuhn, a coordination-aware framework that connects computer-supported cooperative work dimensions with distinct scientific contexts. Using this framework, we synthesize recent human--agent systems and benchmarks to examine how coordination demands and failure risks may vary across contexts. Our synthesis identifies five recurring failure modes: procedural drift, grounding substitution, evaluative flattening, proxy optimization, and epistemic black-boxing, and argues for evaluations that move beyond task accuracy and toward grounding, provenance, disagreement preservation, and long-horizon scientific reliability. Our corpus and coding artifact are available at this https URL .

papers.title: Semantic-Enhanced Sparse Temporal Modeling for Dynamic Engagement Estimation in Multimodal Interactions
papers.abstract: Dynamic engagement estimation aims to infer participants' evolving engagement states from continuous multimodal interaction streams. Existing approaches typically combine acoustic, pose, and visual representations with temporal models to capture observable interaction patterns. However, conversational semantics are difficult to align with frame-level engagement annotations in the same manner as continuous audio-visual signals, leaving dialogue context less effectively exploited in existing temporal modeling pipelines. Moreover, engagement annotations often evolve smoothly over time, making dense frame-level modeling computationally redundant and potentially sensitive to local annotation noise. To address these issues, we propose SEST, a Semantically-Enhanced Sparse Temporal framework that models engagement-related information from both semantic and temporal perspectives. SEST leverages Multimodal Large Language Models to extract multimodal semantic embeddings, providing dialogue-aware contextual information beyond conventional frame-level features. In parallel, SEST replaces dense-to-dense temporal modeling with a sparse-to-dense pathway, where continuous frame sequences are first encoded into compact temporal dynamics to reduce redundant computation and broaden temporal coverage, then fused with semantic context and recovered to the original label resolution for dense engagement prediction. Experiments on the MEE2026 benchmark demonstrate the effectiveness of SEST, which achieved first place in the challenge.

papers.title: Benefits and Burdens of Technology-Supported Activity Pacing in ME/CFS: A Thematic Analysis of Reddit Discussions
papers.abstract: Technology and self-tracking play an increasingly important role in the self-management of chronic conditions. Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) is a type of energy-limiting condition, with activity pacing as a key self-management strategy that helps individuals regulate their activity within their energy limits to prevent symptom worsening. However, people with ME/CFS frequently adopt technologies designed for healthy bodies, which they have to repurpose to suit their pacing needs. We report findings from a thematic analysis of Reddit data, using the Non-Adoption, Abandonment, Scale-Up, Spread and Sustainability (NASSS) framework as a sensitising concept. We identify three pacing strategies among people with ME/CFS: no-tech pacing, low-tech pacing (e.g., spreadsheets and diaries), and high-tech pacing (relying on continuous passive sensing from consumer wearables), and characterise the benefits and burdens of pacing technology use. Among these, affordability was a salient topic, highlighting the importance of making technology for pacing financially accessible to people with ME/CFS who follow the high-tech route.

papers.title: Industry case studies of adapting TTS for smooth interactions
papers.abstract: Modern, neural-based ASR and TTS systems for speech communication are now very sophisticated, but they are frequently designed for average users in more idealized scenarios, which can underperform when interacting with users having specialized listening needs, or who speak in non-standard ways. Here we review recent TTS research, and note that industrial, production-level implementations of adaptive TTS systems are scarce. We describe how we implemented changes to TTS systems based on prior research, and then report qualitative results from two case studies, where adapted TTS techniques are applied to real-world HRI settings: First, in an older adult care home, and second, in an airport, where noise levels create comprehension problems. Results suggest promising directions using relatively simple modifications to pitch, duration, and intensity of the robot's speech, and offer a framework for larger, more formal studies of how TTS adaptations can improve HRI.

papers.title: Engagement Estimation in Human-Robot and Human-Human Interactions across Domain, Age and Culture: MultiMediate'26 Challenge
papers.abstract: Understanding engagement in human interaction is essential for modelling assistive and context-aware AI systems. Previously, the MultiMediate challenge has focused on estimating momentary continuous engagement values in adult conversation across cultures, achieving high levels of generalisability across domains. However, engagement can be measured in different metrics and manifest differently between children and adults. MultiMediate'26 therefore expands the evaluated domain set to include the PInSoRo dataset of Child-Child and Child-Robot play sessions in English. These sessions were annotated categorically with task and social engagement, diversifying engagement types, age ranges and interaction types. In this paper, we describe the MultiMediate'26 challenge and its goals, introduce the NoXi, NoXi-J, MPIIGI, and PInSoRo datasets, showcase extracted multi-modal features, present our baseline model for engagement estimation across all domains, and discuss challenge submissions and approaches. In an effort to provide a transparent and welcoming challenge environment, baseline code, leaderboard, datasets, and extracted features are publicly available at this https URL .

papers.title: Micro-Randomized Trial of an AI-Simulated Practice Tool for Therapeutic Skills
papers.abstract: Though LLM-simulated practice may support psychotherapy education, open questions remain about which system features provide the most educational value. We developed an AI-simulated practice tool for use in psychotherapy classrooms that provides speaking practice with LLM-based patients, followed by a post-practice activity that includes feedback from a fine-tuned LLM and written reflection exercises. We deployed the tool in a graduate psychotherapy course (n=25, 5 weeks) using a micro-randomized trial (MRT) - a method which can estimate the causal excursion effect of an intervention by leveraging longitudinal repeated randomization with participants. Testing four conditions crossing AI feedback (present/absent) with reflection granularity (utterance/session-level), we found surprising interaction effects on student engagement and educational value: utterance-level reflection paired with AI feedback significantly outperformed all conditions. Students valued comparing the AI suggestions to their own rather than passively accepting them. As the first MRT in a health education setting testing an LLM-simulation system, this work demonstrates that MRTs, a method mostly used in mobile intervention research, offers a viable evaluation paradigm for AI systems deployed in health education settings.

papers.title: Reaching the last mile? How Design Decisions Shape Medical Device Qualification and Classification of Patient Support Chatbots in the EU
papers.abstract: Few AI chatbots have transitioned the 'last mile' from research prototypes to clinical practice, partly because mapping conversational design decisions to regulatory requirements is complicated. This paper presents a design-oriented regulatory analysis of a chatbot supporting stroke survivors. Using Design Space Analysis operationalised through the QOC (Questions, Options, Criteria) framework, HCI researchers and legal scholars assess how variations in three conversational functions - health Q\&A, recovery monitoring, and motivating medical adherence - influence qualification and classification under the European Medical Device Regulation (MDR), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and AI Act (AIA). Our findings show that seemingly minor design decisions - such as role, actionability, and proactivity - influence regulatory obligations. The paper contributes insights into ten conversational design considerations influencing regulatory interpretation and demonstrates how QOC can support integrating legal considerations into human-centred design workflows. Finally, we suggest compliance-aware pathways to market, while reflecting on whether all chatbots should pursue the 'last mile'.

papers.title: Facilitating Reproducibility in Visualization Systems Research Through Containerization
papers.abstract: In this position paper, we argue for the importance of containerizing visual analytics artifacts to improve the scientific progress of our research community. First, based on our previous experience authoring, reading, and reviewing visual analytics research from the previous decade, we identify risks and impediments to empirical research in visual analytics within the broader reproducibility crisis, including an inability to compare systems and techniques and a slow pace of adjusting to a rapidly changing ecosystem of analysis methods, such as machine learning and artificial intelligence. Next, we analyze the benefits of different artifact sharing and deployment setups across five artifact goals: reproducibility, replicability, portability, performance, and scalability. Then, we argue that containerization addresses the issue of reproducibility in visual analytics research, with downstream benefits in terms of replicability, portability, performance, and scalability. To demonstrate the ease of use and the utility of containerization, we deploy ten visual analytics systems developed over the course of a graduate seminar onto a live server using containerization with the help of agentic AI. We share lessons learned through the containerization process, and describe a suite of potential benefits for our research community as well as research opportunities for leveraging modularity to improve the artifacts themselves.

papers.title: Can You Spot the Virtual Patient (VP)? Expert Evaluation, Turing Test, Linguistic Analysis, and Semantic Similarity Analysis
papers.abstract: Communication is a core clinical competency and essential for safe, effective patient care. Virtual patients (VPs) powered by large language models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative to traditional formats such as standardized patients (SPs). However, few studies have quantitatively as well as qualitatively evaluated their realism across diverse clinical scenarios using behavioral studies and linguistic dialog analyses. This study evaluated the realism of GPT-4o-generated VPs through expert review, Turing testing, linguistic analysis, and semantic analysis. We generated 44 VPs using structured illness scripts derived from doctor-simulated patient dialogues across 17 clinical categories. Experts annotated responses for hallucinations, omissions, and repetitions, with high interrater reliability (ICC > 0.77). A Turing test revealed that participants struggled to distinguish VP responses from those of real patients, with average classification accuracy for VP responses falling below chance level. Lexical and syntactic analyses of over 2,000 conversation turns showed that VP responses were generally realistic, more formal and lexically consistent, while human responses displayed greater emotional variation. Semantic similarity using BioClinicalBERT and cosine similarity averaged 0.871 at the response level and 0.842 at the transcript level. Our findings support the integration of LLM-based VPs in communication training while highlighting areas for trust, transparency, and refinement, contributing to both GenAI deployment in healthcare and its safety evaluation.

papers.title: Human-Likeness is Multi-Dimensional: Evaluating LLM Generated Virtual Patients Against Simulated Patient Dialogue
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate virtual patients (VPs) for medical training. As these systems move toward broader deployment in medical education, reliable evaluation is needed to identify potential failure modes and ensure that generated patient responses remain consistent with human simulated patient (SP) behavior. Inaccurate, unrealistic, or inconsistent responses may introduce educational risks by exposing learners to misleading patient interactions. However, current evaluation approaches rely heavily on human judgment, making large-scale evaluation difficult.
