For a fixed recovery map, syndrome projection produces a block-diagonal logical channel whose diagonal Pauli weights follow from code-induced error classes, with no physical Pauli twirl; concatenation is then iterated redistribution, with the dominant logical error guiding the next code. The bit-flip and phase-flip three-qubit codes with standard recoveries supply a closed-form benchmark, and logically inequivalent recoveries appear as a design degree of freedom for shaping the channel presented to the next decoder. For amplitude damping, the three-qubit rules select C2(sigma_y)C1(sigma_x): one level converts the damping into a nearly pure logical-X channel at the price f1 = 1 - 3gamma/4, the second level suppresses that channel to f2 = 1 - (9/4)gamma^2, and the concatenated protocol overtakes the unencoded channel below gamma_c = 0.292 (f_c = 0.848); across the n-qubit repetition family the suppression order rises as gamma^(w+1), with w = (n-1)/2, while the gate budget grows as n^L. Correlated noise requires joint class statistics, whereas coherent noise retains intra-class coherences that make the same transformation usable in reverse as a tomographic fingerprint; there the companion work proves local identifiability from a rank certificate evaluated inside the parameter domain, classifies the sole permutation-symmetry ambiguity as structural at any chain length, and closes it with one two-qubit marginal channel. The construction remains an analytic benchmark, not a universal prescription for an inner code beneath a surface code.

papers.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
Beyond the Fock Vacuum in Finite-$N$ Bilocal Algebras of Vector Models
papers.abstract: We discuss the finite-$N$ Hilbert space of bilocal operators that underlies bilocal holography of vector models, beyond the sector built on the Fock vacuum. If the microscopic oscillator Fock space carries a multiplicity-free dual action of a compact color group $G$ and a bilocal algebra, Howe duality implies that projection to the derived subgroup $[G,G]$ selects precisely the characters of the abelianization $G^{\rm ab}=G/[G,G]$ that occur in the Fock space. Thus $O(N)/SO(N)=\mathbb Z_2$ gives two sectors, $U(N)/SU(N)=U(1)$ gives integer determinant-charge sectors, while $Sp(N)$ is perfect and gives no additional sector; Bose/Fermi statistics and the number of modes determine which sectors are actually realized. We construct the epsilon and determinant backgrounds that generate these sectors, together with their finite-$N$ constraints and Casimirs, and find that the two bosonic $O(N)$ sectors are not distinguished by any Casimir. Using group-integral projectors, we derive explicit sector-resolved characters for the $O(N)$ and $U(N)$ theories. Around each new background we solve the constraints with auxiliary oscillators, which form a Fermi sea for bosonic matter. In the free vector model on $\mathbb R\times S^2$ the lowest states in the new sectors are baryonic primaries; we determine their energies, degeneracies and spin content exactly at finite $N$, together with their lowest energy at fixed angular momentum.

papers.title: Learning-Oriented Fault-Tolerant Control for UAVs with Time-Varying Fault Estimation
papers.abstract: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in safety-critical applications has created a growing demand for control strategies that remain reliable in the presence of actuator and sensor faults. This paper presents a fault-tolerant control framework that combines constructive mathematical modeling, proportional--integral (PI) fault estimation, and learning-oriented control. A nonlinear quadcopter model is first developed using both the Newton--Euler and Euler--Lagrange formulations, from which a discrete-time linear model is derived for observer and controller design. A PI observer is then proposed to estimate actuator and sensor faults, with exponential estimation-error convergence established for constant faults in the absence of disturbances and ultimate boundedness established for slowly time-varying faults under bounded disturbances. The estimated fault signals are incorporated into an active fault-tolerant control architecture together with a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) controller, which is trained using only the yaw channel and subsequently applied to improve closed-loop tracking performance. Numerical simulations illustrate the observer's estimation performance under constant and slowly time-varying faults, including bounded disturbances, and the tracking performance of the integrated controller under multiple actuator and sensor fault scenarios. The proposed framework combines model-based fault estimation with learning-based control to improve fault accommodation and tracking performance in UAV systems.

papers.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
Phase-Stabilization-Free Information Processing on Unstable Photonic Processors
papers.abstract: Hadamard-coded optical receivers commonly require stable interference conditions for absolute codeword discrimination. Here we encode four symbols as differential Hadamard operations: no phase change or a $\pi$ shift on exactly two of three non-reference input modes. The information is carried by the selected phase-change operation, rather than the absolute optical codeword. We investigate a fixed eight-port intensity-only receiver that reconstructs six coupled trigonometric observables from simultaneous power measurements. Their deterministic sign transformations allow an analytical decoder to identify the applied operation from successive measurements without continuous optical phase stabilization or knowledge of the initial absolute codeword label. An earlier measured signature and sufficiently limited inter-measurement drift remain necessary. We establish exact observable reconstruction, characterize exceptional phase configurations and conditional noise sensitivity, and compare ideal four- and eight-port detection under an equal-photon budget. Experiments on programmable photonic processors yield 96.19\% analytical decoding accuracy; a separate machine-learning analysis reports 98.31\% on a held-out experimental trace. The results demonstrate differential, intensity-only Hadamard operation decoding under the tested conditions.

papers.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
papers.abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and d log-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level and loop-integrand cosmological correlators, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a Mathematica package MadStree. To demonstrate the efficiency of our method, we evaluated up to $10^6$ points for each master integral in our examples, and found that the average computational cost per numerical point per master integral is on the order of $\mu\mathrm{s}$.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates
papers.abstract: Learned barrier certificates provide a principled mechanism for establishing safety of stochastic systems, but their validity may deteriorate during deployment when the underlying dynamics differ from those used for training. We propose an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits a learned barrier certificate using observed closed-loop trajectories. The monitor is intended to detect loss of statistical support for the deployed barrier condition; it does not by itself guarantee detection before unsafe entry or safety of a subsequent intervention. Specifically, the conditional barrier-drift condition is formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test, and observed barrier increments are transformed into a nonnegative test supermartingale, yielding finite-sample false-alarm control under arbitrary stopping times. Inspired by finite-horizon safety verification, we further introduce a deterministic temporal shaping of the monitoring boundary, making the monitor more conservative early in a prescribed deployment horizon while preserving anytime-validity. The monitor is designed to detect statistical evidence that the safety certificate is no longer consistent with the observed dynamics, rather than to predict unsafe entry. To assess the monitor empirically, we evaluate empirical alarm behavior under valid and invalid certificates. Code and data are available at this https URL .

papers.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
papers.abstract: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions whose bulk dual is not yet identified, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. We show that the $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and analytically compute their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

papers.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
papers.abstract: We study the boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in a probe Abelian Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane. Different drives ending at the same charge density can prepare states with different slow mode amplitudes. Two pulses cancel the slowest mode at linear order, but charge exchange during preparation and radial Maxwell feedback regenerate a slow tail at cubic order. We derive the complete cubic response from the lower order field equations, including feedback after source removal, and use it to predict a compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms that the compensation reduces the residual slow amplitude from third to fifth order in the source strength. For a representative protocol, the slow amplitude is reduced by a factor of about 600 relative to linear cancellation. This extends the fast relaxation window without changing the final quasinormal mode spectrum. Further nonlinear tuning suppresses the estimated residual amplitude to the level of numerical resolution. The prepared states can overtake a weakly driven reference despite having a larger excess free energy at source removal. Three pulses also suppress a second slow channel over the resolved time window and reveal interference between faster modes. Starting from a common initial state, controls with zero net charge transfer reach a given relaxation threshold sooner than passive relaxation, even when the full control duration is included.

papers.title: Mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim beyond the polylog quotient
Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
papers.abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $\alpha<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in parametric regressions involving stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for three classes of heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We also develop limit theory for functionals of strongly nonstationary heavy-tailed fractional processes. We demonstrate that the proposed methods, particularly a weighted extension of IVX, facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes mildly and nearly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/\alpha<d<2-1/\alpha$, where $\alpha\in(1,2]$. A related weighted instrumental-variable estimator is also considered, primarily for estimation purposes.

papers.title: Increased-order generalized synchronization in memristive neurons: dissipativity analysis and data-driven control
papers.abstract: We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses next-generation reservoir computing to learn predictors from uncoupled full-state trajectories and an affine synchronization map through dynamical consistency. The resulting sampled-data controller achieves small residual tracking errors without access to the governing equations. Relative to a reference map within the data-driven framework, the learned map reduces median control effort approximately eightfold while improving tracking accuracy. These results connect synchronization-map selection with conditional convergence guarantees and reduced control requirements.

papers.title: A learner-free swarm approximates the explore-exploit equilibrium allocation: A self-organized attractor in place of reinforcement-learning machinery
A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.

papers.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.

papers.title: QRecoupling.jl: numerical and exact computation of classical and quantum recoupling coefficients
papers.abstract: The Julia package QRecoupling evaluates classical and quantum recoupling coefficients, such as Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and $3j$ and $6j$ symbols, and user-defined sums of factorial products, with numerical, exact and symbolic targets. One compact factorial rule covers classical and deformed evaluations, while its cyclotomic exponents reveal common factors and determine which terms contribute at unitary levels. Adaptive arithmetic resolves strongly cancelling sums, while exact tests in quantum integers distinguish algebraic zeros from small nonzero values without a computer-algebra system. At spin cutoff 500, classical $3j$ and $6j$ symbols are evaluated about 7 and 15 times faster than with WIGXJPF. For the tested quantum deformations, relative errors remain below $4\times10^{-14}$ through spin cutoff 400. Recurrences compute fusion matrices with 401 channels about 100 times faster than loops over their entries. The resulting coefficients support recoupling identities, changes of coupling basis and tensor-network calculations.

papers.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
papers.abstract: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow, with several flutter speeds at one Mach number. We map this boundary and its elastic-axis family with coupled Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate of the damping trained by batch active learning, and distribution-free split conformal prediction, which bounds the marginal error rate of stability calls. Three failure modes of damping labels are invisible in the residuals, and the half-degree mean incidence left by an impulsive start at $1^\circ$ freestream incidence raises the flutter speed at the dip by 2.8%, more than any numerical setting. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 63 of 64 independent runs correctly, and at most 1.8% of calibrated calls on held-out runs are wrong. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations show that, for the case A structure about the axis, the inviscid fold exists only for axes more than about 0.4 chord ahead of the leading edge, on two meshes. Chordwise energy budgets, closed three ways, explain both branches. On the lower branch the falling reduced frequency, at unchanged shock phase, raises the shock input and lowers the upstream damping similarly. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge; moving the axis aft brings the flutter-mode pivot towards the section, so the upstream damping falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes.

papers.title: Perron--Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for inhomogeneous random graphs
Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
papers.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $\mu$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

papers.title: A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
Stable topology and stable compactness
A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
papers.abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

papers.title: A wind memory for odour source search in reversing wind
papers.abstract: After wind reversals, old odour arrives while the sensed wind points away from the source, so wind followers, which surge upwind, are misled. A hold gate stores the wind at first odour contact and feeds it to an unchanged follower while the live wind points over 90° away. On 60 random simulated reversing flows it raised a published moth model's success by 10.8 points (95% CI 6.6 to 15.4) and four other followers' by 6.0 to 10.1, but cost the moth model 5 points in steady wind. A fixed wind delay was not resolvably worse at insect scale, but in simulation rescaled to a legged robot's sensors and turn rate the gate beat the best delay for two followers, only one margin surviving Bonferroni correction. As the robot never ran the gate and a plain spiral searcher beat the gated moth model, it is an add-on, not a better searcher.

papers.title: Square-difference factorization: ring structure, torsion splitting, and ideal classes
All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134 .

papers.title: pcNN-SN: a physics-enhanced predictor-corrector neural network algorithm coupled with the discrete ordinates method for neutron transport equations
papers.abstract: Super-resolution machine learning methods hold promise for addressing the high computational costs associated with high-dimensional features in traditional transport simulations. This paper proposes a physics-enhanced neural network coupling algorithm for discrete ordinates (SN) transport calculations. Based on high- and low-accuracy data, we develop a predictor-corrector neural network (pcNN) to predict correction factors for coarse-grid solutions. Based on transport equations, local physical features containing subgrid-scale information are selected as network inputs. Dimensionless transformation of physical quantities reduces the input space dimensionality and narrows the range of parameter distributions, thereby facilitating network training. Physical constraints are incorporated into the network model, and the corrected solution retains its original conservation properties. pcNN and SN transport sweeps are internally coupled, and numerical solutions are corrected online. Numerical results demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively improve coarse-grid solutions to achieve a level of accuracy comparable to that of fine-grid results. The physics-based network design enables the model to demonstrate a certain degree of reusability under different computational conditions. Compared to mesh refinement, the pcNN-SN algorithm reduces the computation time for the three-dimensional test problems by more than 60%.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
papers.abstract: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using a novel multipole re-summation technique, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. This serves as a non-trivial check on our results. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.

papers.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
Rapid Graviton Thermalization through a Scalar--Gauss--Bonnet Coupling
papers.abstract: We show that gravitons can thermalize much faster than the universe expands in an effective scalar-mediated model. A thermal fermion bath maintains a massive scalar close to equilibrium, while scalar decay and inverse decay, $\phi\rightleftarrows g+g$, drive the graviton distribution toward a Bose--Einstein distribution with zero chemical potential. We establish this equilibrium state and calculate how it is reached from an initially empty graviton sector. For a scalar mass of $1\,{\rm TeV}$, an interaction scale $\Lambda_{\rm int}=m_\phi/0.03$, and a Yukawa coupling $y=0.03$, the graviton occupations approach their equilibrium values to within $0.1\%$ over $0.1\leq p/T\leq5$ after approximately $0.024$ initial Hubble times, including cosmic expansion and energy transfer from the bath. This interval contains the thermal energy-spectrum peak. The scalar remains close to equilibrium, its vacuum decay widths are narrow, and the graviton interaction is perturbative over the reaction domain. Assuming the effective theory applies on this domain, our results demonstrate that gravitons can reach near-thermal equilibrium under these conditions. We also derive the present-day thermal spectrum for a specified decoupling and entropy history.

papers.title: Universal Scaling and Geometric Correction of High-Frequency Mass Transfer in Porous Electrodes
papers.abstract: Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. Transient operation can nevertheless produce peak interfacial fluxes above this steady limit, although the time-averaged flux remains bounded. Here, we use a frequency-domain volume-averaging framework to study this transient response in porous media. In the perfectly reactive limit, the spectral Sherwood number approaches $\Shnd\sim\sqrt{\iu\wstar}$ at high frequency, with magnitude proportional to $\omega^{1/2}$, phase $\pi/4$, and a universal leading prefactor. A boundary-layer analysis shows that this response follows from local transient diffusion and is independent of the global pore geometry. Numerical results for parallel plates, circular tubes, and twelve porous microstructures confirm the scaling across variations in particle shape, symmetry, porosity, array arrangement, flow orientation, and flow strength. We also derive the first geometry-dependent correction, which depends on interfacial area, surface curvature, and sharp edges, and verify it without fitted parameters. Comparisons with published impedance measurements for a carbon-felt fiber and a vanadium flow-battery electrode are consistent with the predicted transport response. Finally, we derive bounds on pulse duration and identify operating windows for representative redox couples. These results establish a temporal route to enhanced peak transport in porous electrodes without requiring surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic instability.

papers.title: Optimal Design of Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph for China's Large Segmented Telescope
papers.abstract: China's next-generation large telescopes, such as the Expandable Aperture Segmented Telescope (EAST) and the Large Optical/Infrared Telescope (LOT), are being planned as flagship facilities for high-angular-resolution astronomy, including the direct imaging and characterization of exoplanetary systems (e.g., exoplanets, circumstellar disks). However, their segmented, centrally obscured apertures present significant challenges for coronagraph design: diffraction from segmented gaps and spiders severely limit contrast, particularly at small inner working angles (IWAs). To address this, we investigate an optimal Shaped Pupil Lyot Coronagraph (SPLC) architecture tailored for these telescopes, which combines a binary shaped pupil apodizer, a focal-plane occulting mask, and a Lyot stop to suppress stellar glare and enhance contrast. We further augment the coronagraph design with a two-deformable-mirror (2-DM) adaptive optics (AO) system to correct atmospheric turbulence and residual aberrations. End-to-end simulations based on site parameters for Lenghu in Qinghai Province and assuming idealized extreme AO (ExAO) correction demonstrate that the optimized 2DM-SPLC designs can achieve raw contrasts of order 10^-6-10^-7 in the V, H, and K bands, providing an upper-bound estimate of the system performance. The simulated performance highlights the advantages of the SPLC in mitigating diffraction from segmented and centrally obscured pupils while maintaining a small IWA and practical throughput, indicating that the 2DM-SPLC is a promising coronagraphic architecture for high-contrast exoplanet imaging on China's future large segmented telescopes.

papers.title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
papers.abstract: The Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark standardized evaluation in molecular optimization, but it is built on simple property-based oracles that do not capture structure-based drug design. As the field has moved to docking-based objectives, evaluation practice has become unstandardized, and different methods report results on different docking tasks, often without a shared protocol for fair comparison or sample-efficiency constraints. To address this, we introduce Practical Molecular Optimization for Docking (PMO-Dock), a benchmark and protocol for docking-based optimization consisting of 25 tasks covering hit generation, lead optimization, and a new specificity task requiring strong on-target binding while penalizing off-target interactions. The protocol separates model development from final evaluation: validation tasks are used for hyperparameter tuning, and test tasks are held out for final evaluation and are not used during development. Evaluation on the test tasks is done under a strict oracle budget to reflect realistic drug-discovery settings. We benchmark four diverse high-performing methods spanning different optimization paradigms, Saturn (reinforcement learning), GenMol (discrete diffusion), Genetic-guided GFlowNet, and ChemLlama (LLM-based evolutionary search). Our results show no universally best method across tasks, additional analyses of hyperparameter transfer (cross-task and cross-category) and sensitivity show that transfer is often limited and varies by method, motivating method-dependent selection strategies. This benchmark provides a concrete standard for evaluating generalization to unseen tasks and sample efficiency under a limited test-time oracle budget.

papers.title: IC 1297: The Most Distant Known X-ray Planetary Nebula and One of the Most Luminous
papers.abstract: We present the first targeted Einstein Probe (EP) X-ray observations of any planetary nebula (PN). Using the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT), we detect X-ray emission within the central region of IC 1297. The spectral analysis yields a plasma temperature of $kT = 0.086^{+0.054}_{-0.058}$ keV ($T\sim1.0 \times 10^{6}$ K), characteristic of shocked wind bubbles in PNe, whereas there is no evidence that its Wolf-Rayet central star emits X-rays. The absorption-corrected X-ray luminosity in the 0.3--2.0 keV energy band is $L_{\mathrm{X}} = 2.8 \times 10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$, also consistent with a hot bubble. At an adopted distance of $\sim3.8$ kpc, IC 1297 is the most distant X-ray emitting PN found to date, opening up a new observational window on hot-bubble formation and evolution. It is also among the most luminous known X-ray-emitting PNe. Our results demonstrate the capability of the EP FXT for detecting and characterizing faint, extended X-ray sources in the soft X-ray band for distant PNe, extending the known spectral properties of detectable X-ray emitting PNe. We also compiled the X-ray properties of all 41 known Galactic XPNe, finding a clear correlation between distance and X-ray luminosity that reflects an observational bias toward detecting the brightest sources at large distances. The compilation also shows a separation in X-ray luminosity between hot bubbles powered by H-rich and [WR]-type central stars, with the latter reaching luminosities up to an order of magnitude higher. The ten most luminous XPNe all host [WR]/PG 1159 central stars.

papers.title: Imaging the topological sign of a Dirac mass with spin-polarized tunneling
papers.abstract: A Dirac mass is characterized not only by its magnitude but also by its sign, which influences the Berry curvature, Hall response, and the propagation direction of chiral boundary modes. However, local spectroscopy of magnetic topological surfaces has so far accessed only the gap magnitude $|M|$. Here we show how the topological sign of $M$ can be determined locally. We first establish the sign information that spin-resolved tunneling can access and the reference required to obtain an absolute Hall sign. Although spin--orbital entanglement generally obscures the relation between measured spin and Dirac pseudospin, crystalline rotation symmetry alleviates this ambiguity at the band edge. On a $C_3$ axis, an axial tip couples to a fully spin-polarized state whose tunneling asymmetry directly reveals the sign of the occupied-band Berry curvature, independent of orbital composition. We further show that the zeroth Landau level provides an independent mass-sign measurement with an unpolarized tip, while opposite domains and their chiral domain-wall modes provide self-consistency checks. These results pave the way for imaging the locations where the topological character changes within a material, rather than merely identifying where a spectral gap appears.

papers.title: Reduced Embry characterizations of quasinormal operators
Holographic Pseudo Entropy from the Rindler Method in AdS and Flat Space
papers.abstract: Via the Rindler method, we study holographic timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) for a general timelike interval in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$. The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_\phi$ takes one to the other. We clarify the geometric role of the timelike extremal curve in the Rindler frame. We show that it is the line $\tilde U=\tilde V=0$ stretched between the two horizons, starting on the inner horizon, touching the outer horizon at its midpoint, and returning to the inner one. No such curve exists outside the region between the horizons. Its length, $i\pi\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $i\pi c/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.

papers.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
papers.abstract: Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theories, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves, which give the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval. The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which gives rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.

papers.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

papers.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
An Integrated Framework for Rule-Based Data Editing
papers.abstract: Statistical data editing in official statistics must restore consistency while limiting changes to observed data. Exact minimum-change correction can be computationally demanding. This paper develops a general framework for structured data whose dependencies admit a normalized acyclic routing representation. It connects routing metadata and explicitly specified semantic edits to logical admissibility, violation diagnosis, and correction. Under stated record semantics, the generated Horn theory characterizes admissibility without materializing its deductive closure. Canonical indices preserve the origin of each requirement and identify the variables that can affect a violation. With complete diagnostics and strictly positive weights, a nonnegative violation Hamiltonian vanishes exactly on admissible records within the specified domain. This characterization is independent of the correction procedure and provides both an objective for correction and a certificate: a verified zero-energy output is admissible and globally minimizes violation energy within its permitted candidate domain. Minimum modification cost is formulated separately, with sufficient conditions for an equivalent penalized objective and optimality certificates based on attained lower bounds. A household survey application illustrates the construction, the verification of admissible corrections, and minimum-cost certification for a subset of outputs. The framework supports traceable validation and correction in official statistics, while statistical accuracy of replacement values requires separate assessment.

papers.title: Game-Creation-Agents: Autonomous Game Production
papers.abstract: Game-Creation-Agents (GCA) turns a natural-language request into a runnable Phaser 4 browser game. The pipeline first builds a multimodal game design document that couples mechanics and scene contracts to grounded visual references. It then projects that document into a runtime scaffold, machine-readable contracts, and deterministic tests. Eight specialized agents next carry out production: scenes are implemented serially, assets are produced in parallel, and one reduced manifest joins the two branches into a single build. Build-linked real-UI checks and a code-blind critic then verify that build and decide whether the game may ship. Each blocker returns to the agent that owns the affected artifact for a bounded repair, and the game is released once all the gates pass. We evaluate finished games separately, through their rendered interfaces alone, over prompt-matched tasks run under a common protocol. GCA achieves stronger requirement satisfaction, core mechanics, content depth, and functional visuals than a comparable open pipeline. In a side-by-side human study, raters also score GCA's games higher on every dimension and prefer them overall.

papers.title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
Bogoliubov excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate in the presence of the non-Hermitian skin effect
papers.abstract: The non-Hermitian skin effect is one of the most remarkable topological features of non-conservative physics. It causes a macroscopic accumulation of states at the boundaries of a confined system, opening new ways for controlling and directing waves in non-Hermitian settings. The non-Hermitian skin effect has recently been observed in experiments with Bose-Einstein condensates of exciton polaritons and ultracold bosonic quantum gases. Here, we develop a non-Hermitian extension of the Bogoliubov-de-Gennes theory for the collective excitations of the condensate, both in the semiclassical (mean-field) and second-quantised framework. By considering a trapped condensate under the action of an imaginary gauge field, we find that while the repulsive interactions oppose the localisation of the condensate, its excitations continue to display a strong skin effect. As a consequence, in the presence of harmonic confinement, we predict a strong shift in the dipole oscillation frequency, in contrast to Hermitian systems, where this frequency is fixed by the trap dimensions. Furthermore, we find that a second-quantised treatment removes the shift of the dipole oscillation frequency entirely. The two approaches describe different physical regimes, and identifying which one a given platform realises requires a microscopic open-system description. We suggest that this discrepancy between the two theoretical approaches can be resolved in experiments.

papers.title: Equilibria and Consensus in Mixed Weighted-Average and Weighted-Median Opinion Dynamics: The Consensus-Promoting Role of Weighted-Average Individuals
papers.abstract: How individuals respond to their neighbors' opinions shapes whether a networked group reaches consensus. This paper analyzes synchronous discrete-time opinion dynamics on a fixed influence network, where individuals use either weighted-average (WA) or weighted-median (WM) opinion-aggregation mechanisms with individual-specific inertia coefficients. We characterize equilibria through graph-theoretic conditions on opinion level sets and WA balance equations, proving that every solution converges to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. We define type-dependent cohesive sets, whose WA members assign all their influence weight to the set and WM members assign at least half. The absence of two disjoint such sets gives a necessary and sufficient graph-theoretic criterion for consensus from any initial condition. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent dissensus. Converting WM individuals to WA cannot create type-dependent cohesive sets and preserves existing guarantees of consensus from any initial condition. If the conversion eliminates every disjoint pair of these sets, the converted system also guarantees consensus from any initial condition. Four numerical studies examine the locations and proportion of weighted-average individuals, as well as the influence weights, while comparing the consensus criterion with finite-horizon simulation outcomes. In the four network ensembles with 100 individuals, the observed frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with WA proportion at each tested simulation horizon. This trend supports the consensus-promoting role of WA individuals, although individual realizations need not follow it.

papers.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
Perfect discrimination of an orthogonal $2\otimes2$ basis may require collective separable measurements on two copies
papers.abstract: We consider an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ with three entangled states and one product state. This basis is not perfectly distinguishable by LOCC or even by separable measurements when a single copy of the unknown state is available. We show that with two copies no adaptive separable protocol, which measures the copies one at a time, distinguishes the basis perfectly. We then show that a collective separable measurement on the two copies does. Whether two copies suffice for LOCC remains open.

papers.title: Resource Allocation with Midterm Review
papers.abstract: A principal funds an agent's project over two periods, with a midterm review providing a public signal about project quality. The agent privately knows the project's quality and always prefers more funding, while the principal wants to match funding to quality. We show that the optimal mechanism frontloads the review's information value: the principal's expected payoff is strictly higher in the first period than in the second, even though she is better informed after the review. In the optimal mechanism, higher-quality projects receive more funding initially but face larger cuts after a bad review, leaving them with less funding than lower-quality projects. A good review increases funding, but the resulting allocation does not preserve the initial ranking of projects and, under a mild condition, declines with quality near the top.

papers.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array
papers.abstract: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.

papers.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
Comparing randomized trials: a formal approach
papers.abstract: Disagreements between randomized trials that address the same causal question pose challenges for the interpretation and synthesis of evidence. We sketch a causal framework for comparing the results of randomized trials that explicitly accommodates the possibility of trial engagement effects. Using counterfactual outcomes defined under joint interventions on treatment assignment and trial-related actions, we compare trial-native treatment effects with the effects transported from one trial to the population of another in a common target population. We show that standard conditions for transporting treatment effects across trial populations are not sufficient to guarantee agreement between transported and trial-native effects. Agreement additionally requires conditions governing how trial-related actions affect outcome across studies - for example, absence of trial engagement effects, equivalence of such effects across trials, or lack of interaction between trial engagement and treatment assignment. Our framework clarifies potential sources of disagreement across trials and extends existing approaches to study comparison to settings in which trial engagement effects may be present.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian Secular Dynamics of Hierarchical Triple Systems: A Consistent Canonical Treatment of Cross Terms
papers.abstract: We derive the secular Hamiltonian for hierarchical triple systems from the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) three-body Hamiltonian through first post-Newtonian (1PN) order, using Lie--Hori--Deprit canonical perturbation theory and time averaging over the inner and outer orbits. The canonical framework systematically incorporates higher-order cross terms through scalar generating functions and Poisson brackets while preserving the Hamiltonian structure. We recover the electric and magnetic 1PN--quadrupole terms of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST), rather than those reported by Lim and Rodriguez (LR). We further derive the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term, the Newtonian quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian, and a third-order coupling between inner 1PN precession and the squared quadrupole. The outer-pericenter dependence of the quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian is removable by a canonical redefinition of the mean elements. Direct integrations of the Einstein--Infeld--Hoffmann (EIH) equations confirm the de Sitter term, the direct electric term, and the binding-energy renormalization of the inner-binary mass. For the systems considered by LR, the canonical terms do not reproduce the extreme merger acceleration they reported. Instead, the relativistic modulation of the eccentricity cycles is driven primarily by the outer-pericenter-dependent part of the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term.

papers.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
$q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
papers.abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in ( arXiv:2510.12431 ) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

papers.title: MLP-Initialized Reinforcement Learning for Exit Timing in SPX Short-Straddle Portfolios
papers.abstract: This paper studies exit timing for SPX short-straddle portfolios using a two-stage supervised and reinforcement-learning framework. Historical episodes first generate ex-post optimal hold/exit labels for training a multilayer perceptron (MLP) using only contemporaneously available state variables at deployment. The trained MLP then initializes reinforcement-learning actors that are fine-tuned with a risk-aware trading reward. Out-of-sample evaluation over 2024-2026 shows that the supervised MLP substantially outperforms passive holding and representative fixed-time and profit-and-loss-based exit rules. Across seven independent seeds, MLP-initialized Actor-Critic averages 37.54% cumulative return and a Sharpe ratio of 1.705, compared with 35.01% and 1.651 for the supervised MLP. Actor-Critic trained from scratch averages only 0.18% return. These findings show that oracle-guided supervised learning provides a stable foundation for reward-based policy fine-tuning in a sparse and path-dependent option-exit problem.

papers.title: Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs
Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
BayesJudge: Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian Meta-Evaluation of Human and LLM Judgments
papers.abstract: AI evaluation pipelines often produce conflicting judgments rather than clean labels. Yet existing methods largely collapse disagreement into a single hard label. As a result, item ambiguity, rater biases, and the position preferences of LLM judges are erased together: evaluation outcomes appear deterministic while concealing the underlying uncertainty, and may even systematically favor one response. This conflict is especially acute in pairwise LLM evaluation. We propose \textbf{BayesJudge}, an online Bayesian meta-evaluation layer for conflicting human-LLM judgment streams. BayesJudge treats the latent preference of each item as a latent variable and jointly models two sources of evaluator bias: rater-specific confusion matrices for human annotation bias, and an explicit order parameter for the position preference of LLM judges, thereby separating response quality from evaluator bias. We derive an exact online posterior recursion and adopt a scalable Rao-Blackwellized assumed-density sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) approximation for streaming inference. Consequently, each comparison yields not a single hard label but a posterior distribution over each response winning (as well as a tie or ambiguity state), together with posterior estimates of the bias parameters, making evaluation uncertainty explicit and quantifiable. On synthetic data, BayesJudge accurately recovers human annotation biases and LLM position biases online, and strictly outperforms variants that freeze either bias channel in held-out predictive log-likelihood. On the real-world SummEval dataset, BayesJudge detects systematic order effects in LLM judgments, distinguishes the behavioral signatures of experts and crowdworkers without rater metadata, and yields posterior uncertainty that reflects genuine human disagreement. Our code is available at this https URL

papers.title: The optimal information complexity of VC learning
papers.abstract: Steinke and Zakynthinou(2020) introduces the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework of analyzing the information complexity of learning algorithms based on algorithm-dependent information-theoretic quantities. We study one of these quantities, the evaluated Conditional Mutual Information (eCMI). It has been an interesting question whether the optimal PAC guarantee for VC classes can be recovered from the algorithm-dependent analyses via CMI. And we show that it is possible to recover this guarantee by constructing a learning algorithm whose eCMI is of order O(d) in the realizable case, where d is the VC-dimension of the concept class. Specially, our algorithm is a randomized Majority-of-5 base learners with optimal in-expectation generalization guarantee.

papers.title: Taxonomic Classification with Tag Arrays
papers.abstract: We present a tool, KATKA, for taxonomic classification with tag arrays. Compared to Ahmed et al.'s state-of-the-art tool Cliffy ({\it Genome Research}, 2025) on the SILVA dataset from their paper and a readset similar to one of theirs, KATKA is faster, more accurate, much smaller and drastically easier to build.

papers.title: Singlet sector of the vector model with angular potential
papers.abstract: We study the singlet sector of large-$N$, $O(N)$ vector model on $S^1_\beta\times S^2_r$ in presence of an angular potential $\Omega$. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-\omega^2)$, where $\omega=r\Omega$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-\omega^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $\omega^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.

papers.title: The consistency strength of the failure of amenable C-sequences
Organizational Lifespan as Commitment: The Case of Foundations
papers.abstract: An organization's lifespan may commit future decision makers to continue, terminate, or retain discretion. We identify when each rule has value for philanthropic foundations. If the same aligned actor chooses investment and subsequent survival, discretion weakly dominates fixed rules; a commonly used investment comparison fails because it omits the option to invest enough to make continuation desirable in adverse states. With noncontractible organizational investment delegated to an earlier actor, however, perpetuity may improve incentives despite inefficient continuation in some states. The result survives an observable-investment extension. A finite terminal date is valuable under governance-induced overcontinuation, and its optimum reflects both direct operating benefits and investment incentives. We establish nonempty environments favoring each regime and distinguish institutional lifespan from payout policy, requirements to preserve the foundation's endowment capital, and the duration of grant commitments.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated Regularized Vector Multiplicative Error Models for Positive-valued Financial Time Series
papers.abstract: The logarithmic vector multiplicative error model (log-vMEM) provides a methodology for modeling and forecasting multivariate positive-valued time series. However, the number of autoregressive parameters increases rapidly with the system dimension and lag order, posing challenges for estimation and model selection. This paper develops a regularized estimation framework for the log-vMEM with multivariate Gamma errors by incorporating hierarchical lag structures to induce sparsity and accommodate heterogeneous lag dynamics. We consider three hierarchical lag structures: componentwise, own-other, and elementwise, in combination with group lasso, adaptive group lasso, group MCP, and group SCAD penalties. Parameter estimation is carried out through an alternating block-coordinate optimization algorithm with sequential Gauss-Seidel updates, while GPU-accelerated numerical quadrature is employed to address the computational burden of evaluating the multivariate Gamma likelihood. Simulation experiments investigate parameter recovery and lag selection under different sparsity structures. The real data analysis is carried out on the realized volatility measures for Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) which allows a comparison of the competing regularization approaches in an empirical financial setting. Together, these developments provide a computational framework for sparse multivariate volatility modeling with flexible lag structures and dependent Gamma errors.

papers.title: Pauli Decomposition by Character Theory: A Memory-Bounded Algorithm for Qubits and Qudits
papers.abstract: Pauli decomposition of an $n$-qubit operator is expensive if each of the $4^n$ Pauli strings is treated as an unstructured object. Labeling those strings by the configuration space $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ makes them displacement operators $X^{\otimes x}Z^{\otimes z}$ on the computational space: shifts by~$x$ and multiplications by characters $Z^{\otimes z}$ in the computational basis. That labeling organizes the operator into $2^n$ fibers of length $2^n$, one per shift~$x$, each collecting the computational-basis amplitudes that hop by~$x$. Expanding each fiber function in the character basis of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ --- a length-$2^n$ Walsh--Hadamard transform --- recovers the Pauli coefficients at total cost $O(n\cdot4^n)$. The same fiber / shift--character picture extends to $(\mathbb{Z}_p)^n$ (Heisenberg--Weyl qudits). \texttt{paulikit} is a memory-bounded realization for qubits: for matrix-sparse inputs, peak memory need not densify to a full $2^n\times2^n$ operator. Performance is checked on a stated low-end GNU/Linux platform for a coupled-oscillator sweep beyond a billion Pauli terms.

papers.title: From Dialogue to Diagnostic Hypotheses: Evaluating LLM Agents for Psychiatric Assessment
papers.abstract: Although LLMs show promising diagnostic reasoning on supplied clinical evidence, their ability to elicit such evidence through free-form psychiatric interviews remains less understood. We evaluate interview quality and diagnostic hypotheses using simulated patients and human participants. For controlled simulation, we introduce PsyCPG, transforming clinical cases into structured patient profiles. On 30 paired cases, experts rate PsyCPG simulations higher in quality than raw-case role-play (4.50 versus 3.83/5). We introduce PsyCIDRA, a dual-agent framework: its interviewer agent uses a notepad tool, expert-written skills, and ICD-11 reference tools to guide interviews; its diagnostic agent analyzes the transcript and produces a report for expert review, ranking differential diagnoses with supporting, conflicting, and missing evidence. Across four models and 53 development cases, PsyCIDRA achieves higher observed diagnostic agreement than direct prompting. On 81 held-out simulated cases, exact-code rank-1 accuracy reaches 60.5% versus 51.9%. We conduct 101 interviews with human participants; two psychologists, blinded to interview condition and model reports, independently assess interview quality and transcript-supported hypotheses. In separate arms, PsyCIDRA agrees with experts on whether to issue a hypothesis in 79.6% of cases versus 65.4% for direct prompting. This study provides an empirical basis for understanding and evaluating LLM agents in free-form psychiatric interviewing.

papers.title: First-order plants are globally asymptotically stable under antithetic feedback
papers.abstract: We show that first-order linear plants are globally asymptotically stable under antithetic feedback. This is shown by constructing an explicit smooth, convex Lyapunov function and by appealing to a Krasovskii-LaSalle invariance principle.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
papers.abstract: Electric vehicles and heat pumps add large, time-flexible loads to low-voltage feeders. When each household independently minimizes its own charging cost against the same electricity price, this flexible demand piles into the cheapest hours, and the resulting synchronization can stress the feeder more than uncoordinated operation does. This work quantifies that effect on a rural low-voltage feeder with photovoltaics (97 buses, 250 kVA transformer) in 913 simulation runs that compare seven strategies across four seasons, device penetrations of up to 90 %, 208 price weeks from 2022-2025, and heterogeneous heat pumps. At 30 % penetration of each device, this decentralized cost minimization drives the transformer to 253 % of rated capacity, more than three times the peak of non-optimized Fixed-random charging with the same mobility and charged energy, and 478 % with electric vehicles alone at 90 % penetration, with undervoltage at the far end of the longest feeder arm. It exceeds Fixed-random and Fixed-times charging in every winter, spring, and autumn price week, and each 30 pp of heat-pump penetration raises its peak by about 110 pp, twelve times as much as without optimization. Centralized peak minimization removes all demand-driven violations. In the heat-pump-free summer case at 60 % photovoltaics, midday reverse power flow sets a transformer floor of 128.9 % that no strategy undercuts, since no commuting electric vehicle is at home at the export peak. With a time-variable grid fee added to the spot price, the weekly peak of decentralized cost minimization falls into the reduced-fee window in 99 of the 104 fee-active price weeks, compared with 53 without the fee, while keeping at least 89.8 % of its height, so the fee relocates rather than removes the synchronization. The simulation and optimization code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Sub-Voxel Displacement and Ipsilateral Territory Decoupling for 3D Bilateral Coronary Artery Tree Reconstruction in Cardiac CT Angiography
papers.abstract: Reconstructing topologically complete, sub-voxel-accurate 3D bilateral coronary artery trees from cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) requires simultaneously recovering continuous centerline trajectories and separating dense left/right coronary territories without cross-ostial collisions. We present a five-stage tubular drift and ipsilateral territory decoupling framework (M1-M5). Stage M1 pairs a 398,843-parameter multi-scale 3D pyramid encoder with a four-head tubular field network predicting vesselness probability, signed tubular boundary distance, unit tangent vectors, and continuous 3D centripetal displacement vectors. Stage M2 introduces recall-preserving multi-task optimization with 7-group AdamW parameter decoupling, L2-SP backbone regularization, and per-step anchor shrinkage. Stage M3 calibrates cylindrical Valsalva-sinotubular-junction wall coordinates and native-resolution orifice contact expectations for robust left and right ostial rooting. Stage M4 constructs a scalar-potential-weighted minimum-cost arborescence followed by normal-plane cross-sectional pullback and centripetal trajectory pruning. Stage M5 enforces coverage-guarded ipsilateral-field-coupled bilateral collision reduction and subtree handover. Across a 14-case held-out development cohort (Dev-14, 17-arm forward incremental build and 9-arm leave-one-out ablation) and an independent 50-case out-of-sample evaluation cohort (OOS-50) benchmarked against seven external architectures (nnU-Net, 3D UX-Net, Swin-UNETR, MedNeXt, CS2-Net, clDice-UNet, and Point-UNet), M1-M5 reduces bilateral chamfer distance on Dev-14 from 3.4381 mm to 2.2759 mm and achieves 2.7671 mm on OOS-50 with 7.11% bilateral collision rate and 79.7% distal branch completeness.

papers.title: Path-Space Optimal Transport with Interactions: Kinetic Equations and Eikonal Structure
Distributed Learning of $α$-Potential Functions in Strategic Multi-agent Systems
papers.abstract: We study the problem of computing the tightest \(\alpha\)-potential approximation of a general-sum game over continuous action spaces, within a prescribed class of potential functions and when each player has access only to its own utility function. The difficulty is twofold: the approximation error involves a worst-case search over an infinite set of unilateral deviations, and the required utility information is distributed across players. For a linear-in-parameters potential class, we use an exact finite-tuple reformulation that separates the problem into a global outer search over deviation tuples and distributed convex inner problems. We develop a primal--dual inner oracle tailored to this structure and establish a uniform one-sided accuracy guarantee. This oracle can be combined with global outer search to obtain an end-to-end guarantee on the outer optimization error. We also develop a projected zeroth-order outer method as a computationally lighter alternative for higher-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy--computation tradeoff between the two outer-search methods and show that the proposed optimization framework can improve upon analytical \(\alpha\)-potential constructions.

papers.title: Diffuse Galactic Backgrounds with SPHEREx: A Pilot Study of Background Modeling and Its Impact on Extinction
papers.abstract: We present a spectral analysis of diffuse Galactic background emission using SPHEREx data in a pilot Galactic-plane field, where uncertainty in the estimation of the diffuse infrared background is a major source of systematic uncertainty in extinction studies at near- and mid-infrared wavelengths. We construct channel-resolved background maps across the 0.75--5~$\mu$m range using a Large Median Filter approach and then carry the extinction analysis forward only for the cleaner long-wavelength subset at $\lambda \geq 3~\mu$m. In the present field, comparison against an earlier masked-median background model gives a median channel-by-channel background difference of about 6\% and a maximum change of $|\Delta\tau_{\rm norm}|\simeq 7.4$ near 3.205~$\mu$m, underscoring the importance of wavelength-dependent background modeling. These results demonstrate that spectral mapping with SPHEREx provides a practical framework for controlling diffuse background systematics and enables improved constraints on dust opacity and extinction in the Galactic plane.

papers.title: On pointwise convergence of singular integrals of Christ-Journé type
The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labordère
No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
papers.abstract: Relativistic heavy quarks equilibrate even when their microscopic drag and momentum diffusion violate the Einstein relation. We investigate how equilibration proceeds as a function of the coupling and compared to simplified Fokker-Planck models. To do this, we present a detailed calculation of the momentum-transfer kernel in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas through strict $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$, and study the resulting dynamics at leading order in the inverse heavy-quark mass. Beyond leading logarithm, its non-Gaussian structure plays a crucial role in equilibration. We examine closely the analytic structure of the evolution kernel, determine the large-order asymptotics of the momentum-transfer cumulants, and show how the kernel's bounded analytic domain fixes asymmetric exponential tails at the level of the momentum transfer probability. Strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM also features an approximately Gaussian core and exponential tails, but differs in the nature of the kernel's singularities and the velocity dependence of the transport coefficients and tail exponents. These differences have distinct dynamical consequences: for the parameters studied, the persistence of the relativistic population in steeply falling spectra is largely explained by drag alone at very weak coupling, whereas fluctuation-induced survivor bias produces a large relative enhancement at strong coupling. Nevertheless, the shared qualitative structure between weak and strong coupling points the way towards a practical phenomenological description of heavy quarks anchored in first-principles field theory.

papers.title: On wall-crossing invariant combinations of Welschinger numbers for rational surfaces with a conic bundle
