Benchmark calculations for an exactly solvable nonequilibrium impurity model agree well with the exact results and reveal a low-rank structure of the integrands. When applied to interaction-quench problems in the half-filled Hubbard model, the method reproduces fast thermalization at a critical interaction strength with accuracy comparable to CT-QMC. Away from half filling, where the sign problem becomes even more severe, the present approach remains well controlled, revealing a crossover instead of a sharply defined fast thermalization point in the 3/4-filled case. The solver can also be applied to steady-state DMFT problems, yielding accurate spectral functions in the metallic regime without analytic continuation.

papers.title: Causal Inference for All: Marginal Estimands for Outcomes Truncated by Death
Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers
papers.abstract: Modern LLM workflows move coordinate-indexed objects across checkpoints: steering vectors, sparse autoencoders, top-$k$ neuron sets, attribution lists, LoRA updates, optimizer states, and merge alignments. This requires fixing the model's residual-stream gauge. We show that the native coordinate-preserving orthogonal gauge is architecture-dependent: LayerNorm residual charts have permutation gauge $S_d$ up to a global sign flip, while RMSNorm charts with generic gains have signed-permutation gauge $B_d = S_d \ltimes \{\pm 1\}^d$. Permutation-only alignment is thus symmetry-incomplete for RMSNorm models. We introduce sign-marginalized Hungarian matching and prove that with decorrelated coordinates, signed-correlation matching has a permutation-accuracy ceiling equal to the true gauge's positive-sign fraction up to $O(d 2^{-d})$, which sign-marginalized matching removes. Omitting signs induces expected squared error $2\|\Delta W\|_F^2$ on weight updates and loses orientation on vectors and AdamW first moments, while RMSNorm gains and AdamW second moments permute without signs. Controlled tests confirm these laws: a Qwen2.5-1.5B SST-2 LoRA adapter retains 0.944 accuracy (from 0.945) under $B_d$ transport vs. 0.523 under $S_d$, and steering preserves effects to $<10^{-4}$ at zero raw top-10 overlap. Across natural checkpoints, inherited slots suffice for same-base descendants (96.2%-100% retention), whereas cross-generation pairs support sparse prompt-stable subsets with causally decisive negative signs ($+0.185$ vs. $-0.010$ at $8\sigma$ on Qwen2/2.5-0.5B; $+0.189$ vs. $-0.021$ on 1.5B). Along fine-tuning trajectories, composing local $B_d$ gauges recovers 91.1% of cross-run Qwen2.5-1.5B coordinates at 1,500 steps vs. 60.3% for endpoint matching. Merge and interpretability audits confirm that coordinate names are reproducible only relative to an explicit $B_d$ gauge.

papers.title: Self-consistent field theory of semiflexible nematics: Density-nematic coupling, anisotropic elasticity, and defect core sizes
papers.abstract: Landau--de Gennes theory provides a successful continuum description of nematic order and topological defects, but connecting its phenomenological coefficients to microscopic molecular properties remains challenging in lyotropic liquid crystals. They often exhibit strong elastic anisotropy and, as is the case in lyotropic chromonics, defect cores are much larger than characteristic molecular length scales. A self consistent field theory for fixed length wormlike chains is introduced to describe the effects of chain flexibility and of density--nematic order coupling on equilibrium uniform and defected states. Results show that while the coupling between density and nematic director is weak, a stronger density--degree of order coupling softens collective nematic fluctuations, controls the limit of stability of the nematic phase, and modifies the magnitudes and anisotropy of the correlation lengths. Near a $+1/2$ disclination, density deviations relative to the uniform state are shown to be large, and modify the extent of the core. Further, the director profile is anisotropic. The defect core size is found to scale approximately linearly with the bulk correlation length, a trend also observed in an augmented Landau--de Gennes model. These results provide microscopic insight on how chain density and flexibility couple to nematic order, and point to an augmented Landau--de Gennes model for lyotropic liquid crystals.

papers.title: Muon learns balanced solutions in matrix factorization without slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics
papers.abstract: Matrix factorization (i.e., problems of the form $\min_{\mathbf{P},\mathbf{Q}} \|\mathbf{M}^\star - \mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{Q}\|_\mathrm{F}^2$) is a minimal learning problem that exhibits both nonlinear parameter dynamics and representation learning. In this setting, we study how parameter trajectories under the Muon optimizer differ from those of gradient descent. We identify three main dynamical differences: (1) Muon avoids the slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics of GD from small initialization. Muon instead learns all the top singular vectors of $\mathbf{M}^\star$ at the same rate, and they saturate in order of increasing (rather than decreasing) singular value. (2) Muon does not diverge even when the learning rate exceeds the critical threshold set by the local loss sharpness. This frees the learning rate from the condition number of the problem, enabling rapid convergence via exponential learning rate annealing. (3) Once the weights are aligned with each other and the target, Muon flow conserves the matrix quantity $\sqrt{\mathbf{P}^\top \mathbf{P}}-\sqrt{\mathbf{Q}^\top \mathbf{Q}}$, while gradient flow is known to conserve the matrix $\mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{P} - \mathbf{Q}^\top\mathbf{Q}$. Despite having distinct conserved quantities, both optimizers find the so-called balanced solution from vanishing initialization. When training from small random initialization, the weights spontaneously align early in training. We derive the alignment rates in simple settings and show that they predict the empirical alignment rates in general. Finally, we exploit structural properties of Muon to construct a learning rate schedule that achieves near-perfect alignment in only two optimization steps.

papers.title: Finite-resolution exhaustive traversal of thermodynamic state spaces has divergent thermodynamic length
papers.abstract: Resolving a prescribed multidimensional control window by a single continuous, serial scan is a task distinct from driving between fixed endpoints. We formulate this task as metric coverage at resolution $\eps$. Classical covering estimates, applied to a compact regular $d$-dimensional Riemannian window, give a required length of order at least $\eps^{1-d}$; local grid traversals attain the same exponent. When a physical friction tensor uniformly dominates the coverage metric, this geometric cost implies a necessary duration of order at least $\eps^{-2(d-1)}$ at fixed quadratic excess-work budget. Fixed-duration divergence refers to the slow-driving quadratic action and is not a claim about exact work outside that regime. A detailed-balance three-state process and an overdamped harmonic trap provide microscopic friction examples. For the trap, independently integrated Gaussian moment dynamics approach the quadratic prediction as the prescribed raster is slowed, while refinement at a controlled work budget increases scan duration. A quasi-uniform operational resolution floor cuts off the geometric divergence. Landau-response and van der Waals proxy metrics serve separately as prescribed diagnostic geometries: independent quadrature tests their coordinate- and protocol-dependent critical prefactors without asserting universal critical dissipation. Morton ordering supplies an ordering/connector benchmark with larger finite-resolution amplitudes. The resulting resource statements apply to exhaustive serial coverage, with metric, interpolation and driving assumptions specified explicitly.

papers.title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
Breathing mode of quantum droplets in dipolar quantum gases: A sum-rule analysis
papers.abstract: We investigate theoretically the ground-state properties and breathing-mode collective excitations of three-dimensional dipolar Bose gases in anisotropic harmonic traps incorporating quantum fluctuations. Combining a Gaussian variational ansatz with a sum-rule analysis, we derive explicit analytical expressions for both axial and radial breathing-mode frequencies, which are validated by numerical solutions of the time-dependent extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Our theoretical predictions show great agreement with existing experimental data for $^{166}$Er and $^{162}$Dy gases. By constructing comprehensive phase diagrams across the parameter space of the $s$-wave scattering length, atom number, and trap aspect ratio, we reveal both discontinuous first-order phase transitions and smooth crossovers between the dilute Bose-Einstein condensate and dense quantum droplet phases. We confirm that the enhanced incompressibility induced by quantum fluctuations significantly elevates the breathing-mode frequencies in the droplet phase compared with conventional weakly interacting Bose gases. Furthermore, the system undergoes a phase transition and a crossover over the scattering length under the elongated and flattened confinements, characterized by discontinuous jumps and continuous crossovers in peak density and atomic cloud sizes, respectively. Our work offers a useful analytical framework to characterize collective excitations in dipolar quantum gases, providing quantitative insights for forthcoming ultracold atom experiments in lanthanide atoms and polar molecules.

papers.title: The Maximum Initial Mass in low-thrust spacecraft trajectory design
papers.abstract: We introduce the maximum-initial-mass problem as a standalone optimal-control formulation for low-thrust trajectory design and analyze its structure within Pontryagin's framework. For prescribed transfer time and endpoint states, the formulation maximizes the initial spacecraft mass, with necessary conditions yielding full-throttle control in the nondegenerate case and standard primer-vector steering. We establish that extremals of this single formulation correspond to extremals of two distinct problems: minimum-time and maximum-time transfer. The sign of the terminal dynamics-only Hamiltonian distinguishes the two normal representations, while the zero-Hamiltonian case admits an abnormal representation. We also clarify the relationship between free-time transversality and costate normalization in indirect formulations. This unified perspective offers two practical advantages. For reachability analysis, it replaces separate minimum- and maximum-time conditions with a single initial-mass threshold, simplifying both feasibility checks and the learning of reachability maps. For homotopy methods, it opens extended continuation paths that connect branches beyond those accessed by tracking individual time-optimal solutions. Applied to a benchmark multiple-revolution GTO-to-GEO transfer, the approach recovers the best known minimum-time solution, identifies previously unreported extremals, and reveals a funnel-like arrangement of transfer-time minima and maxima along a constant-initial-mass contour, including a previously reported trajectory that is a local maximum rather than a minimum.

papers.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing, Formalized in Lean 4
papers.abstract: The Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing states that a market is free of arbitrage exactly when it admits an equivalent martingale measure. We formalize it in Lean~4 over Mathlib in three settings: a finite-state market with one risky asset over a finite horizon (Harrison--Pliska), and one-period markets with one asset or finitely many assets on an arbitrary probability space. The finite case is the geometry of a separating hyperplane. In the one-period case the proof builds the equivalent martingale measure from a minimiser of the potential $\theta\mapsto\E[\log(1+e^{\langle\theta,Y\rangle})]$: absence of arbitrage makes the potential coercive off the redundant directions, its first-order condition is the martingale property, and the logistic weight of the minimiser, normalised, is the density; a bounded tempering removes integrability, so the return need only be measurable. The construction uses no Hahn--Banach theorem, no $L^0$-closedness argument, no measurable selection and no non-redundancy hypothesis. One predicate serves every time index, with one forward theorem. The same separation also yields the Artzner--Delbaen--Eber--Heath representation of coherent risk measures on a finite state space. We add the second theorem on finite spaces (complete if and only if the martingale measure is unique) and, on any probability space, the reduction of the Dalang--Morton--Willinger theorem to its conditional one-period form. That conditional step, which needs a measurable selection, is assumed, not proved, so the multi-period theorem remains open; in continuous time only the forward direction, for simple strategies, is proved. Every theorem discussed is \texttt{sorry}-free and uses only Lean's three standard axioms, enforced by the build.

papers.title: The Optics of Shadow Bands
papers.abstract: Shadow bands are transient, rippling patterns of light and dark that may appear in moments before and after totality in a solar eclipse. Despite centuries of reports, their physical origin has remained unresolved. This article develops a geometric-optical solution in which the Sun's extended structure produces a celestial analog of Young's double-slit experiment, generating an interference and fringes on the ground. The analysis combines solar limb geometry and a wave-based formulation that yields quantitative predictions for fringe width and spacing. Some other properties of shadow bands are also analyzed.

papers.title: Mosaic: A Benchmark Suite for Differentiable Physics Solvers
papers.abstract: Differentiable partial differential equation (PDE) solvers underpin solver-in-the-loop MLtraining, gradient-based optimal control, and inverse problems, yet the practical cost of obtaining correct, usable gradients from a given solver on a given problem is largely undocumented. Integration effort, computational cost, memory, gradient accuracy, and numerical stability vary widely across solvers and are discoverable only by trial and error. We introduce Mosaic, an extensible benchmarking framework for differentiable PDE solvers that standardizes access to solver gradients. Each solver is packaged as a containerized component (Tesseract) exposing a uniform gradient API regardless of language or automatic differentiation (AD) strategy, enabling researchers to evaluate, compare, and build on non-trivial physical solvers. Our evaluation of 14 solvers across fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, and heat transfer demonstrates that the benchmark surfaces practically relevant differences: order-of-magnitude variation in computational cost and memory, alongside setup incompatibilities and instabilities that rule out solvers for specific tasks. Despite this variation, all solvers that produce gradients converge to similar optima on our tasks, indicating that the practical barriers are memory limits, numerical stability, and setup compatibility rather than gradient accuracy alone. Mosaic is open-source and available at this http URL .

papers.title: New interpretation of the Minkowski limit of $R^2$ gravity
papers.abstract: It is well-established that the Minkowski limit of pure $f(R)=R^2$ gravity breaks down, unlike that of full Starobinsky theory $f(R)=R+\alpha R^2$. We provide a novel interpretation of this phenomenon using the recent thermal analogy between scalar-tensor gravity and Eckart's relativistic dissipative fluids. In this framework, we show that approaching the Minkowski background corresponds to a diverging effective ``gravitational temperature'' along certain non-stationary FLRW trajectories, while the gravitational temperature remains identically zero along the exact de Sitter family. This perspective naturally rephrases the strong coupling problem as a thermal singularity, demonstrating that $R^2$ gravity departs infinitely far from General Relativity rather than recovering it.

papers.title: Too shy to spin? Cosmic wallflowers as proto-globular clusters
papers.abstract: We investigate the rotational properties of star-forming clusters at $z \sim 7.6$ in the high-resolution simulation MassiveBlackPS, focusing on two formation channels: clusters forming in galactic discs via gravitational instability and isolated circumgalactic systems, referred to as cosmic wallflowers, born out of cosmic filaments. Using stellar kinematics, we compare their rotational velocities, $v_{\rm rot}$, and rotational support, $v/\sigma$, to study whether formation environment leaves a clear dynamical imprint. We find a clear separation, wherein cosmic wallflowers systematically have lower rotational velocities and span a wide range in $v/\sigma$, whereas the identified disc clusters are strongly rotation-dominated and extend to higher $v_{\rm rot}$. When combined with stellar surface densities, a subset of the low-$v_{\rm rot}$ cosmic wallflowers lie surprisingly close to the observed globular cluster population in the Milky Way, whereas disc clusters remain offset. Within the cosmic wallflower population, we identify two regimes: lower-density, weakly rotating systems that overlap with these globular cluster properties, and denser, more rotationally supported systems that likely follow a different evolutionary pathway, possibly linking them to the origin of massive black hole seeds at high redshift. We further find that the gas content correlates with this behaviour, with gas-rich cosmic wallflowers preferentially occupying this low-rotation regime. This all suggests that environment and baryonic content together play a key role in setting the initial dynamical state and possible fate of clusters. In particular, weakly rotating, gas-rich cosmic wallflowers emerge as natural proto-globular cluster candidates, potentially evolving towards present-day systems through angular momentum loss and dynamical heating.

papers.title: Holographic light-quark energy loss in a spinning plasma
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled plasma described by a spinning black-brane background obtained from the large-black-hole limit of the Myers-Perry geometry. The parameter $a$ characterizes the boost/rotation parameter of the dual fluid in this holographic setup and is related to the angular velocity in the corresponding limit. We employ two complementary probes, the falling-string and shooting-string descriptions, to compute the stopping distance and the instantaneous energy loss of a light quark moving either transverse or parallel to the local tangential-flow direction. The results show that light quarks quench more readily in a hot environment. For parallel propagation, a counter-propagating configuration enhances energy loss, whereas a co-propagating configuration suppresses it. For transverse propagation, increasing the magnitude of the rotational motion promotes energy loss. In addition, the instantaneous energy loss increases along the trajectory of the endpoint. These results describe classical probe dynamics in the local planar limit and do not include intrinsic-spin effects.

papers.title: A Differentiable DFT-Based Framework for Inverse Materials Design
papers.abstract: Discovering solid-state materials with target properties remains a central challenge in computational materials science. Existing data-driven approaches rely on training data and may generalize poorly outside the training distribution. Here we develop a first-principles inverse-design framework that requires no training data. It integrates reverse-mode automatic differentiation (AD) into the Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker method combined with the coherent potential approximation (KKR-CPA), in which elemental concentrations serve as continuous optimization variables. Reverse-mode AD computes all concentration gradients in one backward pass, enabling optimization over dozens of candidate elements. Any differentiable quantity computable within KKR-CPA can serve as an optimization objective. We demonstrate this generality in permanent-magnet and half-metal design, identifying candidates such as (Nd$_{0.983}$Pr$_{0.017}$)(Co$_{0.72}$Fe$_{0.28}$)$_2$Fe$_3$ and FeMn(As$_{0.83}$P$_{0.17}$), respectively. We also synthesized materials with five SmCo$_5$-based compositions selected during optimization for higher magnetization. Their measured magnetization agreed closely with calculated values. Our framework offers a first-principles route to designing materials with target properties.

papers.title: Energy Extraction via Magnetic Reconnection from a Rotating Dyonic Black Hole in $N = 2, \ U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity
papers.abstract: We study energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating dyonic black hole in four-dimensional $N=2$, $U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity. Using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism in the ZAMO frame, we derive the asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy $\epsilon^{\infty}_\pm$ and determine when reconnection outflows attained negative energy at infinity. By varying the spin $a$, electric and magnetic charges, NUT parameter $N_g$, and gauge coupling $g$, we compute the cutoff magnetization $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and map the region of parameter space that admits $\epsilon^{\infty}_-<0$. We find that $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $\Xi$, and the quartic horizon function $\Delta_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.

papers.title: Taming Symbolic IBP Reduction with Intermediate Bases
papers.abstract: Despite many years of development in integration-by-parts reduction, reconstructing all reduction coefficients, which are rational polynomials of kinematic variables and the space-time dimension, remains a non-trivial problem. The main difficulty comes from the large number of unknowns in a general ansatz, which can lead to a linear system that is too large to solve. In this paper, we present an algorithm for reconstructing reduction coefficients through a sequence of intermediate bases. The resulting analytic reduction coefficients are products of a few analytic matrices, whose non-zero entries are simple rational polynomials. We demonstrate the efficiency of this algorithm with two cutting edge examples: a three-point massive box-triangle and a four-point massive pentagon-triangle. Reconstructing all reduction coefficients for the box-triangle (pentagon-triangle) requires 3289 (13013) numerical samplings, significantly fewer than the number of unknowns in the general ansatz, 1407406 (21638331).

papers.title: RoverDevKit: An open, physics-grounded tradespace toolkit for conceptual design of lunar micro-rovers
papers.abstract: The number of planned lunar micro-rovers is increasing, yet few open, benchmarked tools exist to explore trade-offs in their design. Rover sizing is a highly coupled problem with a feedback loop between vehicle mass and mobility: a heavier rover sinks deeper into loose regolith, deeper sinkage increases power demand, more power requires a larger array, and the array adds mass. We present RoverDevKit, an open-source tradespace exploration toolkit with an evaluator that couples a closed-form wheel-soil model with bottom-up mass, solar-power, thermal-survival, and traverse models. The evaluator is fast enough to serve as the fitness function of a multi-objective genetic algorithm (NSGA-II): a search comprising 3,000 mission evaluations takes under a minute on a single laptop core. We use it to map trade-offs among distance traveled, vehicle mass, and slope capability on mare, polar, highland, and crater-rim missions. The limiting factor varies by mission: energy storage at high latitude, slope traction on loose highland regolith, and traverse range on mare and crater-rim terrain. The wheel-soil model reproduces measured single-wheel drawbar pull from two independent datasets with accuracy consistent with the 20-30% error typically reported for this class of model, and the mass model predicts published 5-50 kg rover masses with median absolute percentage error of 10.5%. A comparison with five published rover designs in the same mass class shows that they lie near the predicted Pareto front.

papers.title: Instabilities of the continuous superradiant laser
papers.abstract: We investigate the intensity stability of the superradiant laser. Our study focuses on the architecture where a continuous beam of atoms in an electronically excited state crosses the mode of a high-finesse Fabry-Perot cavity, which has been proposed as a new architecture of an active optical clock. We show that such superradiant laser can become unstable and develop chaotic behavior. We derive an analytical criterion for this instability and find that it may only occur when the lifetime of photons in the cavity is significantly shorter than the lifetime of atoms. This criterion allows for refining the necessary parameters to run a superradiant laser as a frequency reference in the optical domain. In particular, we point-out the consequences of the instability on intensity fluctuations and laser linewidth. On the other hand, we also point out that the superradiant laser, when in the unstable regime, can become an interesting playground for studying chaos. At the mean-field level, there is a direct mapping to the Bénard instability associated with fluid turbulence; however quantum fluctuations associated with photon out-coupling and atom re-filling substantially modify the expected behaviors. Finally, we point-out the existence of a regular self-pulsing regime at large atom numbers.

papers.title: Loss-Cone-Limited Dark Matter Capture by Early Black Hole Seeds
papers.abstract: The rapid appearance of supermassive black holes at high redshift motivates a reassessment of non-baryonic growth channels. We develop a new loss-cone framework for collisionless dark-matter (DM) capture by early black-hole seeds, with particular attention to phase-space depletion and refilling. The calculation combines Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, a relativistic direct-capture boundary, and an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of angular-momentum transport. Primordial black holes (PBHs) are treated as massive perturbers whose refilling strength depends on both their abundance and individual mass. Collisionless refilling by triaxial or chaotic centrophilic orbits is included as a phenomenological upper-envelope channel. We show that ordinary stellar relaxation gives negligible DM-driven growth for the fiducial high-redshift seeds. PBH-driven granularity can yield order-of-magnitude growth in sufficiently compact halos, while triaxial or full-loss-cone supply can produce a rapid early burst. In the self-consistent calculations, however, the evolution generally becomes supply-limited. Once the accessible low-angular-momentum phase-space reservoir is depleted, the capture rate collapses and the black-hole mass saturates. Fixed-background NFW calculations therefore overestimate sustained growth, especially in the full-loss-cone limit. A TNG50-calibrated NFW benchmark gives negligible growth even under optimistic refilling assumptions. Collisionless DM capture is therefore unlikely to solve early SMBH growth in generic NFW-like halos, but it can provide a radiatively dark upper envelope in rare compact environments with efficient angular-momentum refilling.

papers.title: State estimation of Rayleigh-Bénard convection with reduced-order models
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a state estimation framework for two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard (RB) convection that combines a stable Galerkin reduced-order model (ROM) with an extended Kalman filter (EKF). The ROM, constructed from controllability modes of the linearized Boussinesq equations, provides the nonlinear dynamical model for the filter prediction step. Direct numerical simulations (DNS) are used to generate synthetic measurements for data assimilation. We assess filter performance across periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic regimes, demonstrating that the filter tracks the most energetic modes with high fidelity and achieves time-averaged reconstruction errors below $16\%$ for velocity and $19\%$ for temperature. We apply the ROM-based EKF to a hybrid simulation scenario where the system state is assimilated from velocity measurements. It is shown that velocity observations alone suffice to reconstruct the state, including the temperature field. Finally, we exploit the Kalman gain matrix to develop a greedy sensor placement strategy that progressively removes the least informative sensors. The algorithm reveals a clear hierarchy among sensor types and can be used to derive skeletal observation configurations. It also provides guidance on which measurement variables and spatial locations are most informative for state correction. The present framework is general, and may be applied to other quadratic Galerkin ROMs for state estimation.

papers.title: SierpinskiCam: Camera-Controlled Video Retaking with Sierpinski Triangle Pattern Cues
papers.abstract: Generating novel renderings of a scene along user-defined camera trajectories from a single monocular video, dubbed video retaking, is a compelling but difficult problem in content creation and visual effects. Existing geometry-guided approaches reconstruct a 4D representation from the source video and render it along the target trajectory to condition video diffusion models. However, this guidance degrades as the target camera departs from the source trajectory, leaving newly revealed regions sparse or entirely missing. We propose SierpinskiCam, which addresses this limitation by augmenting geometry-based guidance with Sierpinski dome texture cues that contains rich trackable features even under large viewpoint changes. We further introduce a reference video conditioning mechanism that appends source-video tokens to the target-token sequence and separates the two streams with negative RoPE indices, enabling appearance grounding without architectural modification or per-video adaptation. Extensive experiments show that SierpinskiCam achieves significant gains in camera controllability, geometric consistency, and video quality across diverse and challenging retaking scenarios. Project page: this https URL .

papers.title: Excitonic quasi-condensation in a mass-asymmetric electron-hole biwire
papers.abstract: We study a mass-asymmetric one-dimensional electron-hole biwire system at zero temperature using the diffusion quantum Monte Carlo method. We characterize electron-hole pairing and long-distance pair coherence through the pair correlation function and the projected two-body density matrix over a broad range of carrier densities $r_{\rm s}$ and interwire separations $d$. We identify distinct correlation regimes ranging from a weakly correlated two-component electron-hole plasma to a quasi-condensate excitonic regime and a strongly correlated Wigner-like regime. To understand long-distance pair coherence, we analyze the algebraic decay of the projected two-body density matrix and extract the corresponding power-law exponent $\alpha$ which is less than 2. Strong electron-hole Coulomb correlations allow quasi-excitonic coherence to persist to high densities, down to effective $r_{\rm s} = 0.3$ a.u.\ in addition to low densities. For a representative parameter set, we further find that mass asymmetry suppresses long-distance pair coherence while enhancing short-range electron-hole pairing. Our results provide a microscopic characterization of competing pairing and spatial ordering correlations in mass-asymmetric one-dimensional electron-hole systems.

papers.title: A Fully Specified Bayes Factor Range for Hypothesis Testing and Sensitivity Analysis in Process Tracing
papers.abstract: A Bayes factor can be used in process tracing to reason about the probative value of evidence for a working hypothesis against a rival (Fairfield and Charman 2022). However, relying on the researcher's own sense of probative strength may inflate confidence in $H_1$ (Zaks 2021). We show how to fully specify a generative model of observations to compute Bayes factors in process tracing: First, researchers count the evidence. Second, they classify it as favoring either hypothesis. Third, they formalize a data-generating process that makes the evidence more expected given $H_1$ and another for a rival $H_R$. The ratio of these probabilities yields a fully specified Bayes factor. We compute two Bayes factors under different assumptions, yielding a Bayes factor range that allows researchers to decide whether the balance of evidence favors $H_1$ considering probability thresholds. Our method also facilitates sensitivity analyses of common assumptions, including those about bias and the probative weight of a smoking gun.

papers.title: Hausdorff operators and fractional Hausdorff operators in the Dunkl setting
Closing the Approximation Gap in Simulation-free Latent SDEs
papers.abstract: Recovering dynamical systems from noisy observations is a recurring challenge across scientific domains, including neuroscience and physics. Latent stochastic differential equations (SDEs) address this by modeling the system as an unobserved state that evolves according to a learnable SDE and generates the observations. Variational inference (VI) provides a tractable objective for fitting latent SDEs. Traditional VI algorithms evaluate this objective by numerical simulation over a time discretization, trading fidelity for computational cost. A recent class of algorithms, simulation-free VI, sidesteps this tradeoff by parameterizing the posterior through its instantaneous marginals rather than its drift. In this work, we show that the efficiency of existing simulation-free VI algorithms comes at a price: their parameterizations restrict the approximate posterior to a subset of the SDEs available to simulation-based methods, degrading posterior inference and parameter learning. We propose Helmholtz-SDE, a simulation-free VI algorithm that closes this gap by optimizing over path laws compatible with a prescribed collection of marginals. Helmholtz-SDE recovers dynamics more faithfully than prior simulation-free methods, with the largest gains under high posterior uncertainty. It further matches the performance of simulation-based VI at a fraction of the runtime. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: PromptShift-CRC: What Drift-Aware Weighting Adds to Online Conformal Risk Control for Foundation Models
papers.abstract: A risk threshold calibrated on old prompts can stop being valid when prompts to a foundation model drift. We study PromptShift-CRC, a rule that weights past prompts by feature similarity, falls back to recent prompts when the current prompt is unlike the past, and updates its level online. We prove that the update controls the long-run violation rate for any weights, so marginal coverage cannot separate weighting schemes. We give a conditional bound at a fixed level whose cost is a weighted total variation distance, bounded by a computable prompt-drift term up to an unknown Lipschitz constant. We propose a comparison protocol: a matched short-window baseline, a validity and sharpness frontier, 30-seed synthetic streams, and real-output streams ordered without using the model's output. On MMLU, TruthfulQA (Qwen2.5-1.5B) and RealToxicityPrompts (GPT-2, replicated with a second generator and classifier), every online method reaches the target. PromptShift-CRC stays within 0.0055 of the Adaptive CRC frontier and avoids the worst window, but DtACI matches or beats it in most settings. The rule performs like a mid-ranked window without having to choose one. Tests fixed in advance to favor the weights show no consistent gain over the frontier. Code, outputs and streams are released.

papers.title: Drift-Aware Spectral Conformal Prediction for Non-Exchangeable Streaming Data: A Controlled Evaluation
papers.abstract: Does drift-aware spectral conformal prediction (DASC) narrow the intervals of adaptive conformal inference (ACI) when all methods share one forecaster per data set and one tuning criterion? Not with the projected update. At DASC's step size, projected DASC and ACI widths differ by at most 0.43 per cent on electricity and weather; DASC is wider on finance. With DASC's step size tuned at a larger budget, or with wider step-size sets and scaled bandwidths, paired width intervals against ACI include zero or lie above it. Coverage is near nominal for the adaptive methods, with some under-coverage at the selected settings. The paper contributes a reproducible simulation and resampling design, released with code and saved results: twelve simulated scenarios and three real streams, paired moving-block bootstrap intervals with block-length and seed checks, a perturbation test that every interval uses only past observations (0 failures in 630 checks), and one-at-a-time measurements of how evaluation choices move widths. An earlier preprint reported width reductions of 28 and 42 per cent that came from centring DASC on a different forecast from the baselines. The replacement theory states the status of each result; the earlier long-run theorem was false for the projected update.

papers.title: Spectral Similarity Weights for Adaptive Conformal Prediction: A Bias-Variance Account and a Benchmark
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction intervals lose their guarantee when a series is not exchangeable. We study weighting calibration residuals by the similarity of local Fourier power features, combined with the adaptive level update of ACI. A two-term account of the coverage error, mismatch that falls and sampling error that rises as the bandwidth shrinks, holds with exogenous features and conditionally independent residuals, but not for features computed from the series itself, which is how the method is used. In four simulations, spectral weighting lowered the mean regime-level deviation of coverage by 17% to 19% when the features came from the response and by 75% when they were exogenous, and not clearly under gradual drift. In each recurring-regime design a scaled-error baseline or Conformal PID control calibrated better. On nine public series with 36 forecast origins, spectral weighting with the plain weighted quantile did not differ from projected ACI in coverage error, and Conformal PID and scaled ACI were the best calibrated methods. The features are blind to seasonal phase, so the weights act like a recency kernel. A pure recency kernel did at least as well, especially with a finite-sample rank correction (mean absolute coverage error 0.039 against 0.090 for ACI; a post hoc check). Calendar phase weights narrowed German electricity intervals by 23% at equal coverage, but were not better than ACI across the series. We suggest trying adaptive baselines first, and similarity weights only where regimes differ in spectral shape or season and the effective sample size stays large.

papers.title: Measure the Deployment, Not Just the Model: Rethinking Hardware-Aware Model Selection for Microcontrollers
papers.abstract: Selecting an energy-efficient model for periodic sensing requires accounting for time between inferences. Hardware-aware model search typically measures inference alone, even when the application cares about energy per release. We present CREST (Cross-platform Runtime Evaluation and Search Tool), an open-source hardware-in-the-loop experimentation system that evaluates model and hardware configurations under a specified release schedule. Researchers can vary the objective, schedule, target and candidate proposer while reusing evaluation and replay. Records preserve comparison conditions and separate valid measurements from deployable candidates. Three case studies demonstrate the system. First, searches and controlled replay on STM32 N657 show how waiting changes model and clock selection. For one architecture, continuous inference favors 800 MHz over 300 MHz at 8.0 versus 17.1 mJ per inference, but additional waiting offsets 97% of this saving in a fitted decomposition. With STOP between releases, 300 MHz uses about 0.3-0.4% less board energy per release at 100 and 500 ms. At a fixed clock, the preferred architecture changes between release periods, which a model with shared waiting parameters cannot produce. Latency predicts continuous energy within a median 1.7% on held-out observations, yet most release-energy error remains in scheduled terms. In paired replay, one of six randomly selected near-latency pairs reverses its continuous-energy order by 5.8 mJ per release. Second, replay on three Arduino targets shows proxy-selected inertial-odometry candidates can fail to fit or use more energy than measured selections, with only 9 of 16 FLOPs-selected candidates fitting the most memory-constrained board. Third, an audio classification study reuses the evaluator with LLM-based candidate proposers, and cross-target replay moves a selected configuration from third to last in energy rank.

papers.title: Discrete Coplanarity Rigidity and Local Mahler Volume Growth Near the Cube
Lyapunov-Based Sample Complexity Analysis for Weakly-Coupled MDPs
More Residually Solvable One-Relator Groups
Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
Revisiting the Axial Anomaly and Chiral Magnetic Effect in Dense Matter, with Applications to Axion Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We explicitly compute the axial anomaly in dense matter and show that it takes the same form as in vacuum, even in the massless limit. This result follows from a subtle cancellation in the anomalous Ward identity between the medium-induced contributions to the divergence of the axial current and to the pseudoscalar density. We then revisit the chiral magnetic effect in a fermionic medium coupled to an axial chemical potential in an external magnetic field. We show that, in the clean limit, the medium supports a persistent, conserved anomalous current carried by fermions. The current is determined by the axial chemical potential and suppressed by the Fermi velocity, in agreement with anomalous axial-current correlation functions. Finally, we discuss applications to axion physics, where axion dark matter acts as an effective axial chemical potential, and estimate how helicity relaxation by impurity scattering limits the induced current in realistic conductors.

papers.title: Quantum statistics in an extended collider coupled to a qubit
papers.abstract: Mesoscopic colliders provide an effective platform for probing the mutual statistics of quantum particles. Recent experiments have successfully extracted the mutual statistics of fermions, and more exotic anyons using quantum point contacts (QPCs). Coupling a point-like collider, such as a quantum point contact, to a two-level impurity or qubit can induce statistical transmutation of fermions, causing them to display boson-like bunching tendencies. Here, we extend the analysis to an extended collider. We investigate the scattering of two incoming fermionic and bosonic wave packets in the presence of postselection on the impurity state, and systematically analyze the possible benchmarks used to characterize bunching and infer the underlying mutual statistics. We show that only a specific benchmark faithfully captures the mutual statistics of the colliding particles, while alternative choices can produce spurious statistical signatures. Hence, the correct benchmark for probing the quantum statistics depends on the intricate details of the mesoscopic collider.

papers.title: Express Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

papers.title: Self-Organized Antipodal Multifunctional Micromotors via Evaporative Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation
papers.abstract: Active microparticles with spatially organized multifunctionality could enable new forms of autonomous transport and chemical activity, yet creating such architectures within individual particles remains challenging. Here, we show that such complex functional architectures emerge spontaneously when multiple functional components (enzymes, nanoparticles, etc.) are introduced into evaporating multicomponent droplets undergoing liquid-liquid phase separation. Coupled Marangoni flows and interfacial dynamics drive the asymmetric localization of functional nanoparticles, positioning distinct functionalities on opposite sides of a microparticle in an architecture we term antipodal. This organization generates emergent magnetic anisotropy when magnetic nanoparticles are incorporated, enabling catalytically propelled motion parallel or antiparallel to a uniform magnetic field without an external chemical gradient. We also demonstrate enzyme-enzyme antipodal micromotors that combine weak chemotactic steering with strong propulsion driven by a spatially uniform chemical fuel, a strategy relevant to environments where chemical gradients are weak. Extensive theoretical modelling elucidates the underlying interplay of Marangoni flows and interfacial dynamics, providing a mechanistic basis for tunability. Our findings establish a route to spatially programmed active matter, in which functional architectures and directional capabilities emerge spontaneously through coupled hydrodynamic and interfacial dynamics.

papers.title: Anatomy of fast current-induced skyrmion motion in synthetic antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: The high mobility of current-driven skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets (SAFs) is widely explained by the macroscopic suppression of the skyrmion Hall effect through gyrotropic force compensation. This established view, however, overlooks a concurrent and significant reduction in the Gilbert damping parameter {\alpha}, a key factor in the Thiele equation governing skyrmion velocity. Here, we show that this damping attenuation originates from a reconfigured magnon-electron scattering landscape. Using a microscopic s-d model, we demonstrate that the strong antiferromagnetic interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) exchange coupling in SAFs increases the magnonic gap of skyrmion collective modes, thereby suppressing the thermal magnon population and, consequently, the magnon-electron scattering rate that dominates damping in metallic ferromagnets. Our work establishes a dual-mechanism framework to fully explain the superior kinetics of SAF skyrmions: the macroscopic topological effect rectifies the motion direction, while the microscopic dissipation mechanism reduces the drag. This synergy enables high-speed and efficient motion, providing a fundamental elucidation of the enhanced mobility reported in recent studies such as the work by Pham et al. [Science 384, 307-312 (2024)].

papers.title: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
papers.abstract: Traditionally, atomistic simulation has been constrained by the computational scaling limits of ab initio methods and the parameterization overhead of empirical force fields. The recent emergence of universal machine learning interatomic potentials has significantly mitigated these bottlenecks, offering near-quantum accuracy and generalizability across diverse chemical spaces at a fraction of the computational cost. However, this shift has relocated the bottleneck to the human dimension: time-consuming mechanical processes, such as input preparation and data analysis, now dominate the research lifecycle. We introduce Paimon, a Platform for Agentic Integration in Materials Optimization and Nanoscale-simulations. Through hundreds of trials on an expert-level liquid electrolyte simulation, we show that Paimon substantially improves the reliability of agentic workflows by suppressing silent errors: plausible yet physically incorrect results. Paimon accommodates a new capability without modifying the agents already present, which we demonstrate by integrating an externally developed scientific agent. As an agent harness for atomistic simulations, Paimon affords researchers a continuous, science-centric workflow throughout the entire simulation lifecycle.

papers.title: BSTabDiff: Block-Subunit Diffusion Priors for High-Dimensional Tabular Data Generation
papers.abstract: High-Dimensional Low-Sample Size (HDLSS) tabular domains (e.g., omics) are characterized by $n \ll m$, where $n$ = number of samples, and $m$ = number of features. Such domains often exhibit strong local correlation groups, sparse cross-group dependencies, heavy-tailed non-Gaussian marginals, heteroscedastic noise, and structured missingness, making direct density learning in $\mathbb{R}^m$ ill-conditioned since $n \ll m$. We propose BSTabDiff, a block-subunit generative framework that partitions the $m$ observed features into $M$ latent blocks ($M \ll m$) and generates each block via a shared low-dimensional subunit variable, concentrating global dependence learning in the compact block-latent space $\mathbb{R}^M$ while decoding to the full feature space with copula-driven dependence, flexible per-feature marginals, and explicit missingness mechanisms. BSTabDiff can induce a data-driven feature ordering and block construction before latent partitioning, allowing the model to better align with local dependency structure when such organization is beneficial. BSTabDiff supports modern deep priors on block latents, including diffusion and normalizing flows, enabling stable synthesis and controllable benchmark generation in the HDLSS regime. Empirically, BSTabDiff produces more realistic and more stable high-dimensional synthetic data when compared with unstructured tabular generators on HDLSS data.

papers.title: A criterion for weighted uniform distribution along functions from a Hardy field
How Similar Can Fractional Chern Insulators Be to Fractional Quantum Hall States? Moiré-Enhanced Gaps and Excitation-Spectrum Correspondence
papers.abstract: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) realize fractional quantum Hall topology in lattice bands, but their excitation spectra remain far less understood than their ground states. Here we establish a theoretical principle relating the periodic electron-density modulations of flat Chern bands to the many-body gap and excitation spectrum of FCIs. Contrary to the conventional view that such density modulations are detrimental to fractional topology, we show that different reciprocal-lattice Fourier components play sharply distinct roles: components at smaller reciprocal lattice vectors suppress the FCI gap, whereas components at larger reciprocal lattice vectors enhance it. By suppressing the harmful small-wave-vector components and amplifying the beneficial large-wave-vector components, the gap enhancement can, in principle, be made arbitrarily large within the projected flat-band theory. Moreover, the same enhancement factor rescales the full low-energy spectrum, making the FCI excitation spectrum predictable from the corresponding Landau-level problem. We further generalize this correspondence to non-Abelian states. Applying this principle to moiré Chern bands, we identify these reciprocal-lattice density components as practical diagnostics for robust FCIs.

papers.title: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars at Finite Temperature
papers.abstract: We study the radial oscillation spectrum of relativistic stars within Israel-Stewart and Navier-Stokes theories, extending previous analyses to include heat diffusion and a thermodynamically consistent finite-temperature equation of state. The inclusion of heat flux gives rise to a distinct thermal sector in the mode spectrum, whose structure closely mirrors the dispersion relations of an infinite dissipative fluid. Within Israel-Stewart theory, the thermal modes transition from purely damped to propagating behavior above a critical overtone number, providing a finite-size realization of relativistic second sound in compact stars. Remarkably, the finite stellar geometry can push even the fundamental thermal mode into the propagating regime -- a feature with no continuum analogue. For the class of equations of state considered here, where finite-temperature corrections enter as controlled, Sommerfeld-type perturbations of a cold polytrope, the thermal sector couples only weakly to the ordinary fluid oscillation spectrum, with the coupling being of second order in a suitable temperature parameter. We further show that the discrete stellar spectrum is well captured by an analytic ansatz constructed from the flat-spacetime dispersion relations, with the star's finite radius discretizing the continuous mode structure. Our results complete the analysis of radial oscillations of viscous stars by incorporating the last remaining dissipative degree of freedom within the Israel-Stewart framework.

papers.title: Superconductivity beyond band geometry: emergence of pair quantum geometry
papers.abstract: The quantum geometry of Bloch states is known to shape the effective mass of single particles in multiband systems. We show that this connection extends to paired states. For a multiband Hubbard model with on-site attraction, we derive an exact effective-mass theorem for two-body bound states in vacuum and its counterpart for Cooper pairs near the critical temperature within Gaussian fluctuation theory. In both cases, the inverse mass contains, besides a ``conventional'' term from band dispersion and band geometry, a distinct term governed by a quantum metric on the manifold of paired states. This pair-geometric term requires a sublattice pairing texture that varies with the pair momentum and, like the band quantum metric, depends on the orbital embedding, whereas the total mass does not. The one-body, two-body, and Cooper-pair theorems follow from a single construction, with the band mass recovered as a special case. When a collective mode lies inside the two-particle continuum, its continuation to the second Riemann sheet renders the fluctuation kernel non-Hermitian, leading to a biorthogonal quantum geometry and a complex Cooper-pair mass whose real and imaginary parts describe propagation and damping. Exact calculations for the sawtooth, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger, Hofstadter, and fluorite-like lattices show that pair geometry contributes significantly to the mass of bound pairs, and the fluorite-like lattice exhibits both an undamped Cooper pair with a real mass and a damped one with a complex mass. Pair quantum geometry thus emerges as an essential ingredient of multiband superconductivity beyond band geometry.

papers.title: VASTO: Simultaneous reconstruction of vascular geometry and blood flow from tomographic projections via differentiable topology optimization
papers.abstract: Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) is widely used to reconstruct vascular geometry from projection measurements, with conventional approaches such as Filtered Back-Projection (FBP) and Iterative Reconstruction (IR) forming the clinical standard. Despite recent advances, these methods remain susceptible to sparse and noisy measurement, making accurate recovery of critical anatomical features challenging. This consequently leads to poor estimation of blood flow. In this work, we present a fluid-physics-constrained reconstruction framework that leverages topology optimization (TO) to jointly recover vascular geometry and blood flow directly from time-resolved CTA sinograms. The formulation couples a steady incompressible flow model with a transient advection-diffusion contrast transport model, mapped to sinogram space through a differentiable projection operator. The velocity field is recovered as part of the reconstruction, and thus hemodynamic information can be obtained without requiring a separate computational fluid dynamics pipeline. The proposed method is demonstrated on synthetic phantoms under varying sparsity and noise levels, and on representative projection data.

papers.title: Fast Organic Crystal Structure Prediction with Unit Cell Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Organic crystal structure prediction (CSP) is a requirement for computational modelling of organic solids, but traditionally costs several CPU-years per molecule. Generative models such as OXtal dramatically reduce this cost by sampling stable organic crystal structures directly. However, OXtal forgoes explicit lattice parametrization in favour of modelling large crops of the bulk material with expensive triangle layers, which can incur a computational cost of minutes per molecule. In this paper, we reduce this to seconds with Clari, a large-scale flow matching model that generates redundancy-free unit cells and replaces triangle layers with pair-bias attention. Clari requires only atom types and bonds as input and does not need an RDKit-sanitizable input molecule, which expands its applicability to challenging chemistries such as fullerenes, metal complexes, and atom clusters. We further ablate key design choices such as auxiliary losses, timestep distributions, noise priors, and self-conditioning. On OXtal's test sets, we surpass OXtal's solve rate while obtaining a speedup of 15-30$\times$. Because Clari also models explicit hydrogens, it supports inference-time scaling via direct energy ranking, without any decoration or relaxation step. When generating 150 crystals and selecting the top-30 by energy, we further improve solve rate while maintaining a speedup of 5-8$\times$. We also introduce the CSD Teaching Subset as a new test split of diverse and complex molecules for future benchmarking. Our contributions enable CSP within seconds, making large-scale virtual screening of organic solids practical. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Hidden Commitment Power Is Powerless
papers.abstract: A principal who offers a contract may renege when her default option is sufficiently attractive. The size of this temptation, which inversely measures her commitment power, is often the principal's private information. This paper asks how contracting outcomes change under this information asymmetry. Disciplining off-path beliefs with the Intuitive Criterion, I find that every type of principal behaves and earns payoffs as if she were commonly known to have the least commitment power. Hidden commitment power is therefore powerless, although commitment power can be valuable under symmetric information. The result delivers an unambiguous policy lesson on how to mitigate this information asymmetry prior to contracting: only measures that improve the worst case have value. In an application to credit rating, when the cost of a rating system grows with its number of grades, a rating system that sorts issuers into ordered bands is optimal, and each issuer contracts on the terms warranted by the floor of her band.

papers.title: Anharmonic lattice dynamics and superconductivity in strained bulk and surface niobium
papers.abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we investigate how homogeneous strain and crystallographic surface orientation modify the vibrational and superconducting properties of niobium. For bulk Nb, tensile strain strongly softens the phonon spectrum and enhances the electron--phonon coupling, increasing the superconducting transition temperature from 9.5 K at equilibrium to 14.5 K at $\sim\!6\%$ lattice expansion. For the low-index Nb(001), Nb(110), and Nb(111) surfaces, harmonic phonon calculations exhibit imaginary modes, showing that anharmonic lattice effects are essential. To treat these effects efficiently, we train Nb-specific machine-learning interatomic potentials on bulk and slab first-principles configurations and use them to accelerate stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation calculations, thereby obtaining anharmonically renormalized phonon modes that are combined with density-functional perturbation theory electron--phonon matrix elements to construct the Eliashberg spectral function. Among the clean free-standing slabs considered here, Nb(001) exhibits the strongest electron--phonon coupling and the highest calculated transition temperature of 10.0 K, while Nb(110) and Nb(111) show progressively reduced pairing strength. Finally, by analyzing the Eliashberg spectral function and the functional derivative $\delta T_\text{c}/\delta\alpha^2F(\omega)$, we identify the phonon energy ranges most effective for superconducting pairing. Our results show that strain, surface termination, and anharmonic phonon renormalization provide complementary and interrelated microscopic routes for tuning superconductivity in Nb.

papers.title: Spectrum Anomaly Detection in OFDMA Systems: Simulation Framework and Benchmark Dataset
papers.abstract: Wireless connectivity underpins modern society and industry, enabling critical applications such as 5G ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) for industrial automation. However, the openness of the wireless medium exposes it to spectrum anomalies, including unintentional interference and malicious jamming, which threaten communication and sensing functionalities in 5G and emerging 6G networks. Despite its importance, spectrum anomaly detection research is hindered by a lack of publicly available datasets reflecting real-world scenarios. To address this, we present a benchmark dataset for spectrum anomaly detection in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing access (OFDMA) systems, a core technology for 5G and beyond. The dataset includes spectrograms generated across a distributed network of sensing units, covering five distinct jammer types, from simple noise to advanced pilot-aware attacks. These anomalies are simulated in an industrial factory environment using a versatile open-source framework developed and published as part of this work, enabling extensibility to new scenarios and interference types. We provide baseline evaluations for supervised and unsupervised learning methods, demonstrating the challenges posed by different jammers and highlighting areas for further research. The dataset and framework support reproducible studies and serve as a foundation for advancing spectrum anomaly detection, with applications extending to network digital twins. By bridging the gap in open dataset availability, this work empowers the research community to validate and compare advanced detection methods for resilient next-generation wireless systems.

papers.title: A Formally Verified Library of Mathematical Finance in Lean 4
papers.abstract: We describe a library of mathematical finance in the Lean 4 proof assistant, built on Mathlib and the BrownianMotion package. Its benchmark records 804 results from the literature, each with a Lean statement, a status, and a published account of what the formalization leaves out: 766 are proved in full, 18 restate an upstream theorem, and 20 are reduced cores that prove less than the result they are named after. The library is about 158,000 lines of Lean, contains no sorry, and a build-time audit pins every library constant that a benchmark proof cites to Lean's three standard axioms. The Itô integral is constructed rather than assumed. On it the library proves Itô's formula for C2 functions of Itô processes as an identity of processes, Lévy's characterisation, martingale representation, Girsanov's theorem for bounded predictable drifts, which yields a Brownian motion for the filtration when the driver's paths are almost surely continuous, and unique L2 solutions of Lipschitz stochastic differential equations on every horizon. These results reach the contracts a user prices. In a contract language that separates payoffs from models, the Black-Scholes call is replicated by its delta hedge up to every date before maturity, and every fixed-dated contract on the physical Black-Scholes asset has, under the Girsanov measure of a horizon containing its dates, its risk-neutral value. An audit of faithfulness makes the logical status of every claim checkable, and its review has caught what mechanical gates cannot see, including a convergence theorem whose hypothesis could never be satisfied. Nearly all of the mathematics is classical, and what a formal base over it produces is certified unification of known results; two contributed developments, by Robert Martin, address problems the library's own survey had listed as open. The contribution is methodological and infrastructural.

papers.title: Multipoint Characterization of Higher-Order Sobolev Spaces
Lipschitz-Guided Machine Learning Framework for Accelerating Transient Stability Analysis of Flexible Traction Power Supply Systems
papers.abstract: The rapidly varying and moving train loads in electrified railways impose stringent requirements on the transient stability of flexible traction power supply systems (FTPSSs). However, the complex dynamic interactions among numerous traction substations (TSs) make it challenging for existing transient stability analysis (TSA) methods to achieve both high accuracy and computational efficiency. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a Lipschitz-guided machine learning framework that leverages Lipschitz continuity to restructure the transient stability verification of FTPSSs. By replacing computationally intensive satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solvers with a deterministic algebraic check on a finite mesh, the proposed method ensures the Lyapunov conditions between mesh points without simplifications of the FTPSS dynamics. Validated on FTPSSs with three to five TSs through extensive case studies, the proposed framework accelerates training by up to 12 times compared with SMT-based neural Lyapunov methods and certifies the five-TS system. Furthermore, the proposed framework achieves up to a 33.5-fold increase in the estimated region of attraction (ROA) compared with linear matrix this http URL advancement provides an efficient TSA solution for droop-controlled FTPSSs.

papers.title: Weighted Conformal Clustering
Advances in electrical contacts to single crystals of emerging materials for transport measurements
papers.abstract: Transport measurements that probe electrical resistivity of a material under varying external stimuli, such as temperature, magnetic field, optical illumination, and gate voltage, are among the most important experimental techniques in condensed matter physics. These measurements provide critical insights into the fundamental electronic properties of materials. In recent years, they have facilitated the discovery and exploration of intriguing physical phenomena (e.g., superconductivity and quantum oscillations) and unique device functionalities (e.g., photoresponse and electrostatic gating effects) in various emerging materials, particularly in the form of single crystals. However, unlike large-scale wafers or thin films, newly synthesized single crystals often pose substantial challenges in establishing reliable electrical contacts due to their irregular geometries, limited dimensions, inherent structural characteristics, and potential susceptibility to degradation. In this review, we highlight recent technological advancements in the fabrication of high-quality, lithographically defined multi-terminal electrodes on both exfoliable and non-exfoliable single crystals for transport measurements. Our work provides a practical guide for researchers seeking to select appropriate contact-fabrication strategies tailored to unique characteristics of emerging crystals.

papers.title: Orbital Networks in the Three-Body Problem
papers.abstract: Orbital transfers in multi-body systems are often studied as isolated trajectory design problems, making it difficult to identify the larger transport structure connecting families of periodic orbits, including which families act as hubs, gateways, relays, or persistently difficult-to-access regions. This work introduces a reachable-set-based framework for constructing orbital networks in the circular restricted three-body problem. Finite-$\Delta V$ and finite-time-of-flight reachable-set overlaps are used to infer accessibility relationships between representative periodic orbit families on a common Jacobi energy manifold and to assemble these relationships into a weighted orbital network. Applied to the Earth-Moon system, the resulting network reveals distinct accessibility regimes in which direct reachability, graph connectedness, and feasible multileg closure emerge separately. The analysis identifies multi-orbiter cycler orbits as the dominant hub, gateway, and relay families, with the (3,2)-cycler dominating across much of the sampled budget plane and the short-period (1,1)-cycler dominating in the low-time-of-flight regime, while the stable 2:1 resonant orbit remains persistently difficult to access. Although the maximum-budget network is nearly complete in a binary sense, its weighted accessibility remains strongly non-uniform. Selected proxy-supported connections are refined into concrete trajectories through differential correction, with corrected transfer costs remaining below the proxy estimates in all tested cases. Together, the results demonstrate how reachable-set overlap geometry can expose large-scale transport structure in nonlinear gravitational systems without requiring exhaustive pairwise trajectory optimization.

papers.title: Nonperturbative renormalization of Haldane pseudopotentials from the exact two-electron spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate how exact two-electron energies and radial wavefunctions can improve many-electron descriptions of Landau-level (LL) mixing. Renormalized pseudopotentials are defined from the lowest interacting relative-motion branch in each lowest-LL angular-momentum channel. They include changes in Coulomb and magnetic kinetic expectation values nonperturbatively and recover the leading two-body perturbative correction. Matched three- and four-electron benchmarks show that the scalar renormalized model improves lowest fixed-sector energies and first fixed-sector spacings over conventional lowest-LL projection, although the tested perturbative models give more accurate lowest energies. Retaining the same second-order induced three-body term while replacing the perturbative two-body input by the renormalized pseudopotentials yields a hybrid with smaller absolute lowest-energy errors throughout the sampled coupling range. At the Coulomb-to-cyclotron energy ratio $\gamma_B=3.5$, the errors decrease by approximately $58\%$ and $57\%$ for three and four electrons, respectively, relative to the tail-completed two-plus-three-body perturbative comparator. At the same coupling, complementary antisymmetric multi-LL variational states built from the pair radial amplitudes recover $99.41\%$ and $99.11\%$ of the matched finite-cutoff LL-mixing energy lowering for five and six electrons, outperforming equal-rank first-order-pair controls. These results establish pair energies and radial structure as complementary, quantitatively useful inputs for many-electron treatments of LL mixing.

papers.title: Chem-PerturBridge: a harmonized compendium of small molecule perturbation transcriptomic effects
papers.abstract: Large perturbation models require training data encompassing chemical, cellular, and assay diversity. Current transcriptomic resources for small-molecule modeling, however, are fragmented across technologies, metadata conventions, controls, doses, and preprocessing pipelines. We introduce Chem-PerturBridge, a harmonized multi-dataset resource comprising over 37k compounds, 136 cellular contexts, and 1.25M transcriptomic samples across eight assay types, with standardized identifiers, metadata, and replicate-aware condition-level effects. We use the resource to evaluate matched-condition agreement across datasets and replicate agreement within datasets. Matched same-compound conditions show weak absolute agreement in fine-grained $\mathrm{logFC}$ rankings and magnitudes across most dataset pairs. However, they generally exceed individual same-context different-compound signatures, while often falling below the smoothed centroid of such signatures. Same-compound retrieval is above chance in all pairs. $\mathrm{LogFC}$ direction agreement is high in absolute terms, and exceeds both baselines in most cases. We further evaluate Chem-PerturBridge as a pretraining resource for compound representation learning. Under a compound-held-out OP3 evaluation split, embeddings pretrained on Chem-PerturBridge improve over L1000-only embeddings, Morgan fingerprints, chemical language model embeddings, and the descriptor-free OP3 baseline across metrics. An extensive molecule-holdout evaluation across 11 datasets further shows that models trained on Chem-PerturBridge outperform or match those that are not. Chem-PerturBridge therefore supports both diagnostic evaluation of cross-dataset signature agreement and model-oriented reuse of heterogeneous perturbation transcriptomic data.

papers.title: When Are Multimodal Predictions Biologically Supported? A Diagnostic Evaluation Framework
papers.abstract: Multimodal models in oncology can produce accurate predictions, but accurate prediction does not reveal whether the model has learned biology that is shared across modalities, biology confined to one modality, or spurious correlations that reflect confounders rather than genuine biology. We introduce DECAT, a model-agnostic post-hoc evaluation framework that classifies multimodal representations into four diagnostic scenarios (shared, spurious, modality-specific, or no signal) for a given task and modality, using five null-referenced metrics and a rule-based decision procedure. The framework operates on learned representations, requires no knowledge of which specific confounder is present, and returns indeterminate when the evidence is insufficient. We evaluate multimodal architecture properties using DECAT on synthetic data across four multimodal model classes spanning over 2,500 trained representations, and demonstrate its operational use on 8,979 TCGA patients with both multimodal model embeddings and five pretrained pathology foundation models. Entangled models (e.g., CLIP) detect shared signal near-perfectly on synthetic data but also falsely claim it when it is absent, doing so in the majority of such cases on real foundation model embeddings. This false claim rate increases with signal strength and sample size, so that larger cohorts and stronger representations produce more confident but still incorrect diagnoses. Applied to both multimodal TCGA embeddings and five pathology foundation models without paired RNA, DECAT detects confounding invisible to AUROC without requiring the confounder labels, as confirmed by post-hoc stratification.

papers.title: OmniMem: Scalable and Adaptive Memory Retrieval for Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video generation extends videos by producing latent chunks sequentially, but scaling to long videos requires repeated access to a growing historical KV cache. Existing methods reduce this cost by truncating the KV cache or compressing it into implicit memory, but both lose explicit access to query-relevant historical details. We propose OmniMem, an explicit full-range memory retrieval framework that performs sparse KV retrieval over the historical cache. To make this practical for chunk-based AR video generation, OmniMem addresses two issues: (i) local bias in sparse KV selection and (ii) Union Explosion in memory access. Adaptive Window Exclusion removes local-window blocks from the selection candidates when sufficient long-range history is available, preserving the sparse budget for informative long-range retrieval. Query-Shared KV Selection reduces cross-query diversity, while Per-Head Scattered KV Access avoids expanding head-specific selections into a large selected KV buffer. This allows each attention head to retrieve non-contiguous KV blocks according to its own selection pattern. Experiments on long-video generation show that OmniMem improves Dynamic Degree by 52.3% and preserves strong consistency over strong baselines, while maintaining comparable memory usage.

papers.title: GRUFF: LLM Pronoun Fidelity, Reasoning, and Biases in German
papers.abstract: Third-person singular pronouns have long been used to study stereotypical biases in language models and to test their abilities to reason about reference. More recently, the interplay between reasoning and bias has been investigated with the task of pronoun fidelity, which assesses models' abilities to correctly reuse a previously-specified pronoun for a discourse entity, independent of other potentially distracting discourse entities mentioned in between. However, such research focuses on English, a language with limited grammatical gender and almost no gender agreement. In this paper we contribute a novel, large-scale dataset, GRUFF, to measure pronoun fidelity in German, covering four different gender agreement systems in nouns, and four sets of pronouns. With this dataset, we show that LLMs display strong grammatical agreement for masculine and feminine entities in the absence of explicit context, but not for neopronouns xier and en. In the presence of distractors, however, models degrade on all pronoun sets. Finally, we show that occupational stereotypes in this context are poorly correlated across grammatical cases and most models, except ones with closely related architectures.

papers.title: List Recovery for Random Low-Rate Linear Codes
Work that Counts, and Work that Doesn't: Reconciling Experimental and Observational Labor Supply Elasticities
papers.abstract: Do workers behave the same in experiments as they do in real life? Combining a real-effort emoji-counting experiment with platform records, self-reported expectations and recalls, and smartphone screen-time logs, we compare how the same workers on Prolific respond to wage changes in the experiment and in their actual work. Our results reveal that workers' behavior in experiments is remarkably different from their behavior in real life.
